She draws a fish and writes "I love you".
She puts the note under Fluffy's bed.
She hopes Fluffy will see it and like it.
But Fluffy does not see the note.
He is too busy playing with his toys.
He runs and jumps and chases a ball.
He does not go to his bed.
Anna is curious.
She wonders if Fluffy saw her note.
She goes to his bed and looks under it.
She sees the note.
It is still there.
It remains under the bed.
Anna is sad.
She thinks Fluffy does not love her.
She picks up the note and hugs it.
She cries.
Fluffy hears Anna cry.
He stops playing.
He runs to her and rubs his head on her leg.
He purrs and licks her hand.
He loves her.
Anna smiles.
She sees Fluffy loves her.
She gives him the note and a hug.
She says "I love you too".
Fluffy takes the note and puts it in his bed.
He keeps it.
He remains happy.
Once upon a time there was a boy named Joe.
He was three years old and wanted to explore the world.
He was very brave and didn't let things scare him.
Joe had some equipment that he liked to use to explore.
He had a cape, a helmet and a backpack.
He thought these things made him look like a superhero.
One day Joe went exploring and found a big, ugly bug.
It had a lot of legs and he was scared.
But Joe was brave, so he decided to look at it and think.
He thought that the bug was trying to tell him something.
Joe kept exploring and found some much bigger and uglier creatures.
He was a little scared, but kept thinking.
He thought to himself that maybe the creatures weren't that bad and that he should try to understand them.
So he did!
And Joe learned a lot that day.
"Come on, mama!" said Lily as she watched the little bird try to fly away.
The little bird had a broken wing and could not fly.
Mama put her hands on her hips.
"We have to help him, Lily," she said.
Lily and Mama grabbed a large blanket and carefully covered the bird.
"We have to take him to the vet," said Mama.
Mama drove quickly to the vet's office and the vet gently took the bird from them.
After examining the bird, the vet said the wing would need to be rescued.
The vet put a cast on the bird's wing and soon the bird was able to fly again with a clean wing.
"We did it, Mama!" said Lily with a smile as the little bird flew into the sky.
"We rescued the bird!"
Once upon a time there was a furry creature named Larry.
He was a very curious creature who loved exploring and learning new things.
One day Larry was walking around, when he stumbled upon a peculiar object.
It was an oyster.
Larry was confused and didn't understand what it was.
A friendly raccoon appeared out of nowhere and said to Larry, "That's an oyster, Larry.
It holds a special surprise inside it."  "What surprise?" Larry wondered, his eyes wide with curiosity.
The raccoon smiled and explained, "Inside the oyster is a pearl.
It's smooth and shiny.
And very special."  Larry nodded and said, "I understand now.
Thank you for teaching me about oysters".
The raccoon smiled and said, "My pleasure, Larry.
Now let's see what kind of surprise the oyster might have!"  They both smiled excitedly and together they opened the oyster.
Inside was a beautiful shiny pearl!
Larry was so happy and couldn't believe his eyes.
He had learned something new and found a wonderful surprise.

Once upon a time, there was a bear.
He was always very hungry and wanted something sweet to eat.
He decided to search all around the forest to find something yummy.
He looked high and low but he just couldn't find what he was looking for.
Suddenly, he saw a dark tree and had an idea.
He climbed up the tree and saw a beehive.
He knew that this was the solution to his problem.
He carefully opened up the hive and started to search inside.
He was so happy when he found some honey!
He ate all the honey he could find and was very full.
He also decided to take some of the honey with him, so he could eat more later.
He put the honey in his pocket and headed home.
From that day on, the bear always searched for honey in the dark tree.
Whenever he was hungry, he remembered the delicious honey he had found in the tree and went back for more.
Anna loved rice.
She ate it every day with her mom and dad.
Sometimes she had rice with chicken, sometimes with fish, sometimes with soup.
She liked all kinds of rice.
One day, Anna went to the park with her mom.
She saw some ducks in the pond.
She wanted to feed them.
She asked her mom if she could give them some rice.
Her mom said no.
She said rice was not good for ducks.
She said ducks could get sick from rice.
She said Anna should only feed them bread or seeds.
But Anna did not listen.
She was curious.
She wanted to see what the ducks would do with rice.
She took some rice from her lunch box and threw it in the pond.
The ducks came to eat it.
They made loud noises.
They looked happy.
Anna felt happy too.
She threw more rice in the pond.
She laughed and clapped.
She did not see her mom's angry face.
She did not hear her mom's warning voice.
Then something bad happened.
One of the ducks started to choke.
It made a strange sound.
It flapped its wings.
It splashed in the water.
It looked scared.
Anna felt scared too.
She stopped throwing rice.
She ran to her mom.
She cried and said sorry.
Her mom hugged her and said it was okay.
She said Anna did not know.
She said Anna should not do it again.
She said Anna should learn from her mistake.
She said Anna should be kind to animals.
Anna nodded and said yes.
She looked at the duck.
It was still choking.
It looked sad.
Anna felt sad too.
She wished she had not thrown rice.
She wished she had listened to her mom.
She regretted what she had done.
She hoped the duck would be okay.
She learned a lesson.
She never fed rice to ducks again.
Once upon a time, there was a kind boy named Timmy.
He loved to draw on paper with his crayons.
One day, Timmy met a kind girl named Sarah.
They played together and had lots of fun.
As they grew up, Timmy realized he wanted to marry Sarah.
So, he drew a picture of a ring on a piece of paper and asked her to marry him.
Sarah said yes and they had a big party with lots of cake and balloons.
From that day on, Timmy and Sarah were married and they drew lots of pictures together on paper.
They lived happily ever after.
The end.
One day, Mommy and Jimmy went to the store.
Mommy was looking for a new model for the house.
Jimmy was looking for something colorful.
Everywhere Jimmy looked, he saw something different.
He started to get frustrated that he couldn't find anything.
Then, he saw a colorful model sitting on a shelf.
It was perfect!
Mommy said, "Excellent choice Jimmy!" Jimmy was so excited that they took the model home with them.
But when they got home, Mommy started ignoring Jimmy and the model.
Jimmy was very sad, but he was determined to make Mommy see what a great model he chose.
Jimmy set up the model and waited.
Finally, Mommy saw it.
She couldn't ignore it any longer!
Mommy said, "Jimmy, this model is so colorful and beautiful!" Jimmy smiled, proud that his choice had been recognized.
He knew if he looked hard enough he would find something special!
Once upon a time, there was a funny owl named Hoot.
Hoot loved to make his friends laugh by telling silly jokes.
One day, Hoot's friends had an argument and they were not talking to each other anymore.
Hoot felt sad and wanted to help his friends unite again.
He flew to each of his friends and said, "Let's be friends again.
It's not fun when we're not together." His friends listened to Hoot and realized that their argument was not important.
They hugged each other and said sorry.
Hoot felt happy that he could help his friends unite again.
He learned that it's important to be a good friend and to help others.
The moral of the story is that friendship is important and we should always try to make things right when we have an argument with our friends.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
Timmy loved to explore and learn new things.
One day, he found a tiny microscope in his backyard.
He picked it up and looked through it.
He saw tiny bugs and plants up close.
It was so cool!
Timmy's mom came outside and asked him what he was doing.
Timmy showed her the microscope and said, "Look, Mommy!
Tiny bugs!" His mom smiled and said, "That looks like fun, Timmy.
Would you like some lemonade to drink while you explore?" Timmy nodded his head and said, "Yes, please!" His mom went inside to get the lemonade.
When she came back, Timmy was sitting on a comfortable chair, looking through the microscope.
His mom handed him the lemonade and said, "Enjoy your drink, Timmy." Timmy smiled and took a sip of the sweet lemonade.
He was having so much fun exploring and learning new things.
Once upon a time, there was a boy named Max.
Max had a razor that he used to shave his dad's beard.
One day, Max's dad asked him to go to the store to buy milk.
Max was tired, but he wanted to help his dad, so he said, "Okay, I will go." Max put on his shoes and started to jog to the store.
When Max got to the store, he saw his friend Lily.
"Hi, Max!" Lily said.
"What are you doing here?" Max replied, "I came to buy milk for my dad." Lily said, "That's nice of you.
Do you want to play?" Max said, "I'm too tired to play.
Maybe later."  Max bought the milk and jogged back home.
When he got home, his dad was happy to see him.
"Thank you for getting the milk, Max," his dad said.
Max replied, "No problem, dad.
I'm happy to help."
Anna and Ben were playing hide and seek in the big house.
Anna was the seeker and Ben was the hider.
Ben ran to the living room and saw a long curtain that touched the floor.
He thought it was a good place to hide behind.
He moved the curtain a little and went inside.
Anna counted to ten and then opened her eyes.
She looked around and tried to find Ben.
She saw the toys, the sofa, the table, and the window.
She did not see Ben.
She wondered where he was.
She walked to the living room and saw the curtain.
She thought maybe Ben was behind it.
She walked to the curtain and pulled it back.
She saw Ben, but she also saw something else.
It was a big, furry, unknown animal.
It had sharp teeth and claws and it growled at them.
Anna and Ben were very scared.
They did not know what to do.
They remembered what their mom had told them.
She had said, "If you ever see an unknown animal, do not touch it or run away.
Stay calm and trust me.
I will come and help you." Anna and Ben trusted their mom.
They held hands and said, "Mom, mom, help us!" Their mom heard them and came to the living room.
She saw the animal and recognized it.
It was a bear that had escaped from the zoo.
She grabbed a broom and chased it away.
She hugged Anna and Ben and said, "You are very brave and smart.
You did the right thing.
I am proud of you." Anna and Ben were happy and relieved.
They thanked their mom and said, "We love you, mom." They decided to play a different game.
Once upon a time, there was a wild cat.
The cat had big eyes and a long tail.
One day, the cat saw a bird with a pretty bow on its head.
The cat wanted to catch the bird, so it ran and ran.
The bird flew away, but the cat saw a zipper on a bag.
The cat played with the zipper and had fun.
The end.
One day, a little girl named Emma was walking down a post-lined street.
Everything seemed calm and peaceful.
Suddenly, Emma noticed something in the distance and she felt frightened.
She blinked and the darkness had come closer.
It was a big, dark cloud!
Emma had never seen anything so big before and it scared her.
She started to run, blinking away her tears.
As the dark cloud came closer, it began to rain.
Eventually, the storm cloud was over Emma.
Lightning lit up the sky and Emma was so frightened that she couldn't move.
Emma felt like she was in a dream.
Suddenly, she remembered something her mum had told her about thunder and lightning; it was a sign of danger.
Emma had been foolish enough to go outside in the storm and now she was in danger.
Emma blinked again and the thunder roared.
The storm cloud had caught up with Emma and it was too late.
She was gone, swallowed up by the darkness.
There was a dove.
It was very comfortable in the tree.
The dove liked to hang from the branch.
Every day it would hang upside down and close its eyes.
One day, a little girl walked by the tree.
She was 3 years old and she saw the dove hanging.
She was very excited.
She put her hand out and tried to touch it.
The dove didn't mind; it felt comfortable with the little girl.
The girl smiled.
She said hello to the dove and the dove tilted it's head.
She touched it very gently and then started to climb the tree.
Soon, the little girl and the dove were both hanging from the branch.
The dove was happy and the little girl was smiling.
They stayed there together until the sun went down.
Then they both flew away, up into the sky.
Once upon a time, a three year old child named Sarah was playing in the park.
She was having lots of fun running around and playing tag with her friends.
But then she noticed the park was too tidy!
Everywhere she looked the grass was cut short, the playground was all the same, and the flowers were in straight, neat rows.
Sarah was really disappointed.
Suddenly, the whole park started to get really cold and everything began to freeze.
Winter had come early to the park!
Sarah was so sad that she couldn't play in her favorite park any more.
But then her friends had an idea.
They got together and worked hard to make the park cozy and fun.
They cleared the ice, planted flowers of all different shapes and sizes, and laid down warm blankets and cushions for everyone to play on.
When Sarah saw the park again, it was more fun and colorful than ever!
Now the park was perfectly tidy, but in a much more cozy, fun way.
Plus, Sarah and her friends could play in it all year round!
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
One day, Lily's mommy asked her to help make pancakes for breakfast.
Lily was very excited to help.
Mommy said, "Can you hurry and get the butter from the fridge, please?"  Lily ran to the fridge and got the butter.
It was easy for her to hold because it was soft.
As they were making the pancakes, Lily's mommy said, "You're doing a great job, Lily!"  Lily smiled and replied, "Thank you, mommy!
Making pancakes is so much fun!"  After they finished making the pancakes, they sat down to eat.
Lily spread the butter on her pancake and took a big bite.
It was delicious!
One day, Arnold and his family were on their way to the park.
Arnold was so excited, he could barely wait to get there.
He knew it was going to be perfect.
As they drove along in their family vehicle, Arnold noticed an old tractor in the field next to them.
He asked his Mom if they could part and go see it.
But his Mom said no, they were running late, so they had to keep going.
Arnold was really disappointed.
He really wanted to see the old tractor and he knew it was perfect.
But they just couldn't part and go see it.
So, Arnold decided to do something.
He asked his Dad if they could at least drive by slowly and take a look at it.
His Dad smiled and agreed.
So, as they drove along, Arnold was so happy, as he was able to catch a glimpse of the tractor.
It was perfect!
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She wanted to prepare a special dinner for her family.
She went to the kitchen and saw that there was no food.
She was worried and fearful that she could not make dinner.
Lily asked her mom for help.
Her mom said they needed to go to the store to buy food.
They went to the store and bought everything they needed.
Lily was happy and started to prepare the dinner.
She set the table with plates and cups.
But then, Lily's little brother came and knocked over the table.
All the food fell on the floor.
Lily was sad and didn't know what to do.
Her mom came and helped her clean up the mess.
They made dinner again and this time, Lily's family loved it.
They all had a great time together.
John felt happy.
He had a new book that he found.
It was nice and blue and he wanted to keep it forever.
He wanted to show everyone.
So he ran to the living room and showed it to his mom.
Mommy said "Oh, John, this book belongs to you now!" John smiled.
He looked at the book and said, "This book is mine and I love it!" He would carry it around the house all day.
Every time he felt sad, he looked at the book and it made him feel happy.
Now he had something that belonged just to him, and that made him smile.
Sam and Mia are twins.
They like to play with their toys.
They have many toys, but they want more.
They see a big shop with many modern toys.
They see cars, dolls, robots, and games.
They pull their mom to the shop.
"Mom, mom, can we go in?" they ask.
Mom looks at the shop.
She sees the price tags.
They are very high.
She shakes her head.
"No, sweeties, we can't go in.
Those toys are too expensive.
We have enough toys at home.
Maybe for your birthday, we can get one treat each." Sam and Mia are sad.
They want the modern toys.
They pout and whine.
"Please, mom, please.
Just one toy.
We will share.
We will be good." Mom sighs.
She loves her twins, but she can't buy them everything they want.
She has an idea.
"Look, there is a park across the street.
Why don't we go there and have some fun?
They have swings, slides, and a sandbox.
Maybe we can find some friends to play with.
And if you are good, I will buy you an ice cream on the way home.
How does that sound?" Sam and Mia think about it.
They like the park.
They like ice cream.
They like friends.
They nod and smile.
"Okay, mom, let's go to the park.
That sounds like a good treat." Mom smiles and hugs them.
She takes their hands and crosses the street.
They go to the park and have a lot of fun.
They forget about the modern toys.
They are happy with their treat.
Once upon a time, a little bird named Tweety lived in a tree.
One day, Tweety met a friendly squirrel named Nutty.
Nutty said, "Hi Tweety, do you want to make a home together?" Tweety said, "Yes, let's make a gentle home in this tree." They worked hard and made a cozy home with soft leaves and twigs.
One day, a big storm came and destroyed their home.
Tweety and Nutty were sad and had to find a new home.
They learned that even when you work hard, bad things can happen sometimes.
The moral of the story is that we should be kind to others and help them when they need it, because we never know when we might need help ourselves.
Tom and Lily were playing in the park.
They liked to run and jump and slide.
They saw a big swamp with green water and mud.
They wanted to go near it and look for frogs and bugs.
"Let's go to the swamp!" Tom said.
"No, it is too far and dirty.
Mom said we should not go there." Lily said.
"Come on, it will be fun.
We can pass the bridge and see what is on the other side." Tom said.
He took Lily's hand and ran to the bridge.
The bridge was old and shaky.
It made loud noises when they stepped on it.
Lily was scared.
"Tom, I don't like this.
The swamp is smelly and the bridge is broken.
Let's go back." Lily said.
But Tom did not listen.
He wanted to see the distant trees and flowers.
He ran faster and faster.
Lily tried to keep up.
She did not see the hole in the bridge.
She stepped on it and fell.
She screamed.
"Help!
Help!
I'm in the swamp!" Lily cried.
Tom heard her and turned around.
He saw Lily in the water.
She was covered in mud and weeds.
She looked sad and scared.
Tom felt sorry.
He ran back to the bridge and tried to help her.
"Lily, I'm sorry.
I was wrong.
Hold on, I'll get you out." Tom said.
He reached for her hand and pulled.
Lily came out of the swamp.
She was wet and dirty.
She hugged Tom and cried.
"Thank you, Tom.
You are a good brother.
Let's go home and clean up." Lily said.
They walked back to the park.
They passed the swamp and the bridge.
They did not look at them.
They learned their lesson.
They decided to play in the sandbox instead.
They were happy.
Once upon a time there was a fat fairy.
She lived in a big forest and was very happy.
But one day, something bad happened.
Suddenly she heard a loud noise and started to panic.
She looked around, but she couldn't see what was causing the noise.
All she could see were big trees and bushes.
The noise got louder and she started to run.
She ran and ran until she came to a big river.
But when she looked down, she saw a big, fat monster in the water.
She panicked and tried to run away.
But the monster was too powerful.
He grabbed her and swallowed her whole.
The poor fat fairy was never seen again.
The monster burped and waddled off into the sunset.
And that was the end of the poor fat fairy.
Once upon a time, there was a busy faucet named Tess.
Tess lived by the river and everyday she listened to the sound of the flowing water.
Tess noticed a family living in the nearby village.
The family was very poor, they had no water and wanted to take some from Tess.
Tess thought it was important to help the family so every day she let them take some of her water.
As the seasons changed so did the water levels.
Sometimes there was a lot and sometimes there was very little.
One hot summer's day the family came to Tess, desperate for water.
But Tess didn't have much and had to tell the family to go find some better water.
The family went away and soon returned with good, clean water from a clean source.
Tess had listened carefully to what the family had said, and realized this was the better water she had been looking for.
From then on Tess asked the family to bring clean water from a clean source to everyone in the village, to make sure everyone had access to clean water.
The moral of the story is: Always listen carefully.
It may lead you to the solution that you need.
Once upon a time, there was a princess who had a special jewel.
It was very pretty and sparkly.
One day, the jewel fell off her crown and got lost.
The princess was very sad and didn't know what to do.
A kind man found the jewel and gifted it back to the princess.
She was very happy and thanked the man.
The princess wanted to restore the jewel to her crown, so she took it to the jeweler.
The jeweler was able to restore the jewel and put it back on the princess's crown.
Now, the princess was very happy and wore her crown with the beautiful jewel everywhere she went.
The end.
Once upon a time, there was a kind lady who had a bed.
She was an honest lady who always lent her bed to her friends.
One day, her best friend came to visit.
He was tired, so the kind lady lent him her bed so that he could rest.
He thanked her and slept in the bed all night.
In the morning, he thanked her again for lending him the bed, and she smiled.
The kind lady enjoyed lending her bed to her friends, because she was an honest lady and she wanted to help people in any way she could.
Her friends were always happy with the bed and thanked her for her kindness.
The kind lady learned that being honest and lending her bed to her friends was a great way to make them happy.
Once upon a time, on a Wednesday, there was a chubby cat.
The cat saw a flower that was about to bloom.
The cat was very happy because it liked to watch flowers bloom.
The cat said to the flower, "Hi flower, I can't wait for you to bloom!" The flower did not say anything because flowers cannot talk.
But the cat did not know that.
The cat waited and waited for the flower to bloom.
But then, a big wind came and blew the flower away.
The chubby cat was very sad.
It cried and cried because it could not see the flower bloom.
The end.
"Once upon a time there was a small, harmless mouse.
The mouse liked to chew and escape from danger.
One day, the mouse spotted a giant piece of cheese in the corner of the room.
Chewing as fast as possible, the mouse was determined to find a way to escape with her prize.
Suddenly, the mouse freezeed as it heard a gruff voice speaking.
It was an evil cat, who planned to catch the mouse in his claws and make it his next snack.
The mouse quickly devised a plan.
She started to chew her way through the floorboards, desperately seeking an escape.
Finally, the mouse had made a hole big enough to fit her body throught to freedom.
But it was too late!
The cat had spotted the mouse just as she was soaring through the hole, and lunged toward her with claws outstretched.
The mouse had no choice but to frantically run away and leave her cheese as the cat's reward.
She was lucky to escape, but the cheese was gone without a trace.
The End"
One day, Charlie and his family were at the beach.
It was hot and sunny, and Charlie wanted to cool off.
He looked around and saw a pond nearby.
Charlie said, "Mom, I want to soak in that pond!" His mom smiled and replied, "That sounds like fun, Charlie.
Be careful not to get wet too much though, okay?" Charlie ran over to the pond and started splashing in the cool water.
He noticed something small and white floating in the pond.
He picked it up and saw it was a tiny flea!
He said "Mom, look at this flea!" His mom said, "Oh, it's so kind of you to look after the flea.
Can you put it back in the pond?" Charlie smiled and put the flea gently back in the pond.
As it floated away, Charlie watched it with a happy smile.
Then he went running back to the pond and started to soak some more.
Sara and Ben are friends.
They like to play outside.
They plan to go to the park today.
They put on their coats and hats.
It is cold outside.
They walk to the park.
They see a big slide.
They want to go on the slide.
But there is a problem.
The slide is wet.
It rained last night.
Sara and Ben are sad.
They see a boy and a girl.
They have towels.
They are wiping the slide.
They are making it dry.
Sara and Ben go to them.
They say hello.
"Can we help you?" Sara asks.
"Sure, you can.
We are making the slide dry.
Then we can all play on it." The boy says.
"That is very nice of you.
Thank you for sharing." Ben says.
They all work together.
They use the towels.
They make the slide dry.
Then they take turns.
They go on the slide.
They have fun.
They laugh and smile.
The sun comes out.
It makes the park bright.
It makes them warm.
They are happy.
The moral of the story is: Sharing and helping others can make everyone happy.
One day, a boy named Tim and a girl named Sue went to a party.
They were very excited to enjoy the yummy cake.
The cake was big and original, with many colors and shapes.
Tim and Sue couldn't wait to eat it.
At the party, they met a new friend named Max.
Max said, "I like cake too!
Can I have some?" Tim and Sue said, "Yes, let's all share the cake!" They were happy to share the cake with their new friend.
But then, a big dog came into the party.
The dog saw the cake and wanted it too.
The dog jumped up and ate the whole cake!
Tim, Sue, and Max were sad.
They did not get to enjoy the original cake.
The party was not fun anymore.
Summer and her mom were walking around the park on a cold Sunday morning.
The leaves on the trees were starting to change color, and the air felt chilly.
Summer liked the park and skipped ahead with her mom close behind.
Suddenly, Summer saw a swing and ran toward it.
But when she got close, she stopped and let out a big sigh.
The swing was wet, cold, and too slippery to sit on.
Summer looked up at her mom sadly.
Her mom smiled and took Summer's hand.
She said, "Let's find something else to do.
I bet there are lots more fun things in the park!" Summer and her mom spent the morning playing on the slide and exploring the trails.
By the time they were ready to go home, the cold Sunday had turned into a sunny, fun-filled day.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy who liked to play outside.
He loved to run and jump and play with his friends.
One day, he noticed a youth sitting all alone on a bench.
The youth looked sad and lonely.
The little boy went over to talk to the youth.
He asked him why he was sad.
The youth said he had lost his way and didn't know how to get home.
The little boy wanted to help, so he offered to walk the youth home.
As they walked, the sun began to set and the light started to fade.
They were getting farther away from the little boy's house and he started to feel scared.
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise and a car came speeding towards them.
The little boy tried to push the youth out of the way, but it was too late.
The car hit them both and they were hurt very badly.
The little boy's family was very sad when they heard the news.
They knew he had been trying to help the youth and they were proud of him.
But they were also very sad that he had been hurt.
The little boy didn't make it, but his family knew he had died trying to do something good.
Once upon a time, there was a big, brown bear named Benny.
Benny had a big, bushy mustache that he loved to show off.
One day, Benny was walking in the forest when he saw a little bird with a broken wing.
The bird was helpless and couldn't fly.
Benny felt sad for the little bird and wanted to help.
"What can I do to help you?" asked Benny.
The little bird replied, "Can you please shut the door to my nest so no one can bother me while I heal?" Benny was happy to help and went to the little bird's nest.
He shut the door tight and made sure no one could get in.
The little bird felt safe and thanked Benny for his help.
From that day on, Benny and the little bird became good friends and Benny's big, bushy mustache would always make the little bird smile.
Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to skip.
Every day she would go outside and skip down the street.
She was always so happy.
One day she noticed something strange.
In the neighbor’s garden, there was a crop of corn growing.
The little girl was curious and wanted to try it.
So she went into the garden and tried the corn.
It was so sweet and delicious.
Suddenly, she felt guilty.
She hadn’t asked the neighbor if she could take the corn.
She knew it was wrong and she had to tell the neighbor.
So she quickly ran over to the neighbor’s house and told her what she had done.
The neighbor said it was alright but asked her to never do it again.
The little girl was relieved and promised that she wouldn't do it again.
After that, she kept skipping down the street, happier than ever.
One day, Tom and Sue found a big toy car in the park.
It was red and shiny and had four wheels.
They wanted to play with it, but they did not know how to make it move.
"Maybe it needs a wire," Tom said.
He looked around and saw a long wire hanging from a tree.
He pulled it and tied it to the car.
"Let's go!" Sue said.
She sat in the car and Tom pushed it.
The car rolled down the hill, faster and faster.
Sue laughed and waved to Tom.
But then, the car hit a rock and stopped.
Sue bumped her head and cried.
The wire snapped and fell to the ground.
Tom ran to help her.
"Are you okay?" he asked.
"That hurt!" Sue said.
"And the car is broken!" They looked at the car and saw that it had a dent and a scratch.
They felt sad and sorry.
"Maybe we should not have taken the car," Tom said.
"It was not ours." "You're right," Sue said.
"We should have asked first." They decided to take the car back to the park and look for the owner.
They hoped he would not be angry.
As they walked, they met a man who was looking for something.
He had a remote control in his hand.
"Hey, that's my car!" he said.
"Where did you find it?" "We're sorry, mister," Tom said.
"We thought it was a toy.
We did not know it had a remote control." The man looked at the car and saw the damage.
He frowned and shook his head.
"That's not a toy, kids," he said.
"That's a model car.
It's very impressive and expensive.
It can go forward and reverse and do tricks.
But you need the remote control and the wire to make it work.
Without them, it's just a piece of metal." He took the car and the wire from them.
He was not happy.
"Next time, don't touch things that don't belong to you," he said.
"You could get hurt or break something.
And always ask before you borrow something.
That's the polite thing to do." Tom and Sue nodded and said they were sorry.
They learned their lesson.
They walked away, feeling ashamed and sad.
They wished they had been more careful and respectful.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
He loved playing soccer with his friends.
One day, his team won a big trophy.
Timmy was very happy and thought it was the most beautiful trophy he had ever seen.
But then, Timmy accidentally broke the trophy while playing with it.
He felt very sad and told his friend, "I regret breaking the trophy.
It was so beautiful." His friend said, "Don't worry, Timmy.
It's just a trophy.
We can always get another one.
The important thing is that we had fun playing together." Timmy felt better and realized that his friend was right.
It wasn't about the trophy, but about the memories they made while playing soccer.
From that day on, Timmy learned to value experiences more than material things.
Once upon a time, there was a poor little cube.
One day, the lonely cube wanted to jump around so he decided to try it out.
He jumped up, up, and up!
Suddenly, the cube heard a voice.
He looked around and then saw a little girl.
She smiled and said "Hello cube!
My name is Susan.
Would you like to play?"  The cube was so excited and he nodded his little block head.
"Yes, I would love to play!" The cube and little Susan played all day.
They jumped and jumped and jumped.
But soon, the sun began to set and it was time for Susan to go home.
The cube waved goodbye to Susan and said "Come back soon!" And then the poor little cube jumped up in the air, feeling happy and content.
Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily.
She had a wallet that was very important to her.
One day, she went to the park to play with her friends.
She put her wallet on the bench and forgot about it.
When she came back, her wallet was gone.
She looked everywhere but couldn't find it.
Lily was sad because she had her favorite toy in the wallet.
Her mom told her not to worry and they went to the lost and found.
They found the wallet, but it was ugly because someone had scribbled on it.
Lily was happy to have her wallet back, but sad that it looked so bad.
Her mom told her not to worry and took out a sticker from her bag.
She said, "Let's cover the ugly scribbles with this pretty sticker." Lily was excited and helped her mom cover the scribbles.
Now her wallet looked beautiful again, and she was happy to have her favorite toy back.
Once upon a time, there was a kind lady who loved to cook.
Every day, she would provide delicious meals for her family and friends.
She always made sure her kitchen was clean before she started cooking.
One day, her friend came over to visit.
The lady was happy to see her friend and decided to provide her with a special meal.
She cooked some yummy spaghetti with meatballs and a clean salad.
Her friend loved the meal and thanked the lady for providing such a tasty and clean dinner.
They had a great time together and promised to do it again soon.
The lady was happy to have provided a good meal for her friend.
Jack and his Grandma were walking in the park.
Jack had a question.
"Grandma, why are those flowers so expensive?" Grandma answered, "That's a very good question, Jack!
They are expensive because they are very special flowers." Jack asked, "What do you mean?" Grandma smiled.
"Take a closer look, Jack.
See how each flower is different than the other?
They are all like little works of art.
That's why they are so expensive." Jack looked more closely at the flowers.
He could see that Grandma was right.
Each one had a unique image.
They were like little pieces of art.
He felt very lucky to be able to look at them.
Suddenly, a rude voice interrupted his thoughts.
"Why are you taking such a long time?
We don't have all day!" It was a lady that looked like she was in a hurry.
She was pointing at the flowers and scowling at Grandma.
Grandma smiled and said, "We were admiring the beauty of these special flowers.
We'll be on our way now." The woman huffed and walked away.
Grandma said, "Come on, Jack.
Let's go find something else to look at." Jack smiled and nodded.
He was glad to have such a special moment with his Grandma.
Mommy and Tommy were making cookies together in the kitchen.
Tommy was very excited to help.
"Let's bake some yummy cookies!" Mommy said.
They mixed the ingredients together and put them in the oven.
When the cookies were done, Tommy asked his mommy if they could take some to the library.
Still, Mommy answered, "Let's leave some for ourselves, it was so much fun to make them together." So they shared the cookies between them and went to the library.
When they arrived, they saw all the pretty books and there were lots of people reading them.
Tommy and Mommy left the cookies on the counter.
One librarian looked very surprised.
"What a nice thing to do!" she said.
Tommy was happy and he knew this was the right thing to do.
Mommy put her hand on Tommy's shoulder and said, "See, being kind and sharing pays off.
Now let's go check out some books." They both smiled and went off to explore the library.
The moral of this story is that it is important to be kind and to share.
Doing nice things for other people often has unexpected rewards.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane.
She loved to draw and write in her journal.
Every day, she would write about her day and draw pictures of her friends and family.
Jane's journal was very important to her, and she valued it a lot.
One day, Jane went to the park with her journal.
She found a big, disgusting bug.
The bug was green and slimy.
Jane thought it was icky, but she wanted to draw it in her journal.
So, she sat down and drew the bug with her crayons.
When Jane finished drawing, she showed her picture to her mom.
Her mom said, "Wow, that bug looks disgusting, but your drawing is very good!" Jane was happy that her mom liked her drawing.
She knew that her journal was special and she would keep drawing and writing in it every day.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to play outside in the park with her friends.
One day, they found a big green structure to climb on.
Lily's friend, Timmy, said "Be careful, the edges are sharp!"  Lily replied, "Don't worry, I'll be careful." She climbed up the structure and looked down at Timmy.
"I can see everything from up here!"  Timmy smiled and said, "Wow, you're so brave!"  Lily felt proud of herself and they continued to play on the green structure for the rest of the day.
There was an elephant who really wanted to succeed.
He tried hard every day.
He would try and lift heavy logs, do tricks and practice running.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
Timmy loved to play with his toys, but he didn't like to share them with his friends.
One day, Timmy's friend came over to play.
Timmy didn't want to share his toys, so his friend went home feeling sad.

He felt guilty for not sharing his toys.
The next day, Timmy went to his friend's house and said sorry.
His friend forgave him and they played together happily.
Timmy learned that not sharing his toys could result in losing his friends.
He promised to always share and never make his friends scream or feel sad again.

Sue liked to play with her toys and ask questions.

He tried his best to be kind but the next day, things started to go wrong.
John had an argument with his wife and things only got worse.

She packed her bags and left, taking all her things with her.

He was a big bear and he had a lot of friends.

He had to fold something very fast, so he used his big paws and worked hard.
The bear worked quick and neatly.
He folded and tucked the paper, hands sliding over it, folding it into smaller and smaller pieces.

When he was done, he held the paper up to show his friends.

His friends clapped with delight, praising him for his work.

He started to shout and stomp his feet.
But the kind people did not care.
They were happy that they had all worked together to make something special.

Everyone was happy and they all lived happily ever after.

One day, the pink bunny fell down while playing.

His friends came to help him.
They told him not to worry, and they will help him heal.

Soon, the pink bunny's leg healed, and he could play again.

Her mom told Kim to stay inside, but Kim was too naughty.

Her mom chased after her and finally held Kim tight.

She knew that she had been naughty and that she wasn't allowed to play outside without her coat.
Her mom held her and said, "No more being naughty, Kim.

She followed her mom back inside and put on her coat.
From then on, Kim was good and never forgot her coat when she wanted to play outside.

He and his baby deer lived together happily and the hunter was able to feed them both with his bows and arrows.

Bean was sad.
He missed all of his friends.

He set off with a brave heart.
He meandered through the forest, looking and listening for his friends.

He hugged Daisy and said he missed her.
Daisy said she missed him, too!
Then Bean asked if she knew where the rest of his friends were.
Daisy smiled and said they were all waiting for him at the lake.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.

Every day, the people of the nation would spend their time picking flowers and fruits from the ground.
They were always very careful not to pick anything that didn't look healthy and tasty.
One day, a 3 year old child ventured into the nation.
They saw a tree with a beautiful, pale blooming flower.
The child was excited and wanted to pick it.
But, their parents told them not to pick it.
Despite being warned, the child couldn't resist the temptation and picked the special flower.
As soon as the bloom was in their hands, the pale nation lit up with color!
All the trees, flowers, fruits, and plants suddenly became red, green, orange, and yellow!
The people of the nation were amazed.
They thanked the 3 year old child for bringing color to their nation.
From that day on, they remembered the child as the one who made their pale nation bright and colorful!
There was once a little boy named Tom.
Tom liked to read books at the library.
Every day he would go to the library after school and bring home a new book.

Today, Tracey had a special job.
She was collecting heavy lungs.
Her mom whispered, "Be careful, Tracey!" So Tracey was very careful when she picked up the heavy lungs and put them into her bucket.
The heavy lungs were so big that it was hard to carry them all.
But Tracey carefully found a way to hold them all and she started walking home.
On the way she saw some birds, who were singing in the trees.
Tracey started singing too.
But then she remembered she had to be careful with the heavy lungs.
So she kept singing to herself but quietly so she wouldn't drop them!
Finally, Tracey arrived home.
She opened the door and saw her mom, who was very happy to see all the heavy lungs Tracey had collected.
She said, "Well done, Tracey!
I am so proud of you!" and gave Tracey a big hug.
Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the park.
They had a red ball, a blue bike and a yellow bowl.
They shared their toys and had fun together.
One day, a big dog came to the park.
It was black and brown and had a loud bark.
Tom and Lily were scared of the dog.
They ran to their mom and hid behind her.
"Mom, mom, there is a big dog in the park!
It is scary and noisy!
Can we go home?" they cried.
Mom looked at the dog and smiled.
She knew the dog.
It was Rex, the dog of her friend Sara.
Rex was a friendly and harmless dog.
He just wanted to play.
"Tom and Lily, don't be afraid of Rex.
He is a good dog.
He won't hurt you.
He likes children and toys.
Why don't you say hello to him and give him your yellow bowl?
He loves to play fetch." Mom said.
Tom and Lily were not sure.
They liked their yellow bowl.
They did not want to lose it.
But they also wanted to be brave and kind.
They decided to try.
They walked slowly to Rex and said hello.
Rex wagged his tail and licked their faces.
He was happy to see them.
He saw the yellow bowl and barked.
He wanted to play fetch.
Tom and Lily threw the yellow bowl and Rex ran after it.
He brought it back and dropped it at their feet.
He wanted them to throw it again.
Tom and Lily laughed and played with Rex.
They had a lot of fun.
Mom and Sara watched them and smiled.
They were proud of Tom and Lily.
They learned to overcome their fear and make a new friend.
They learned that not all dogs are scary and that some are harmless and playful.
They learned to share their toys and be generous.

Lily was a big girl who liked to play with her dolls and her blocks.
She had a rare doll that was very pretty and had long hair.
She loved to brush her hair and dress her up.
One day, she was playing with her doll in her room when she felt an urge in her tummy.
She knew what that meant.
She had to go to the bathroom.
She put her doll on her bed and ran to the door.
But the door was closed and she heard water running.
Her brother was in the bathroom.
He always took a long time.
Lily knocked on the door and said, "I need to go!
Hurry up!" But her brother did not answer.
He was singing a loud song.
Lily felt the urge get stronger.
She did not want to wet her pants.
She looked around her room for a place to go.
She saw her doll on her bed.
She had an idea.
She grabbed her doll and ran to the corner.
She pulled down her pants and sat on her doll.
She peed on her doll.
She felt better.
She got up and pulled up her pants.
She looked at her doll.
Her doll was wet and smelled bad.
She felt sorry for her doll.
She did not mean to hurt her.
She heard the bathroom door open.
Her brother came out.
He saw her doll in the corner.
He said, "What did you do to your doll?" Lily started to cry.
She said, "I had to go and you were in the bathroom and I peed on my doll.
I'm sorry.
I'm sorry." Her brother looked at her.
He felt sorry for her too.
He said, "It's okay.
Don't cry.
We can wash your doll and make her clean.
She will be fine.
Come on, let's go to the bathroom and wash her." He took her hand and her doll and led her to the bathroom.
He helped her wash her doll and dry her hair.
He said, "See?
She looks pretty again.
She is a rare doll.
She is strong and brave.
Just like you." He gave her a hug and a kiss.
Lily smiled.
She said, "Thank you.
You are a good brother.
I love you." They hugged and kissed.
They went back to her room and played with her doll and her blocks.
They were happy.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.

She couldn't find her favorite toy car.

They spent the day playing and talking about the body.
At the end of the day, Sally said, "Thank you, Tom, for teaching me about the lung.

Everyday he would stand in front of his stove and stir a pot of soup.

He leaned over and looked to see what it was.
A small foot was poking up from under a blanket!
The man was surprised and yelled, "Who are you?" A little voice said, "It's me, I'm a tiny boy!" The tall man was amazed and asked the little boy what he was doing in his house.
The tiny boy told him that he had followed a mouse in and curled up under the blanket to take a nap!
The tall man smiled and said, "Oh, ok!
How about I make you a bowl of soup?" The tiny boy was delighted and said yes please!
So the tall man stirred the soup and served the little boy.
And they both enjoyed their soup.

When he was done, he held up a big smile.

Mommy was so proud of him.

Max loved to play and run around all day.
One day, Max found a big book called a novel.
Max thought it was a toy and started to chew on it.
But then Max's owner told him to stop and lie down.
Max was sad because he wanted to play with the novel.
So, when no one was looking, Max took the novel and ran away.
Max ran and ran until he found a big tree.
Max climbed up the tree and started to read the novel.
But then, Max got scared because it was getting dark and he couldn't find his way back home.
Max tried to climb down the tree, but he fell and hurt himself.
Max was all alone and couldn't move.
Eventually, Max's owner found him and took him to the vet.
But it was too late, Max had hurt himself too much and didn't make it.
Max's owner was very sad and wished Max had just listened and not taken the novel.
Once upon a time, there was a girl called Poppy.
Poppy was only three years old and she was out for a walk in the park.
Suddenly, Poppy saw a buckle on the ground.
It was a really pretty buckle, but it was also very dirty.
Poppy wanted to pick up the buckle, so she bent down and pinch it.
Then she saw a strange thing - the buckle began to move.
It wasn’t a buckle at all - it was a tiny little mouse!
The mouse said to Poppy: “Oh help me!
I am stuck inside this buckle and I cannot get out!” Poppy was not scared, so she bent down and carefully opened the buckle.
Then the little mouse thanked her and scurried away.
Poppy smiled and put the buckle in her pocket.
She was happy she could help the little mouse.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy.
She was three years old.
One day, her mom said: "Amy, it's time to take a bath!" Amy grabbed her pan and ran to the bathroom.
She splashed water everywhere.
Then, she got into the water and started washing her hair.
It was so funny, because her hair was very hairy!
When she was done, she ran downstairs.
She was dripping wet but she was so excited.
She said: "Mom!
I took a bath!
It was so much fun!" Her mom smiled and said: "Great job, Amy!
Now go put some dry clothes on." The end.
One day, a boy named Tim found a key.
The key was big and shiny.
Tim wanted to find what the key could open.
He looked all around his tidy room, but there was no lock.
Tim was sad.
Tim went to his friend, Sam.
Sam had a big seat in his house.
Tim and Sam sat on the seat and talked about the key.
They wanted to find the lock, too.
But they started to fight.
Tim wanted to keep the key, but Sam wanted it, too.
In the end, Tim and Sam were so mad that they threw the key out the window.
The key was lost in the tall grass.
They could not find it again.
Tim and Sam were very sad and did not find what the key could open.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She liked to play outside in the sunshine with her dog.
One day, while they were playing, Lily discovered a pretty rock.
She picked it up and showed it to her dog.
Later that day, Lily's mom showed her an image of a butterfly in a book.
Lily thought it was very beautiful and wanted to see a real butterfly.
So, she went outside to look for one.
After a while, she saw a butterfly flying around in the garden.
She was very happy to have discovered it.
Lily was a very compassionate girl.
When she saw her friend crying, she gave her a hug and told her everything would be okay.
Her friend felt much better after that.
Lily learned that being kind and caring can make others feel better.
Once upon a time, there was a naughty penny.
The penny loved to get into trouble.
One day, the penny found himself stuck inside of a toy box.
He tried pushing and shaking as hard as he could, but he just couldn't get out!
He called out to the other pennies, but no one answered.
He was lost and alone, until he heard a voice.
The voice belonged to a kind fairy.
She told the naughty penny, “Don't worry, I'm here to help.
I'll use my magic to restore you back to where you belong.” The fairy waved her wand and the penny was suddenly back outside of the box.
The penny thanked the fairy for restoring him back.
From then on, the naughty penny promised to stay out of trouble.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She lived in a small house with her mom and dad.
One day, her mom took her to a fancy store where they sold luxury toys.
Lily saw a beautiful doll and asked her mom to buy it for her.
Her mom said, "We can't buy everything we want, Lily.
That doll is too expensive." Lily felt sad and thought that she would never have that doll.
But then, her mom said, "Let's go to the park and have some fun." At the park, Lily saw a little boy who was dizzy and couldn't walk straight.
She asked him if he was okay, and he said he hadn't eaten anything all day.
Lily's mom bought him some food, and the little boy felt better.
Lily realized that having luxury toys wasn't as important as helping others.
She felt happy that she could help the little boy and thought that being kind was the best thing in the world.
From that day on, Lily always thought about how she could help others and make them happy.
Once upon a time there was a bad thief.
He wanted to take all the good things.
All the nice people were scared.
One day, two friends came by.
They had special powers, and were very brave.
They wanted to help everyone, so they worked together to restore things back to the way they were.
The friends used their powers to make the thief leave.
He was never seen again.
Everyone thanked the friends and was happy to have their good things back.
The friends had made the town safe again.
They were proud of what they had done, and everyone was grateful.
Once upon a time there were two friends who were going for a picnic.
They walked until they came to a tall hill.
As they looked around, they saw a zip running down the side of the hill.
So they followed the zip until they reached a big shade.
The shade was big and unknown.
The friends were excited.
They had found a secret place.
They sat under the shade and ate their food.
They even stayed there to take a nap.
They felt safe and happy under the shade.
After their nap, they decided to explore the area.
As they wandered, they found a zip in the ground.
They dug the zip open with their hands and to their surprise, a shiny golden coin popped out!
They had found a special unknown treasure.
The two friends hugged each other and then put the coin in their pocket.
They followed the zip back to their picnic blanket and talked excitedly about their adventure.
The treasure was their little secret and they kept it safe.
Anna and Ben are friends.
They like to play in the park.
One day, they find a map on a bench.
The map has a big X on it.
"Look, a map!" Anna says.
"Maybe it is a treasure map!" "Let's follow it!" Ben says.
"Maybe we can find gold or jewels!" They take the map and start to walk.
They follow the lines and arrows on the map.
They go past the swings, the slide, the pond and the bridge.
They come to a big tree.
"The X is here!" Anna says.
"The treasure must be under the tree!" They dig with their hands and their sticks.
They dig and dig, but they find nothing.
"Where is the treasure?" Ben asks.
"Did someone take it?" Suddenly, they hear a laugh.
They look up and see a boy in the tree.
He is holding a camera.
"Gotcha!" the boy says.
"It was a joke!
I made the map and put it on the bench.
I wanted to see if you would fall for it.
I filmed everything.
It is so funny!" Anna and Ben are angry.
They do not like the boy's joke.
They think it is mean and silly.
"That is not funny!" Anna says.
"That is rude!
You made us waste our time and get dirty!" "Yeah!" Ben says.
"You are not nice!
You are a bully!
We do not want to play with you!" They throw the map at the boy and run away.
They go back to the park and play with their other friends.
They forget about the boy and his joke.
They have fun and laugh.
They are brave and smart.
They do not let the boy's joke ruin their day.
They are happy.
Once there was a boy, and he was only three years old.
He had a lot of toy horses and one day he decided to take them to a stable.
When he arrived, it was very peaceful.
He saw many animals and he even said hello to them.
The boy then began to play with his horses.
He threw them around and galloped them around the stable.
He played until he was tired and the peaceful stable welcomed him and made him feel very happy.
When the sun set, the boy took his horses and went home, very satisfied with his day.
He knew that the stable was special and he would come back soon.
Anna and Ben were playing in the garden.
They liked to pretend they were chefs and prepare food for their dolls and teddies.
They used leaves, flowers, rocks and sticks as ingredients.
They had a small fire pit where they cooked their dishes.
"Look, Ben, I made a cake with petals and mud," Anna said, holding a round lump of dirt.
"Do you want to try some?" "No, thank you, Anna.
I made a soup with water and grass.
It smells good," Ben said, stirring a pot over the fire.
"Do you want to try some?" Anna nodded and put her cake down.
She went to Ben and took a sip of his soup.
She made a face and spat it out.
"Yuck, Ben, this is not soup.
This is yucky water," she said.
Ben laughed and said, "It's not yucky, Anna.
It's yummy.
You just don't like it because you're a picky eater." Anna was angry and said, "I'm not a picky eater, Ben.
You're a bad cook.
Your soup is gross and your fire is too big.
You're going to burn everything." Ben was angry too and said, "I'm not a bad cook, Anna.
You're a mean sister.
My soup is delicious and my fire is just right.
You're going to ruin everything." They started to argue and shout at each other.
They did not notice that the fire was growing bigger and bigger.
They did not notice that the wind was blowing the smoke towards the house.
They did not notice that their mom was inside, taking a nap.
The smoke reached the house and set off the alarm.
The alarm was loud and scary.
It woke up mom and made her jump out of bed.
She smelled the smoke and ran to the window.
She saw the fire in the garden and her children arguing near it.
She felt helpless and scared.
She grabbed her phone and called for help.
She yelled at Anna and Ben to get away from the fire and come inside.
Anna and Ben heard their mom and saw the smoke.
They realized they had made a big mistake.
They felt sorry and scared.
They dropped their pots and ran to their mom.
They hugged her and said they were sorry.
They waited for the firemen to come and put out the fire.
They learned a lesson that day.
They learned to be careful with fire and to be nice to each other.
Tom likes to jog with his dad.
They jog in the park, where there are many trees and flowers.
Tom likes to see the birds and the dogs that run and play.
Sometimes, they jog to the pond and feed the ducks.
Tom thinks jogging is fun and good for him.
One day, when they are jogging, Tom sees a big hole in the ground.
He does not see it in time and falls in.
He hurts his knee and cries.
His dad hears him and runs to help him.
He lifts him out of the hole and hugs him.
He says, "Are you okay, Tom?
You are very lucky.
The hole was not very deep.
You could have been hurt more." Tom's dad carries him to their car.
He puts a band-aid on his knee and gives him some water.
He says, "Let's go home, Tom.
You need some rest.
We can jog another day." Tom nods and says, "Okay, dad.
Thank you for helping me.
I love you." When they get home, Tom's mom is waiting for them.
She sees Tom's band-aid and asks, "What happened, Tom?
Did you have an accident?" Tom tells her what happened.
She says, "Oh, poor Tom.
You are very brave.
And you are very lucky.
The hole could have been worse.
I'm glad you are okay." She takes him to his room and tucks him in his bed.
She gives him a kiss and says, "You can sleep now, Tom.
You will feel better soon." She turns on his night light and leaves.
Tom looks at his bed.
He likes his bed.
It is soft and warm.
It has a blue blanket and a red pillow.
It also has a green carpet on the floor.
Tom likes his carpet.
It is fuzzy and cozy.
He likes to play on it with his toys.
He thinks, "I am lucky.
I have a nice bed and a nice carpet.
I have a good dad and a good mom.
I have a good life." He smiles and closes his eyes.
He falls asleep and dreams of jogging in the park.
Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a small rabbit.
The rabbit was white and had big ears.
The rabbit's name was Fluffy.
Fluffy liked to play with his friends.
One day, Fluffy found an amazing pebble.
The pebble was shiny and smooth.
Fluffy showed the pebble to his friend, a little bird named Chirpy.
Chirpy said, "Wow, Fluffy!
That is an amazing pebble!
Where did you find it?" Fluffy told Chirpy that he found it near the big tree.
As they were talking, a big loud sound came from the sky.
It made Fluffy and Chirpy tremble.
They were scared.
They hid behind the big tree and held the amazing pebble tight.
After a while, the loud sound went away.
Fluffy and Chirpy came out from behind the tree.
They were not scared anymore.
They laughed and played with the amazing pebble.
They knew that as long as they were together, they would be brave.
From that day on, Fluffy and Chirpy were the best of friends.
They played in the big forest every day.
And they always kept the amazing pebble with them, to remind them of their brave adventure.
One day, Lola was smiling as she sat at the piano.
She had been learning to play it for a couple of months.
Lola had been wanting to play the piano since she saw Mama play it one day.
Mama always smiled so much when she was playing the piano.
Suddenly, Lola heard Mama's voice coming from the other room.
"Come quick, Lola.
You must see something," Mama said.
Lola ran down the hallway to find Mama looking at an old black piano.
"It's for you, Lola," Mama said.
Lola was so excited that she started smiling even bigger than before.
However, when Lola tried to play the black piano, it was not as easy as it was with the other piano.
She felt so frustrated that she wanted to cry.
Mama said, "It's okay, Lola.
You just need practice and soon you will be able to play it just as good as you can play the other piano." So Lola practiced for some days and the black piano started to sound better.
She smiled as she played and soon it sounded just as good as the other piano.
Mama came by to listen to Lola and smiled proudly.
"I knew you could do it, Lola," Mama said.
Lola smiled and continued to play the black piano, feeling happy and proud.
Once upon a time, there was a bright girl named Sally.
She liked to talk to her friends and play games.
One day, she wanted to play baseball.
She asked her friends if they wanted to join her.
Her friends said yes and they all had lots of fun.
Sally hit the ball so hard that it flew over the fence.
Everyone cheered for her.
At the end of the game, Sally looked at the score.
She had the highest score!
She was so proud and she showed her friends her bright smile.
Sally talked about her amazing score all the way home.
She knew she would win the next game too.
Once there was a mom who had a daughter named Emma.
Emma loved to work hard, but she wasn't very good at it.
Mom was always very patient and encouraging when it came to helping Emma learn how to do her work.
One day, Mom said to Emma, "Okay, honey, let's practice working hard together." Mom gave Emma a special job that was too difficult for Emma to do on her own.
So, Mom and Emma started working on it together.
They worked hard, but things weren't going very well.
Emma kept making mistakes, and Mom had to keep helping her, which was getting very tiring.
Finally, by the end of the day, Mom and Emma had finished the job together.
Mom said to Emma, "I'm so proud of you.
You worked so hard, and you did a good job.
See - working hard pays off!" Emma was so proud of herself.
She had learned that when she worked hard, good things would happen.
Tim and Lily are playing in the park.
They like to run and jump and slide.
They hear a noise in the sky.
It is a plane.
The plane is loud.
It makes a zoom sound.
"Look, Lily, a plane!" Tim says.
He points to the sky.
"I see it, Tim.
It is big and white.
Where is it going?" Lily asks.
"I don't know.
Maybe to another park.
Maybe to see other kids.
Do you want to go on a plane, Lily?" Tim says.
Lily thinks for a moment.
She likes to see new things.
But she does not like loud noises.
She shakes her head.
"No, Tim.
I don't want to go on a plane.
It is too loud.
It hurts my ears.
I like to play here with you.
This is our park.
It is quiet and nice." Lily says.
Tim nods.
He understands.
He does not like loud noises either.
He likes to play here with Lily.
They are friends.
They hold hands and run to the swings.
They forget about the plane.
They have fun.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mary.
Mary was very happy, but one day she made a mistake and was too scared to tell her mom.
She started to feel nervous and her heart beat fast.
When her mom asked her what she had done, Mary had to tell the truth.
Her mom was sad and disappointed.
But then she hugged Mary tight and said: "It's okay, I forgive you." Mary felt so much better, like a heavy weight had been lifted off her shoulders.
As a surprise her mom asked her to get in the car and took her to the gas station.
Mary was so excited and couldn't believe it.
As Mary walked into the gas station, she found something special - a big box of chocolates!
Mary was so glad her mom had forgiven her and had given her something special as well.
She thanked her mom and promised that she would never make the same mistake again.
Mary learned a valuable lesson that day - that it was important to forgive and forget.
From then onwards, she would always try her best to use kind words whenever she was feeling nervous.
Once upon a time, there was a bee who lived in a hive.
The bee's hive was crisp and smooth, and it was filled with honey.
Each day, the bee would bravely fly out of the hive, high up into the clouds.
There, the bee would buzz around and find sweet, yummy pollen to collect.
Back at the hive, the bee would carefully unload the pollen into the honeycomb.
Then, the bee would use its wings to flutter around and make a honey so smooth and delicious.
Every day, the bee would yield more and more honey until the hive was filled with it.
The bee was so proud of all its hard work.
It had made the hive so sweet and full of yummy honey.
So with a happy buzz, the bee would fly off to find more pollen and make more delicious honey.
And everyone, of course, was extremely happy with that.
One day, there were two brothers who were both very eager to explore.
The younger brother was very excited to go but the older brother was a bit jealous.
He asked their mum, "Can I go too?" Mum said,"No, you can't come with us.
You have to stay and look after the house, but I will pass you something special."  The older brother was very suspicious but also a bit jealous.
He asked his mum what was going to happen and she said, "I'm going to pass you a key.
It will help you explore the town while we are away."  The younger brother was very excited.
He ran around the house and said, "I'm ready to explore the town!".
Once upon a time there was a strong kite with bright colors.
It loved to sing in the wind!
It was so tough it never got broken.
One day a little boy wanted to fly the kite in the sky.
He was so excited!
He grabbed hold of the kite tightly and ran and sang as it flew.
The kite soared higher and higher and sang louder too.
The little boy laughed and cheered louder and louder as the kite flew and sang higher in the sky.
As the kite flew away, the little boy and the kite sang one last song together.
They both said goodbye as the kite flew away into the clouds.
Once upon a time there was an ancient house.
Every night, the house would make scary noises.
The noises would make the little girl who lived in the house very scared.
One night, something even more scary happened.
The little girl's brother came into the room.
He held a pair of scissors in his hand.
He shook them and said, "I'm going to scare you!" The little girl was very scared.
She was so scared that she couldn't move.
But then, something amazing happened.
The girl's mom came into the room and said, "Stop that!
You don't need to scare your sister!" Her brother put the scissors down and returned to his room.
The little girl felt relieved and safe.
A few moments later, the house became quiet.
The little girl felt better and soon was able to sleep.
Once upon a time there was a poor soldier who had to wander through the forest all alone.
As he wandered he came across a small cottage.
When he knocked on the door the owner of the cottage opened it.
The soldier asked the owner, "Do you have anything to eat?"  The owner replied, "Yes I do.
Please come in and help yourself."  The soldier thanked the owner and stepped inside.
Inside he found a big pot of stew.
The soldier enjoyed the stew and thanked the owner.
The owner said, "It's my pleasure.
The forest can be a scary place and you look like you could use a friend."  The poor soldier was so happy to have a friend.
From then on whenever he needed to wander through the forest he knew he could count on the owner of the cottage for a hot meal and some kind words.
Once upon a time, there was a brother and sister who loved to ride their bikes.
Every day they went out, down the dirt path all the way to the park, ready to explore and find treasures.
One day they found something incredible: a big, green treasure box!
It was full of wonderful things, like shiny coins and golden coins.
But the best treasure of them all was a nice big bike with two sparkly handles.
"Wow, this really is a treasure!" said the brother.
The sister smiled and said, "Let's take it home and ride it together!" The brother nodded, and together they picked up the bike and carefully carried it all the way back home.
From then on, every day they went out to the park and rode their new bike together.
It was so much fun, and it felt so good to ride together.
Soon enough, the brother and sister had many wonderful adventures together on their magical bike.
They were the happiest when they were riding together, and that bike became their special shared treasure.
Anna and Ben were playing in the living room.
They liked to pretend they were pirates and explorers.
They used the furniture as their ships and islands.
They had a lot of fun, but they also made a big mess.
They threw pillows and blankets everywhere.
They tied scarves and belts to the chairs and tables.
"Look, Anna, I made a flag!" Ben said, waving a red scarf.
"We are the best pirates ever!" "Yes, we are!" Anna agreed, holding a wooden spoon as a sword.
"But we have to be careful.
There are sharks and crocodiles in the water!" They jumped from one piece of furniture to another, avoiding the floor.
They made loud noises and laughed a lot.
But then, they heard a knock on the door.
It was their mom, coming home from work.
She opened the door and saw the living room.
She was not happy.
"Anna!
Ben!
What have you done?" she asked, looking at the mess.
"This is not how you treat the furniture!
You could have broken something or hurt yourselves!" "Sorry, mom," Anna and Ben said, looking down.
"We were just playing." "I know you were playing, but you have to be respectful of the things we have.
The furniture is not a toy.
It is for sitting and eating and reading.
You have to take care of it, not ruin it.
And you have to clean up after yourselves, not leave everything lying around.
Do you understand?" mom said, sternly.
"Yes, mom," Anna and Ben said, nodding.
"We understand." "Good.
Now, help me untie these scarves and belts and put everything back where it belongs.
And then, you can play with your real toys in your room.
But no more jumping on the furniture, okay?" mom said, softly.
"Okay, mom," Anna and Ben said, smiling.
"We're sorry.
We love you." They hugged their mom and helped her clean up the living room.
They learned their lesson.
They realized that the furniture was not for playing, but for being graceful and comfortable.
They decided to be more careful and respectful of the things they had.
They still liked to play and pretend, but they did it in a safer and neater way.
They were happy and so was their mom.
One day, Alex and his grandpa were out for a walk.
As they walked along, they saw something strange on the ground.
It was a skull.
Then, he said, "I wish I could become comfortable now!" Grandpa laughed and said, "Let's go home.
I'll make you something comfy to sit on." So, the two of them went home and Alex became comfortable in his new chair.
Once upon a time, there was a grumpy cat named Tom.
Tom did not like to play with others.
One day, he saw a rake in the yard.
Tom decided to have some fun with it.
Tom used the rake to gather leaves into a big pile.
He then wanted to decorate the pile with flowers.
So, he picked some pretty flowers and put them on the leaves.
The pile looked very nice.
Soon, other animals came to see Tom's pretty pile.
They all played together and had fun.
Tom was not grumpy anymore.
He learned that playing with others can be a lot of fun.
Once upon a time there was a very special girl named Jane.
Jane was a three year old with a very big dream.
She wanted to win a crown!
It was finally the day of the competition and Jane was so excited!
Jane was competing with all the other children in her town and she knew it would be hard.
"Don't worry Jane," said her mom.
"I know you will do great!" Jane walked into the competition room with a big smile.
She saw all the other children looking very competitive.
But Jane wasn't afraid.
After everyone finished competing, it was time to give out awards.
Jane was sweating and nervous.
Then the leader of the competition announced that the winner of the crown was Jane!
Everyone clapped and cheered.
Jane was so excited she could hardly believe it.
She was the happiest and proudest three year old around.
She decided to wear her crown everyday and never take it off!
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Susie.
She smiled at all of the creatures she saw when she walked out of her house each day.
One day, she saw an animal with a big, fierce face.
It was a lion!
The lion walked towards her and Susie was scared.
The lion came close and said, “Don't be scared, Susie.
I promise I won't hurt you.” Susie was surprised and stepped back.
The lion laughed and handed her a big jar.
He explained that he wanted her to have the jar as a gift.
The lion smiled and said, “This jar has magical powers.
Whatever you wish for will come true, as long as you promise to use it wisely.” Susie was so excited!
She hugged the lion tight and thanked him.
Since then, Susie has taken great care of the jar.
Whenever she has a wish, she pulls out the jar and closes her eyes.
She whispers her wish, before tightly closing the jar again and making a promise to use it wisely.
Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to buy a new top.
She went to the shop and looked around.
Suddenly, she saw a nice pink blouse.
She liked it so much, so she chose it.
The little girl went to the cashier and paid for it.
She was so excited and couldn't wait to wear it.
When she got home, she put the blouse on.
She twirled around and around, feeling so happy.
The pink color looked so pretty and bright.
She smiled and knew it was a good choice.
The end!
Once upon a time, there was a little girl.
She was only three years old and she wanted to be a chef!
She asked her mom for a pan so she could start cooking.
Her mom agreed, so she got her a special pan.
It was a different kind of pan, she had never seen one like it before.
The little girl was so excited to finally cook with her new pan.
She put all the ingredients in the pan and set to work.
It almost felt like forever before the food was ready.
Then finally, after some delay, the food was ready.
The little girl couldn't wait to eat her cooking.
She tasted it and it was delicious!
She was so happy she had her own pan that she could use to cook.
She knew she could make all kinds of different things with it.
The little girl was very proud of her new pan and she still uses it to this day.
Once upon a time, there was a queen.
She lived in a big castle.
The queen had a thick, warm coat to wear when it was cold outside.
She liked to play in the snow with her friends.
One day, the queen went outside to play.
She put on her thick coat and ran into the snow.
She saw a big snowman.
The queen wanted to play with the snowman, but the snowman was sad.
The snowman told the queen that his hat had vanished.
The queen wanted to help find the hat.
They looked high and low, but they could not find it.
Then, the queen had an idea.
She gave her thick coat to the snowman.
The snowman was happy and not sad anymore.
The queen and the snowman played all day in the snow.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to play outside and explore the world around her.
One day, she saw a big puddle on the ground.
She wanted to jump in it, but her mom said no because it was too high and she might get hurt.
Lily was sad, but then she saw a little bug crawling towards the puddle.
She followed the bug and saw that it went into a drain.
She asked her mom where the drain went and her mom explained that it went to the river and if something goes in the drain, it might hurt the animals in the river.
Lily realized that it was important to follow the rules and listen to her mom.
She decided to play somewhere else and be careful not to hurt anything.
