She had colourful crayons, glitter, and lots of stickers.
One day she decided to decorate a journal.
In it, she put lots of pink and purple stickers and drew pretty little hearts.
She knew it was going to be yummy!
When Sandy finished decorating, she was so excited that she ran around and showed it to everyone she could find.
Her mom, her dad and her brothers all admired her work.
She was so proud of a job well done.
Sandy made the journal her very own special place.
She wrote stories and drew pictures in it every day.
She was the happiest girl around.
Now Sandy always has something both yummy and fun to share with her family and friends.
Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily.
One day, Lily went to her room to play.
She wanted to open the door, but the knob was too high for her.
She said, "Mommy, can you come help me open the door?"  Mommy came to help and opened the door for Lily.
Lily was so happy and said, "Mommy, you're great at opening doors!"  Lily played with her toys for a while, but then she got bored.
She said, "Mommy, can you come play with me?"  Mommy said, "Sure, I would love to play with you!" They played together and had a great time.
John was a popular boy.
He was always playing with his friends and having a great time.
One day, he wanted to go on an adventure.
So he found some yummy treats and put them in a bag.
John took the bag and started walking.
Along the way, they saw a leak in the ground.
John thought it was so cool.
So he decided to eat some of his treats there.
It was so yummy!
John was having a lot of fun.
Soon, his friends joined him and they all had a great time eating the treats.
John was getting more and more popular every day.
Once upon a time, there was an open field.
The field was soft and fluffy, making it a perfect place to play.
On one special day, something amazing came out of the sky!
It was a big rainbow-colored balloon that was so soft and shiny.
The balloon floated around the open field and the children were so excited to play with it.
They reached out to touch it, but the balloon was too quick for them.
It kept flying around in different directions, making them chase after it.
Eventually, the balloon came to a stop near a big tree.
The children couldn't believe their luck!
They raced to the tree, and the balloon landed on the soft grass.
The children were laughing and happy, but then something strange happened.
The big rainbow-colored balloon started to open.
Inside was a secret surprise!
The children gasped in surprise.
It was the best day ever!
Once upon a time there was a little cow called Beth.
Beth was very playful and loved to bounce.
Everywhere she went she would bounce up and down, happy and excited.
One day, Beth caught sight of a long spell in a nearby tree.
She wondered what the spell was but she was too small to reach it.
She thought for a moment before she got an idea.
She carefully bounced as high as she could and managed to grab the spell!
Beth asked the spell, “What can you do?” The spell answered in a whispery voice, “I can make your bounces longer.
Would you like to try?” Beth nodded eagerly and the spell began to work.
Suddenly Beth’s bounces became much longer!
She laughed and bounced around, overjoyed with her achievement.
The long spell had helped Beth to bounce higher than ever before.
From then on, she was always the bounciest cow in the entire land!
Once, there was a little girl named Ruth.
Ruth was three years old and she loved to play.
One day, Ruth went to the park with her mommy.
At the park, there was a big drum.
It was round and soft.
Ruth's mommy said, "Ruth, can you understand what the drum is for?" Ruth smiled and said, "Yes!
I can understand the drum.
I can bang it!" So Ruth and her mommy played with the drum.
Ruth banged it softly with her hands, and her mommy tapped it with her feet.
They made lots of happy music together.
Ruth had fun at the park.
She was very happy to understand how to play the drum.
Once upon a time, there was a brave knight.
He wore a suit of armour, which was shiny and strong.
He journeyed though the unknown, looking for things to explore.
One day, he spotted something in the distance.
He moved closer and was surprised to see an old man holding a sword.
The knight thanked the old man, who said, "You must continue your quest, brave knight.
Go now into the unknown, and bring light to the darkness!"  The knight thanked the old man once again and set off into the unknown on his quest.
Jill was feeling anxious.
She had been dreading this day for weeks on end.
It was her first day at school and she was so scared.
Her teacher smiled at her and handed her a piece of chalk.
She was excited to hold it in her hands.
She grabbed it and tried to draw a picture of a flower on the blackboard.
But no matter how hard she tried, her hand would not stay still.
She was so nervous that the picture was a big mess.
Her teacher was kind and she helped Jill to find the courage she needed to finish the picture.
Beautiful flowers soon appeared on the board.
Jill smiled at her handiwork, but before she could even finish going over the lines with red chalk, she lost her balance and fell.
She was embarrassed, but the teacher comforted her and helped her back on her feet.
Jill had come to this special day ready to learn and have some fun.
All the anxiousness she felt that morning was gone, and she was ready to make her own flowers with the chalk.
Lily and Ben are friends.
They like to play with hoops in the park.
Lily has a pink hoop and Ben has a blue hoop.
They take turns to roll the hoops on the grass and catch them.
One day, a big boy comes to the park.
He sees Lily and Ben's hoops and wants to play with them.
He runs to Lily and grabs her pink hoop.
He says, "This is my hoop now.
You can't have it." Lily is sad and angry.
She says, "No, that is my hoop.
Give it back to me.
You are not nice." Ben is brave and tries to help Lily.
He says, "Leave her alone.
She is my friend.
You have to share." The big boy laughs and says, "No, I don't.
I have a long arm and you are small.
I can keep both hoops." He reaches for Ben's blue hoop, but Ben is quick.
He rolls his hoop away from the big boy and runs to Lily.
They hold hands and run to the other side of the park.
The big boy is mad.
He tries to chase them, but he trips on the pink hoop and falls on the ground.
He cries and says, "Ow, ow, ow.
That hurts." Lily and Ben see a nice lady who works at the park.
They tell her what happened.
She says, "That is not good.
He should not take your hoops.
I will talk to him and make him say sorry." She goes to the big boy and helps him up.
She says, "You should not be mean to other kids.
You have to ask before you play with their things.
You have to say sorry to Lily and Ben." The big boy feels bad.
He says, "I'm sorry.
I was wrong.
Can I play with you?" Lily and Ben are kind.
They say, "Yes, you can.
But you have to be nice and share." They give him a hoop and they all play together.
They have fun and make a new friend.
Once upon a time there was a spoiled shark.
He lived in the big, blue ocean and was always looking for fun things to do.
One day he decided to take a journey.
As he was swimming along, he mentioned to some of his fish friends that he wanted to explore more of the ocean.
They got excited and joined him on his adventure.
They swam for hours, exploring all the different places in the sea.
After a while, they spotted something far away in the distance.
As they got closer, they realized that it was a huge ship!
The sharks were so excited.
They swam around the big boat, poking their noses in all the nooks and crannies.
Soon, they realized that the ship was full of treasure!
Their eyes sparkled with excitement.
The sharks were so happy.
They thanked their friend for mentioning the journey and promised to share some of the coins and jewels with him.
After claiming the treasure, the spoiled shark and his friends happily went back home, swimming and playing in the blue ocean along the way.
Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweetie.
Tweetie lived in a big tree with all of her bird friends.
One day, a big storm came and disturbed the birds' peaceful home.
The wind blew so hard that it knocked down some of the branches and made the birds scared.
Tweetie and her friends decided to fly away to find a new home.
They searched and searched until they found a beautiful garden with impressive flowers and a little pond.
They decided to make their new home there and it was the best decision they ever made.
From that day on, Tweetie and her friends lived a happy life in the garden.
They sang songs, ate yummy seeds, and played in the sun.
They never forgot their old home, but they were grateful for their new one.
Sometimes, when the wind blew hard, it would disturb their peaceful life, but they knew they could always find a new home if they had to.
Lila and Tom were friends who liked to play in the park.
They liked to swing, slide and run.
One day, they saw a big red balloon in the sky.
They wanted to catch it and have fun with it.
They ran after the balloon, but it was too fast and too high.
They tried to jump, but they could not reach it.
They felt sad and angry.
They wanted the balloon so much.
Then, they saw a man with a long stick.
He was selling balloons to other children.
They ran to him and asked for a balloon.
But he said they had to pay him money.
They did not have any money.
They felt more sad and angry.
They decided to wait until the man was busy with other children.
Then, they would take a balloon and run away.
They thought this was a good plan.
They hid behind a tree and watched the man.
But the man was very smart.
He saw them hiding and knew what they wanted to do.
He decided to delay them.
He made a loud noise with his stick and scared the birds.
The birds flew away and made the balloon move with them.
The balloon went far away from the park.
Lila and Tom saw the balloon leaving.
They felt very sad and angry.
They cried and shouted.
They blamed each other for losing the balloon.
The man felt sorry for them.
He saw that they had a strong spirit and a powerful wish.
He decided to give them a balloon for free.
He called them and showed them a big blue balloon.
He said they could have it if they promised to be good and share.
Lila and Tom stopped crying and shouting.
They looked at the big blue balloon.
They liked it very much.
They said sorry to the man and to each other.
They promised to be good and share.
They thanked the man and took the balloon.
They ran to the park and played with the balloon.
They swung, slid and ran with it.
They felt happy and friendly.
They learned that stealing was bad and sharing was good.
They decided to be friends with the man and the birds.
They enjoyed the big blue balloon.
Alice was hungry.
She saw a fan in the corner of the room and it made her happy.
She ran over to it, and skipped around it.
She enjoyed the cool breeze it gave her.
Then she got an idea.
She skipped to the kitchen to get a snack.
She found some yummy cookies and she grabbed one.
She skipped back to the fan to eat the cookie.
While she was eating the cookie, she kept feeling the breeze of the fan.
She was very happy and it kept her cool while she enjoyed her snack.
Once she was done, she gave the fan a big hug and said, "Thank you, fan!" and she skipped away, feeling very content.
Once upon a time there was a little girl called Bella.
She was playing in her garden when she saw two animals, a rabbit and a squirrel, walking by.
She wanted to join them but wasn't sure how.
So she asked them, "Would you like me to join you?" The rabbit hopped over and said, "Yes, we'd love to have you join us!" So the three of them travelled around the garden.
They talked and laughed, looked at the flowers and skipped in the grass.
Then they came across a nut.

The squirrel said, "Look, I know this is a very important nut and I'm sure it will give us great benefits if we all join together and share it!" So they all joined together, holding the nut between them.
But then, before they could start eating it, the squirrel said, "This won't work unless we work together.
If we don't help each other, the nut won't give us anything at all." The little girl smiled and said, "That's a great lesson.

We should all help one another out, then we will be able to achieve a lot more together than if we did it alone!" Moral: In life, it's important to work together, because together we can do bigger and better things!
There was a wall in the bedroom.
It was tall and thick.
It was there for a long time.
One day, a fast truck came and brought a new wall.
It was bigger and brighter.
The workers put the new wall in place of the old wall.
They took away the old wall and replaced it with the new one.
The new wall looked shiny and pretty.
Everyone was very happy.
It was much better than the old wall.
The family had so much fun with the new wall.
They hung up toys and made it a play area.
They used it as a background for fun family photos.
They had many hours of enjoyment with the new wall.
The new wall was much better than the old one.
It was faster, brighter and it made everyone happy.
One night, Henry was camping in a tent with his family.
He felt very independent and he was excited to celebrate his first camping trip.
Henry looked up at the stars in the night sky and called out "Mom, can I stay up a bit longer?"  His mom smiled and said "Yes, I think it's okay".
Henry jumped up and down, excited to stay up late.
He saw a bright light in the sky and asked what it was.
"That's a shooting star, Henry" said his mom.
"Make a wish!" Henry closed his eyes and made a wish.
Then he and his family started to dance around the tent, celebrating his first camping trip.
Henry laughed, feeling so lucky to spend time with his family and to have such an independent adventure.
He was sure it was a night he would never forget.
John and his dad wanted to travel.
So they put on their thick belts and went outside.
They saw a big tree with a bushy top.
Dad said they should travel to the top of the tree.
So they started up the tree.
Dad went first and John followed.
They went slowly and carefully around the trunk and higher and higher.
John got tired, but dad said they were almost there.
And soon enough they were at the top!
It was so high!
John looked around and saw lots of things.
Everywhere was green.
There were birds and grass.
They sat together at the top and looked down.
Below them were houses and streets.
Dad said they had traveled a long way and it was worth it.
John smiled and hugged his dad.
Then they slowly traveled down the tree and went home.
Once upon a time, there was a big toe named Tom.
Tom was envious of the other toes because they were always invited to play games.
One day, Tom decided to invite his toe friends to play a game with him.
Tom said, "Hey friends, let's play a fun game together!" All the other toes were happy and agreed to play with Tom.
They decided to play a game called "Jump the Rock." The toes took turns jumping over a small rock.
As they played, the little toe named Tim jumped too high and landed on the rock.
"Ouch!" cried Tim, "I hurt myself!" All the other toes stopped playing and gathered around Tim.
They felt sad for him.
In the end, the toes decided not to play "Jump the Rock" anymore.
They realized it was not a safe game to play.
Tom was sad because his game had caused his friend Tim to get hurt.
From that day on, the toes never played "Jump the Rock" again, and Tom learned to be more careful when inviting his friends to play games.
Once upon a time there was a girl called Daisy.
Daisy loved playing in the park and playing with her friends.
One day, Daisy was playing in the park and her friends had a kite, which looked so fun!
Daisy's friends asked her: "Do you want to fly the kite with us?" Daisy was so excited and said, "Yes, of course!" Together they flew the kite and it was so much fun.
Daisy felt so happy, but at the same time she was a bit scared, because the wind made the kite go so high!
Suddenly, the wind stopped and the kite fell down.
Everyone was scared and Daisy felt her heart beating so fast.
But luckily, the kite was alright and Daisy and her friends were so relieved.
The next morning, Daisy went back to the park and flew her own kite.
She felt so brave and happy and the wind was so gentle.
Daisy flew her kite until the sun went down and she was so proud of herself.
Once upon a time there was a dependable deer.
Every morning the deer went for a swim in the river.
He enjoyed jumping in the cool water and frolicking in the bubbles.
One day the deer met a new friend.
It was a fox!
They both loved to swim together.
They splashed and laughed and jumped around all morning.
The dependable deer and the fox played together until lunchtime.
Then they both said goodbye, until next time.
The deer was so happy to have a new friend.
He felt so free when he was swimming with the fox.
From then on, the deer and the fox went swimming together every day.
The end.
Once upon a time there was a small boy, he was very curious and wanted to unpack his father's suitcase.
He was about three years old and he excitedly rummaged through the case to find fun things to play with.
He found lots of interesting things, like shiny coins and a colorful sock.
The little boy was so happy with his discovery.
He quickly grabbed the sock and started running to the kitchen to play.
He was singing a loud, noisy song, and the parents were getting annoyed.
They shouted at him to stop and put the sock back in the suitcase.
The little boy was confused, he didn't want to stop his fun.
He started to cry and threw the sock on the ground.
His parents were very angry.
They scolded him and asked him to go to his room.
The little boy slowly walked away with tears in his eyes.
The sock stayed on the ground and nobody played with it again.
Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a famous cat named Tom.
Tom loved to sleep all day long.
He would sleep on the soft grass, under the warm sun.
One day, Tom woke up and found a map on the ground.
The map showed a big park with a lot of trees.
Tom thought, "I want to go to this park and sleep under a tree." So, Tom took the map and started walking.
On his way, Tom met a little dog named Max.
Max asked, "Where are you going, Tom?" Tom showed Max the map and said, "I am going to the big park to sleep under a tree." Max liked the idea and went with Tom.
They walked together, following the map, until they reached the big park.
There, they found a big tree and slept under it, happy and safe.
Today was a special event.
Everyone was happy and excited to celebrate!
The children ran around slowly.
They laughed and hugged each other.
The adults made food.
There were yummy treats and fresh juice to drink.
All the children gathered around and cheered.
They wanted to start celebrating!
First, the youngest child blew out some candles on a cake.
Everyone clapped.
Then they enjoyed the food and took turns opening presents.
Finally, the sun started to set.
Everyone hugged and said goodbye.
It was a great day and everyone enjoyed celebrating the event.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to play outside in the mud and get her hands dirty.
One day, her mommy told her it was time to wash up for dinner.
Lily didn't want to stop playing, but she knew she had to wash her hands.
After dinner, Lily's daddy turned on the TV to watch his favorite show.
But the picture was dull and fuzzy.
He realized there was a problem with the network.
He tried to fix it, but he couldn't.
So, he called a man to come and fix the network.
While the man was fixing the network, Lily's mommy asked her to help her wash the dishes.
Lily didn't want to stop playing again, but she knew she had to help her mommy.
She washed the dishes with soap and water until they were sparkly clean.
The end.
Once upon a time there was a clever little boy named Jack.
Every morning, his Mommy would give him a bowl of cereal and ask him to sign.
He didn't understand why but he was too clever not to listen.
Every time he signed, he got a little bit of a special treat.
He got some chocolates or an extra cereal bar.
Jack really loved signing and he would do it every morning.
One day, Jack found out why his Mommy wanted him to sign.
His Mommy said that signing was a way to say thank you.
Hearing this made Jack happy and he kept signing every morning with a great big smile.
Jack was so happy that he started teaching his friends how to sign.
He would show them how to make the shapes with their hands and it made his friends very happy.
From then on, Jack would make sure to sign for his Mommy every morning and to thank her for his bowl of cereal.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to eat candy.
One day, Timmy was eating a piece of candy when he felt a sharp pain in his tooth.
He cried out and his mom came running to see what was wrong.
Timmy's mom looked in his mouth and saw that there was a big hole in his tooth.
She knew they had to go to the dentist to fix it, but Timmy was scared.
He had never been to the dentist before and the thought of someone poking around in his mouth was unknown and scary.
But Timmy's mom knew what to do.
She gave him a big hug and told him that the dentist was there to help him.
She explained that the dentist would use special tools to fix his tooth and make it feel better.
Timmy felt a little bit better knowing that the dentist was going to help him, so they went to the dentist's office together.
When they got there, the dentist was very kind and gentle.
He showed Timmy all of the tools he was going to use and explained what each one did.
Timmy was still a little bit scared, but he trusted the dentist to make his tooth feel better.
And sure enough, after a few minutes, the dentist was able to fix Timmy's tooth and make the pain go away.
Timmy was so happy and relieved that he gave the dentist a big hug and thanked him for helping him.
Mama was very proud of her little girl, Mandy, who had just turned three years old.
She wanted to give her a special gift to celebrate.
Mama brought out a big, powerful drum that she had bought for Mandy.
Mandy couldn't believe it.
She was so excited to have the drum!
She couldn't wait to make some noise with it.
Mama smiled and said that she would permit Mandy to play with the drum, but only if she used it carefully.
She said that the drum was very powerful, so it must be treated with respect.
Mandy nodded her head and started to play the drum.
She loved its power and was amazed at all the fun noises it made.
Mama watched as she banged the drum, smiling and clapping along with the beat.
Mandy knew now that she too had become powerful.
She would never forget her special gift.
Tommy was a lonely boy.
He had no friends to play with at school.
He liked to draw and read, but the other kids said he was boring.
Tommy wished he had someone who liked him.
One day, he saw a new girl in his class.
Her name was Lily.
She had a big smile and a pink backpack.
Tommy wanted to talk to her, but he was shy.
He thought she would not like him either.
At recess, Tommy sat on a bench and watched Lily play with a ball.
She looked happy and fun.
Tommy felt sad.
He wished he had a ball too.
He looked in his backpack and found a crayon and a paper.
He decided to draw a ball for himself.
He was so busy drawing that he did not notice Lily coming to him.
She said, "Hi, I'm Lily.
What are you doing?" Tommy looked up and saw her.
He felt nervous.
He said, "Hi, I'm Tommy.
I'm drawing a ball." Lily smiled and said, "That's a nice ball.
Can I see it?" Tommy nodded and gave her his paper.
Lily looked at it and said, "Wow, you are good at drawing.
I like your ball.
Can I draw with you?" Tommy felt surprised and happy.
He said, "Sure, you can.
I have a crayon.
Do you want to use it?" Lily said, "Yes, please.
Thank you for sharing.
What do you want to draw?" Tommy thought for a moment and said, "How about a toe?" Lily laughed and said, "A toe?
That's funny.
Why a toe?" Tommy said, "Because toes are funny and cute.
And because I have to use the word toe in my story." Lily said, "What story?" Tommy said, "The story I'm writing for my homework.
We have to use the words supply, toe, and lonely in a story." Lily said, "That sounds hard.
Can I help you?" Tommy said, "Yes, you can.
That would be nice.
Maybe we can write a story about us." Lily said, "That sounds fun.
Let's do it." Tommy and Lily started to write their story together.
They used the crayon and the paper as their supply.
They wrote about how they met and how they became friends.
They wrote about how they drew a toe and how they laughed.
They wrote about how they were not lonely anymore.
They finished their story and read it aloud.
They smiled and hugged.
They said, "We like our story.
We like each other.
We are friends." The moral of the story is: You can find a friend if you are kind and share.
You can have fun if you are creative and curious.
You can use simple words to make a good story.
It was a sunny day and everything seemed perfect.
But then, a "disturb" came along.
Lily, who was a 3 year old girl, saw it and she was scared.
She started to cry and she felt "frightened".
Suddenly, her mother appeared and she asked: "What is wrong, Lily?" Lily replied: "I saw a "disturb" and it scared me".
Her mother asked: "A disturb?
Where?" Lily pointed to the sky, where a bird was flying.
Her mother smiled and said: "Oh, there's nothing to be "frightened" of, it's just a bird, see!
Its name is Lily, just like yours!" Lily smiled and was no longer "frightened".
She watched the bird fly until it flew away into the horizon.
Once upon a time there was a girl.
The girl was wearing a skirt.
She wanted to sharpen her pencil, but she was having trouble.
The pencil was so tough, she couldn't make it sharp.
Suddenly, an idea came to her!
She took her skirt and used it to sharpen the pencil.
She was so happy when it became sharp.
She used it to draw a picture of herself, wearing her skirt.
And she lived happily ever after.
Once upon a time, Farmer Joe had a big bucket full of food.
He had to feed all of his animals, so every day he would go out to the barn.
One day, Farmer Joe noticed that there was a troubled little bunny in the barn.
When Farmer Joe approached the bunny, it began to hop away.
Farmer Joe knew that the bunny needed help and he had just the thing - food!
He reached down, picked up his bucket, and started to feed the bunny.
The bunny was so excited that it began to nibble the food right out of Farmer Joe's hands.
It ate and ate until it was full.
The bunny was so happy and grateful, it hopped around Farmer Joe's feet joyfully.
Farmer Joe laughed and said to the bunny, “I’m glad I could help feed you.” The bunny smiled up at Farmer Joe and said, “Thank you!”
Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived in a house with her Mommy and Daddy.
One day, her Mommy and Daddy said that they would change the ceiling in their house.
The little girl didn't know what that meant, but she asked them anyway.
Mommy said "We need to put something new up on the ceiling because it will look nicer".
The little girl thought it sounded exciting!
The next day, the little girl's Daddy got to work.
He put up a strange, uncomfortable ceiling that didn't match the walls.
The little girl felt so confused and sad because she didn't understand why it had to change.
When Daddy was finished, the little girl asked why he put up the uncomfortable ceiling.
Her Daddy just said "That's just the way it has to be".
The little girl felt so sad and frustrated that she couldn't change the ceiling back.
No matter how much she asked, the ceiling stayed the same.
It made her feel uncomfortable and angry that something in her house could change without her permission.
The little girl was never able to change the ceiling back to the way it was before.
And that's why she never felt quite as comfortable in her house again.
Once upon a time, there was a beautiful plane.
It had shiny red and blue wings.
The plane was going to measure something special.
So the plane flew up high, up into the sky.
It flew all the way to the clouds.
The plane flew around and around, measuring the sky.
When the plane was finished, it flew back down to the ground.
The plane did a happy dance when it finished measuring.
It was so proud of itself that it made a big smile.
The plane was so happy that it flew around and around.
It wiggled and twirled in the sky.
The plane was so beautiful, everyone stopped to watch it.
It was so special that everybody waved and smiled.
The plane was so happy it had measured something so important.
It was so proud of itself that it flew up into the sky.
It flew up to the clouds and kept flying and flying.
The plane flew around and around, and waves goodbye to everyone it had seen.
The End.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to play outside in the sunshine and eat yummy fruits.
One day, she noticed that her mommy seemed worried about something.
Lily asked her mommy what was wrong, but her mommy said it was nothing to worry about.
Later that day, Lily went to play with her friends in the park.
They were playing hide and seek when Lily noticed a strange spirit floating around.
She felt scared and ran back to her mommy's side.
Her mommy hugged her and told her not to worry, that the spirit was just a friendly one.
The next day, Lily's mommy took her to the doctor for a check-up.
The doctor said that Lily was very healthy and that she should keep eating lots of fruits and playing outside.
Lily felt happy and relieved that she was healthy.
She also felt happy that she didn't have to worry about the friendly spirit in the park anymore.
Once upon a time, there was a jeep.
The jeep lived in the woods and was rarely seen by the people who lived near by.
One day, the jeep went off and the people who lived near by heard a loud sound from far away.
The people asked each other, "what was that loud sound?" and nobody could answer.
As days passed, the loud sound kept growing louder.
The sound grew louder and louder, until one day, a little boy said, "It sounds like something is roaring!" Each time the jeep ventured out, the roar grew louder and harsher.
Everyone was scared and confused and did not know what the loud roaring was coming from.
One day, the jeep ventured out, but this time there was something different.
This time, the roar was even more harsh and powerful - it sounded like it was coming from a huge animal!
The little boy said, "It's a lion!" and everyone was so scared.
Suddenly, the jeep came back and everyone saw it had a huge lion in it.
Everyone was so amazed, but they understood that the roaring they had heard before was the lion.
They were so glad the jeep had brought the lion back peacefully.
The end.
Mum was cooking in the kitchen.
There was a big pot of hot stew bubbling on the stove.
Mum stirred the pot with a spoon.
Jenny came in from the garden.
She had a row of carrots in her hands.
She ran to the kitchen and gave the carrots to Mum.
Mum smiled and thanked Jenny for the carrots.
Then she chopped them into tiny pieces.
She added them to the hot stew and stirred them in.
Mum tasted the stew.
It was delicious!
She smiled and said it was ready to eat.
Jenny and Mum filled two plates with the hot stew.
They sat down at the table and enjoyed their meal.
It tasted so yummy!
Once upon a time there was a chubby peach.
It was a special peach that everyone wanted to eat.
But no one knew that the peach was spoiled.
It had been left in the baking hot sun too long and it was starting to rot.
The peach was so sad.
It wanted to be enjoyed like it's brothers and sisters.
One day a little girl saw the peach.
She thought it looked delicious.
She picked it up and was about to eat it when she noticed it was starting to rot.
The little girl frowned and put the peach back down.
But then she had an idea.
She took it home and planted it.
To her surprise, it started to grow!
Soon she had a lovely chubby peach tree filled with delicious, ripe peaches.
The little girl was so happy that she'd saved the peach.
Everyone else was happy too.
They all enjoyed the nice, sweet peaches!
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy.
She loved to write.
Every day, she would write pretty pictures and fun stories.
She had a big box of colors to make her writing look nice.
Yesterday, Lucy went to the fair with her mommy and daddy.
She saw a big wheel that went round and round.
She also saw people eating yummy treats like ice cream and cotton candy.
Lucy was very happy.
At the fair, Lucy found a booth where she could write a story.
She took her colors and wrote a story about her day at the fair.
She drew the big wheel, the yummy treats, and her mommy and daddy.
When she was done, she showed her story to her parents.
They were so proud of her.
And they all lived happily ever after.
Once upon a time there was a brave girl called Amy.
She was three years old and loved to explore.
One day she took a walk in the woods near her house and stumbled across a beautiful lake.
Amy was brave and so she decided to go it alone and explore the lake.
She carefully walked around the edge, admiring the sparkly water and watching the fish swimming.
She could even see a huge frog jumping out of the water.
Suddenly, Amy stumbled and fell into the lake and all she could do was yell for help.
Fortunately, her mother was walking nearby and came to help her.
She jumped in and carried the brave little girl out of the lake and back home.
Amy was so thankful for her brave mother and by the end of the day, both of them were happily dried off and ready for a warm hug.
Once upon a time there was a hot summer day.
A little boy named Joe decided he wanted to have some fun in the sun.
He put on his shoes and ran outside to the beach.
The sand was warm and the ocean was cool.
Joe saw something in the sand.
It was a crab!
Joe was so excited.
He wanted to get closer.
So he slowly moved to the sand.
He was careful not to scare the crab away.
When he got close enough, the crab started to move.
Joe cheered.
He watched the crab enter the water and start swimming.
Joe wanted to follow so he waded in further.
The water felt so nice and it was so much fun!
Joe smiled and giggled.
Joe looked back at the shore, his mom was there smiling and waving at him.
Joe waved back and shouted, "Goodbye, crab!"
Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy.
Timmy loved to play with his toys, but he was always very clumsy.
One day, he accidentally knocked over his mommy's mirror and it broke into tiny pieces.
Timmy was very sad because he knew his mommy loved that mirror.
He tried to put it back together, but it was too broken.
Later that day, Timmy's grandpa came over to visit.
He had a shiny bald head and Timmy loved to rub it for good luck.
Grandpa saw the broken mirror and said, "Don't worry Timmy, accidents happen.
We can buy mommy a new mirror."  Timmy was so happy that his grandpa was there to help him.
They went to the store and bought a new mirror for mommy.
Timmy learned that it's okay to make mistakes, as long as you try to fix them.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside.
One day, she found a pretty flower in the garden.
She picked it up and smelled it, but her mommy told her not to eat it because it was poison.
Lily asked, "Why can't I eat it, Mommy?" Her mommy replied, "Because it's not nice for your tummy.
It can make you sick." Lily understood and said, "Okay, Mommy.
I won't eat it.
But can I keep it?" Her mommy permitted her to keep the flower, but reminded her not to eat it.
Lily was happy and thanked her mommy for being so nice.
They continued to play outside and enjoyed the rest of their day together.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
Timmy was very sad because his mommy had to go to work and he had to stay home.
He wanted to go to the park and play with his friends.
Timmy went to check the mailbox and found a letter from his grandma.
She sent him a toy car!
Timmy was so happy and forgot about his sadness.
He played with his new car for a while, but then he got bored.
Timmy went to his mommy and complained that he was bored.
His mommy said they could go to the park after she got home from work.
Timmy was happy again and waited for his mommy to come home.
When she did, they went to the park and had lots of fun.
Timmy was no longer a poor, sad boy.
Once upon a time, there was a nice and cute puppy.
His name was Boof and he was very friendly.
He liked to run and play in a big loop in the park.
One day, Boof got lost and couldn't find his way back home.
He looked very sad and lonely and didn't know what to do.
Then, he saw something shiny in the sky.
It was a rainbow!
Suddenly, he felt a little bit better and remembered his loop in the park.
With a happy bark, Boof began running and trying to find his way back home.
Luckily, Boof soon remembered the loop and quickly ran back.
He was soon in his familiar park, feeling much happier now.
He jumped and played and soon found his way back home.
Boof was so happy to be home and was glad that he had returned!
Once upon a time, there was a weird pirate.
He had a funny hat and a funny coat.
He always smiled, even when he was sad.
One day, the pirate wanted to bury something special.
He took a shovel and dug a deep hole in the ground.
Then he put something in the hole and covered it up with dirt.
He said it was a secret.
The next day, the pirate said he was going on an adventure.
He took his funny hat and coat and walked out the door.
He never came back.
People asked, "What happened to the weird pirate?" Nobody knew.
Some people said, "Maybe he buried something special and never returned."  Nobody knows the truth.
Maybe the secret is buried forever.
Once upon a time, there was a big dog called Bob.
Bob had a regular tail and he loved to play.
One day, Bob decided to explore.
He entered a forest full of adventure.
Bob had been walking for a while and then he heard a strange noise.
He stopped and listened carefully.
"Help!
Help!", the noise said.
Bob followed the voice and entered a clearing.
At the centre of the clearing was a tiny mouse.
"Oh, thank you for coming to my rescue!" the mouse said.
Bob asked the mouse what was wrong.
"Well, I was walking through the woods and got my regular tail caught in a bush," the mouse replied.
Bob smiled and said, "Don't worry, I can help you." He used his strong paws to untangle the mouse's tail from the bush.
The mouse was so thankful and the two friends said goodbye.
Bob continued his adventure, but this time he was more careful.
He knew that an unexpected tail can be quite a surprise!
Once upon a time, there was a nation of ants.
They lived in a big tree and worked all day to find food.
One day, an impatient ant wanted to go out and look for food alone.
But the other ants said no because it was dangerous.
The impatient ant didn't listen and went out alone anyway.
The impatient ant found some delicious crumbs, but then got lost on the way back to the tree.
The other ants searched for the impatient ant but couldn't find him.
They were sad and worried.
Eventually, they had to let go and accept that the impatient ant was gone forever.
From that day on, the ants always stayed together and never let impatience lead them to danger again.
Once upon a time, there was a clumsy boy named Timmy.
He liked to play with his tools, but he always dropped them.
One day, he was trying to fix his toy car, but he couldn't do it.
He felt sad and didn't know what to do.
His mom saw him and asked, "What's wrong, Timmy?" He shrugged his shoulders and said, "I can't fix my car." His mom smiled and said, "It's okay, Timmy.
Let's fix it together."  Timmy was happy and they worked on the car together.
His mom showed him how to use the tools and he learned a lot.
In the end, they fixed the car and Timmy was proud of himself.
He hugged his mom and said, "Thank you for helping me."
Once upon a time, there was a hero.
He was very brave and strong.
He saved people from danger.
One day, he went to sleep in his bed.
He had a dream that made him nervous.
He woke up in the middle of the night and couldn't go back to sleep.
The next day, the hero went to save people from a fire.
He was nervous because it was a big fire.
He went inside the building to save a little girl.
But the fire was too strong.
The hero couldn't save the little girl and he got hurt.
He was taken to the hospital, but he didn't make it.
Everyone was sad that the hero had died.
They remembered him as a brave and strong hero who saved many lives.
Once upon a time there was a young fox named Bob.
He lived in the woods and liked to explore.
One day he was feeling adventurous and decided to explore a new part of the woods.
He soon realized he was lost.
Bob started to get scared until he saw a bush.
He decided to hide behind the bush so he wouldn't get lost again.
Suddenly, he heard something and noticed a young rabbit.
His name was Ralph.
Bob was curious and wanted to meet him.
He stepped out from behind the bush and waved at Ralph.
Ralph was scared at first but then he stepped closer and they talked.
They soon became friends.
Bob and Ralph spent the day playing together around the bush.
From then on, the two were never scared to explore the woods together.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved sunshine.
Every day, she would be outside as soon as it got light, playing in the gentle sunshine.
On this day, her mum gave her something special.
It was a letter in an envelope, with her name written on it.
It was going to be mailed, so the little girl went out to put it in the mail box.
When she opened the box, she saw a bright yellow can.
She knew that this was how her letter would get delivered.
She made sure to carefully drop her letter into the mail box, and shut the door.
On the way back, the little girl thought about how wonderful it would be if the sunshine she loved could be mailed, too.
She wished it could be mailed in a bright yellow can like the one she had just put her letter in.
When she got back home, the little girl told her mum all about the letter she had sent and the bright yellow can.
She told her, “Oh mum, if only I could mail sunshine!
It's so gentle, and I love it so much!”
Ollie was a very happy 3 year old boy.
He went for a walk in the park one day and saw a big, beautiful tree.
Ollie was so excited and he ran to it with a big smile on his face.
He hugged the tree and said "I love you tree!".
As he hugged the tree, he felt like the tree was hugging him back.
He stopped and thought to himself, "This tree must love me, too!".
So Ollie hugged the tree and played around it for the entire afternoon.
But, one night, there was a big storm.
Wind blew fiercely and thunder crashed loudly.
Ollie knew his tree was in danger and he was so scared for it.
He knew he had to help, so he ran to it and held it tightly to stop it from being blown away.
But the tree was weak and the wind was too strong.
Ollie hugged the tree tight as he felt it slowly being pulled away from him.
Finally, the wind stopped and the Tree was still there!
Ollie was so relieved and hugged the tree again and said, "I love you, tree!".
He knew he could always count on the tree to stay with him no matter what and that they would always love each other.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved flowers.
She had a garden with lots of pretty flowers, but her favorite were the daisies.
One day, she saw a bulb in the dirt and she wanted to squeeze it, but her mom said not to because it was still growing.
The next day, Lily woke up early and ran to her garden.
The bulb had grown into a big flower!
But it was smelly, like stinky socks.
Lily didn't like the smell, but she didn't want to hurt the flower's feelings.
So she said, "Hello flower, you are very pretty, but you are also very smelly." The flower replied, "I know, I'm sorry.
I don't like being smelly, but it's just the way I am." Lily felt bad for the flower and wanted to help.
She asked, "Is there anything I can do to make you smell better?" The flower thought for a moment and said, "Maybe if you water me, I will smell better."  So Lily watered the flower and it worked!
The flower was no longer smelly and it made Lily very happy.
From then on, Lily always took care of her flowers and they were all very happy.
The end.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
Timmy loved to collect shells on the beach.
One day, Timmy found a big, shiny shell that he wanted to keep.
Timmy's mom saw the shell and said, "That's a very humble shell, Timmy.
It's not worth much."  Timmy didn't care.
He loved the shell and wanted to keep it.
But then he had an idea.
He realized that even humble things can be valuable to someone else.
Tim and Lily were playing with their blocks in the living room.
They liked to build towers and houses and cars with the blocks.
They had many colors and shapes of blocks to choose from.
But Tim wanted to use all the red blocks for his tower.
He did not want to share them with Lily.
He took the red blocks from Lily's pile and put them on his tower.
Lily was angry.
She wanted some red blocks too.
She tried to take them back from Tim's tower.
"Stop it, Lily!" Tim shouted.
"These are my red blocks!
Go away!" "No, Tim!" Lily shouted back.
"You are not nice!
You have to share the blocks!" They shouted and pulled and pushed the blocks.
They did not listen to each other.
They were frustrated.
Then, something happened.
Tim's tower was too tall and wobbly.
It fell down with a loud crash.
The blocks flew everywhere.
Some of them hit Tim and Lily.
They were in shock.
They felt pain and fear.
They stopped shouting and started crying.
Mom heard the noise and came to the living room.
She saw the mess and the tears.
She was not happy.
She hugged Tim and Lily and checked if they were hurt.
She said, "What happened here?
Why were you shouting and fighting?
You know you have to share and be kind to each other." Tim and Lily felt sorry.
They said, "We are sorry, Mom.
We wanted the red blocks.
We were frustrated.
We did not mean to make the tower fall." Mom said, "It's okay to want the red blocks, but you have to ask and wait for your turn.
You have many other blocks to play with.
You can make beautiful things together.
You are brother and sister.
You have to love and help each other." Tim and Lily nodded.
They said, "We love you, Mom.
We love each other.
We will share and be kind." Mom smiled.
She said, "That's good.
Now, let's clean up the blocks and start again.
What do you want to build?" Tim and Lily looked at the blocks.
They said, "We want to build a rainbow."
Once upon a time in a small town, there was a kind and humble man named Tom.
He had a big, strong house made of steel.
Tom liked to help everyone in the town.
One day, a little girl named Sue came to Tom's house.
She looked sad.
"Tom, can you help me find my lost toy?" she asked.
Tom smiled and nodded.
"Yes, Sue, I will help you." They looked everywhere for the toy.
They looked under the trees and behind the bushes.
Finally, they found the toy near the river.
Sue was very happy.
She said, "Thank you, Tom!" Tom nodded and smiled.
They went back to the town, and everyone was happy.
Jimmy was very excited.
His mummy and daddy had promised him a new roof for his bedroom.
He had asked for a purple one!
So today was the day when his new roof finally arrived.
When Jimmy saw it, his eyes lit up with happiness.
It was purple, just like he wanted it to be.
He ran outside to show it to his friends.
He was so proud of the roof - he kept pointing to it and laughing with delight.
Jimmy knew this was the best roof ever.
He was happy that his mummy and daddy had kept their promise!
Nancy was walking in the park on a very cold day.
Everywhere she looked, everything was frozen.
Everything around her was still and silent; it was like a magical world!
Suddenly, Nancy saw something moving in the distance.
She ran over to see what it was and gasped.
It was a tiny mouse, hiding under a thin piece of paper.
"Are you scared?" asked Nancy in a kind voice.
"I'm not going to hurt you!" The mouse peeked his head out from under the paper and said, "Yes, I am scared!
It's too cold outside.
I don't want to freeze!" Nancy smiled gently at the mouse.
She picked him up carefully and held him close to keep him warm.
Then, she tucked the thin paper around him so he'd stay cozy.
"Don't worry," said Nancy.
"We'll get you somewhere warm soon." The mouse smiled, relieved.
And together, the two of them set off to find a place where the mouse would be safe and warm.
John was a little boy who loved to play.
He wanted to send a letter to his friend Bob, so he asked his mom for a piece of paper.
His mom gave him a piece of paper and a pencil.
John carefully wrote a letter.
John said to his mom, "Mom, I'm done!
Look what I wrote!" His mom looked at the letter and said, "This is great, honey.
Now you need to put it in an envelope." John took an envelope and put the letter in it.
Then he noticed something strange.
He said to his mom, "Mom, what's this hairy thing in the envelope?" His mom laughed and said, "That's a stamp, honey.
You have to put it on the envelope to show you have paid for it to be mailed." John put the stamp on the envelope, waved goodbye to his mom and ran to the mailbox to mail his letter.
Once upon a time, there was a mysterious avocado.
This avocado was very special.
It could talk and walk.
One day, the avocado met a tomato.
They became good friends.
They played and laughed together every day.
After a while, the avocado and the tomato fell in love.
They decided to marry each other.
All their friends, like the apple and the carrot, came to their wedding.
Everyone was happy and excited.
The avocado and the tomato lived happily ever after.
They had many adventures together.
They were the best of friends and loved each other very much.
And the mysterious avocado was not so mysterious anymore, because it had found a true friend in the tomato.
Once there was a beautiful goose.
She was white with a yellow beak.
She loved to go around and do lots of things.
One day, she went walking in the park.
She saw a big pond, and decided to go swimming.
She spread her wings and glided across the water.
She had so much fun!
When she was done, she flew off again.
This time she went to the farm.
She saw some other geese and asked them to come join her.
They all had a great time playing together in the grass.
Suddenly, a farmer came by and saw them all.
The goose quickly flew away and the other geese ran off into the woods.
The beautiful goose had a wonderful day and she never forgot it.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
Timmy loved to play outside with his friends.
One day, Timmy and his friends found a shiny copper penny on the ground.
Timmy picked it up and held it up to the sun.
"Wow, it's so clear!" he said.
Suddenly, Timmy's mom came outside and started to yell for him to come inside for dinner.
Timmy ran over to his mom and showed her the copper penny.
"Look, Mommy!
I found a shiny penny!" he said.
His mom smiled and said, "That's great, Timmy.
Let's go inside and eat now." Timmy put the copper penny in his pocket and followed his mom inside.
He couldn't wait to show his shiny treasure to his dad when he got home from work.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She was very patient and kind.
One day, she found a big package near her house.
She was so excited to see what was inside.
But the package was too heavy for her to carry.
Lily tried to push the package to her house.
She pushed and pushed, but it was still very hard.
Then, her friend Tom came to help her.
They both pushed the package together.
It was still hard, but they did not give up.
They kept pushing and pushing until they got the package inside the house.
When they opened the package, they found many toys inside.
They were so happy to play with the new toys.
They shared the toys with their friends in the neighborhood.
Everyone had a great time playing together.
And they all learned that being patient and working together can help solve problems.
Once upon a time, there was a happy family.
Mommy, Daddy, and their little girl, Lily.
They loved to play and have fun together.
But one day, Daddy accidentally broke Mommy's favorite vase.
Mommy was sad because the vase was very special to her.
But Daddy said he would repair it, and Mommy felt better.
As they waited for the vase to be fixed, Mommy and Daddy talked about their marriage.
They said they were excited to be together and promised to always love each other.
Finally, the vase was repaired and Mommy was very happy.
The family hugged and played together, and they knew their love would always be strong.
Once upon a time, there was a big ocean.
In the ocean, there was an octopus.
He had eight arms and he loved to swim.
One day, he met a turtle who wanted to race.
The octopus was fast, but the turtle was faster.
The turtle won the race and the octopus was happy for him because he was an honest octopus.
They became friends and swam together every day.
The end.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Daisy.
Daisy loved exploring and one day she went out in the garden.
She saw a big hedge and was excited to unpack what was behind it.
She began to pull away the leaves and found a secret garden full of bright flowers and friendly insects.
She loved exploring and discovering different things.
Suddenly, Daisy heard a noise.
She saw two caterpillars fighting over a leaf.
The caterpillars were very competitive and Daisy wanted to help them.
She put the leaf in the middle of the hedge and helped the caterpillars find new leaves without fighting.
Daisy watched them crawl away, happy and content.
She smiled and went back inside, knowing that she had made two caterpillars happy.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who had a stuffed owl that she loved to play with.
One day, Lily's mommy asked her if she wanted to go for a walk in the park.
Lily was very excited and said, "Yes, mommy!
Can I bring my owl with me?" Mommy smiled and said, "Of course, Lily.
Your owl is very healthy and loves to go on walks with us." So, Lily grabbed her owl and they all went to the park.
As they walked, Lily saw a real owl sleeping on a branch.
She pointed and said, "Look mommy, an owl!
It's sleeping." Mommy said, "Yes, owls sleep during the day and are awake at night." Lily was happy to see the owl and her stuffed owl was happy too.
They all had a fun day in the park together.
Once upon a time, there was a jolly little girl named Lily.
She loved to bake with her mommy and daddy.
One day, they were making pancakes in a big pan.
Lily could hear the sizzle and pop of the pancakes cooking.
After they finished cooking, Lily's mommy and daddy went to take a nap.
Lily snuck back into the kitchen to eat more pancakes.
She climbed up on a chair and reached for the pan, but it was too heavy for her.
The pan fell on the ground with a loud crash and scared Lily.
Lily's mommy and daddy heard the noise and ran into the kitchen.
They saw that Lily was hurt and needed to go to the hospital.
They were very sad that Lily got hurt because they loved her so much.
From that day on, they made sure to always keep the pan out of reach so that Lily would be safe.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia.
Mia loved to wear pretty clothes with lots of style.
She had a favorite dress that was pink and had big, pretty flowers on it.
One day, Mia went to the park to play.
She ran and jumped and had lots of fun.
But when she went home, she saw that her dress had a big hole in it.
Mia was sad because she didn't want to lose her favorite dress.
Her mom saw the hole and said, "Don't worry, Mia.
We can fix it." They found a pretty patch and put it on the empty spot.
Now, Mia's dress was even more stylish than before.
She was so happy and wore her fixed dress with a big smile.
Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a daddy who had a daughter.
The daughter was very happy and loved to play with her toys.
One day, the mommy and daddy told the daughter that they were going to take her to the park.
The daughter was very excited and couldn't wait to go.
But then, the mommy and daddy had to delay the trip to the park because it started to rain.
The daughter was sad because she wanted to go to the park so badly.
The mommy and daddy promised that they would take her to the park as soon as the rain stopped.
After a while, the rain stopped and the mommy and daddy took the daughter to the park.
But when they got there, they saw something weird.
All the swings were missing!
The daughter was confused and didn't understand why the swings were gone.
The mommy and daddy explained that sometimes things can be weird and unexpected, but they can still have fun and play in other ways.
And so, the daughter played on the slide and had a great time at the park.
Anna likes to go to the library with her mom.
She likes to look at the books with many pictures and colors.
She likes to listen to the stories that the librarian tells.
She likes to sit on the big rug with the other kids.
One day, Anna and her mom go to the library.
Anna sees a book about animals.
She wants to read it.
She asks her mom to help her.
Her mom says, "Okay, but we have to finish soon.
We have to go home and make dinner." Anna and her mom sit on a chair and read the book.
Anna learns about lions, elephants, monkeys, and more.
She likes the sounds they make.
She tries to make them too.
She roars like a lion, trumpets like an elephant, and chatters like a monkey.
The librarian hears Anna and smiles.
She says, "You are very good at making animal sounds, Anna.
Do you want to join me for the story time?
I have a story about a zoo." Anna says, "Yes, please.
I love zoos.
Can I bring my book?" The librarian says, "Of course.
Come on, let's go to the rug." Anna and her mom follow the librarian to the rug.
Anna sits with the other kids.
She holds her book.
The librarian starts to tell the story.
She shows the pictures.
She makes the sounds.
Anna listens and watches.
She feels happy.
But then, she feels something else.
She feels dizzy.
She feels her head spin.
She feels her tummy hurt.
She feels sick.
She does not like it.
She says, "Mom, I don't feel good.
I want to go home." Her mom hears her and sees her face.
She says, "Oh, no.
You look pale.
You have a fever.
Let's go home, honey.
We can come back to the library another day." Anna nods.
She does not want to stay.
She wants to go home.
She wants to lie down.
She wants to feel better.
Her mom picks her up and hugs her.
She says, "I'm sorry, Anna.
You are sick.
You need to rest.
We will finish the book later.
I love you." Anna says, "I love you too, Mom.
Thank you for taking me to the library.
It was fun.
But I want to go home now." Her mom says, "Okay, let's go.
Bye, librarian.
Thank you for the story." The librarian says, "Bye, Anna.
Bye, Mom.
I hope you feel better soon, Anna.
Come back when you are well.
I have more stories for you." Anna and her mom leave the library.
They go home.
They finish the book.
Anna feels better.
She sleeps.
She dreams of animals.
She smiles.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
Timmy liked to climb trees.
One day, he saw a big green tree and wanted to climb it.
He said to his mom, "Mommy, can I climb that big green tree?" His mom said, "No Timmy, that tree is too high and it's bad for you to climb it." Timmy was sad but he listened to his mom.
The next day, Timmy saw a smaller tree that was also green.
He asked his mom, "Mommy, can I climb that small green tree?" His mom said, "Yes Timmy, that tree is not too high and it's safe for you to climb it." Timmy was happy and climbed the tree.

One day, a small, independent cat named Kitty went for a walk.
She loved to rock on the swings at the park.
Today, she saw a big box.
Kitty was very excited.
She thought it was a surprise just for her.
Kitty asked her friend Doggy, "What do you think is in the box?
I hope it's a surprise for me!" Doggy said, "I don't know, but you should be careful.
Surprises can be good or bad." Kitty didn't listen to Doggy.
She wanted to see the surprise.
So, she opened the box.
Inside, there were many bees!
The bees were not happy.
They flew out and started to chase Kitty and Doggy.
Kitty and Doggy ran away as fast as they could.
But the bees caught up and stung them.
It hurt a lot.
Kitty and Doggy went home, feeling very sad.
They learned that not all surprises are good, and sometimes it's better to listen to friends.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to play outside in the garden.
One day, she saw a lizard crawling on the wall.
It was green and had a long tail.
Lily asked the lizard, "What are you doing?" The lizard replied, "I am waiting for my friend to ring me.
We are going to have lunch together." Lily thought the lizard was very attractive with its shiny scales.
She said, "You look very pretty.
Can I be your friend too?" The lizard smiled and said, "Of course!
The more friends, the merrier." From that day on, Lily and the lizard became the best of friends.

And whenever the lizard's friend rang, they all had lunch together.

She was three years old and liked to read books.
One day, she saw a shiny book on the table.
She went over and opened it up.

She turned to the first page and began to read.
She was so happy to learn new things.
With each turn of the page she discovered more helpful stories, pictures and phrases.
The little girl smiled as she read the book.
She was so glad the book was helpful and she could improve her reading skills.

The girl was so proud of herself and thankful for the book that helped her learn.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah.
She had a tooth that was very rare.
One day, she decided to take a walk to relax.
As Sarah was walking outside, she saw two dogs playing together.
One was a small pup and the other was a big dog.
She asked the pupppy, “Can I play with you?” The puppy said, “No, I want to relax with my friend.” Sarah was sad and she started to cry.
She wanted to play with the puppy and her rare tooth was hurting her.
Just then, a kind older woman came over and said, “Don’t cry little one.

She followed the woman and they played together until she forgot all about her tooth.
That night, Sarah went to bed feeling happy and relaxed.

He tried again and again, but he just couldn't reach the cat.
Max felt sad, but then he had an idea.
He found a big box and put it under the tree.

The cat and Max became good friends, and they played together every day.

Tweety was very wise and always knew what to do.

Speedy agreed to help and climbed onto Tweety's back.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim.
Tim loved to play outside in the sun.
One day, the sky turned dark, and rain began to fall.
Tim felt sad and started to cry.
"Why are you crying, Tim?" asked his mom.

After a while, the rain stopped, and the sun came out.
The ground was dry, and Tim was happy.
He ran outside and played in the sun all day long.
And Tim knew that even if it rained again, the sun would always come back to make things dry and fun.
Once upon a time, there lived a girl named Sara who was very independent.
Every morning she would get dressed by herself, make her own breakfast and take a walk to the beach.
Today was no different, and soon she was standing on a sandy beach with the sun shining down on her.
She watched the waves pass by - back and forth, back and forth.
Suddenly, she heard a small voice saying, "Sara, why do you come here every day?"  Sara looked around and saw a little boy about her age.
She smiled at him and replied, "I like the beach - it's fun to watch the waves pass by." The little boy nodded and said, "Me too!
Maybe we can be friends and come here together every day?" Sara agreed with a big smile and the two of them "high-fived" to celebrate their friendship.
From that day on, they both continued to come to the beach every day to play and watch the waves pass.

They liked church because they could sing and pray and see their friends.
They also liked the big church building, with its tall tower and colorful windows.
When they got to the church, they saw a big crowd of people outside.
They heard loud noises and saw smoke and fire.
Tom and Lily were scared and held their mom and dad's hands.
"What is happening?" Tom asked.
Mom and dad looked sad and worried.
"There was a powerful storm last night, and it hit the church with lightning.
The lightning made a big hole in the tower and started a fire.
The firemen are trying to put out the fire and save the church," dad explained.
Tom and Lily felt sad too.
They loved their church and did not want it to be hurt.
They wanted to help, but they knew they were too small and the fire was too dangerous.
They prayed to God to protect the church and the firemen.
Then they saw a fireman come out of the church, carrying something in his arms.
He walked towards them and smiled.
He had a black and white cat in his arms.
It was their church cat, Mr.
Whiskers.
He was dirty and wet, but he was alive and purring.
"Look, kids, I found your cat.

Do you want to hold him?" the fireman asked.
Tom and Lily nodded and smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a man who lived all by himself.
Every day, he would look out the window of his house.

She looked very happy, but the man did not know who she was.
He asked his neighbor, but the neighbor said he did not know her.
The man began to look for her every day.
He looked in parks, in cafes, and in shops.
But he could not find her.
One day, he decided to try one last place.
He looked in the temple, and there she was!
The man was so shocked, he said hello to the woman.
She said hello back and asked him why he was looking for her.
The man said, “Because you are my wife!" The woman was very surprised.
She had been looking for her husband too!
They both were so happy, and the man knew his long search was finally over.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to row in her boat.
One day, she went out to row but she felt very sad because her boat was empty.

Her mother came over and asked, "Why are you crying, Lily?"  "My boat is empty, and I have no one to row with me," Lily said.

Once upon a time, there was a big, good dog named Max.
Max loved to run and play outside.

He was happy to be outside again, playing and having fun.
And he learned to be more careful so he wouldn't hurt his tooth again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweetie.
Tweetie loved to fly high in the sky and sing sweet songs.
One day, Tweetie saw a group of animals walking towards the forest.
The animals looked sad and scared.
Tweetie flew down to ask them what was wrong.
The animals told Tweetie that there was going to be an earthquake and they were afraid.
Tweetie didn't know what an earthquake was, but she knew it must be bad.
Tweetie thought hard and came up with a plan.
She flew to the top of the tallest tree in the forest and started to sing her sweetest song.
The other birds heard her and joined in.
Soon, all the animals in the forest were singing and dancing together.
The earthquake came, but because the animals were all together, they were safe.
Tweetie learned that including others and working together can help us overcome scary things.
And the forest was filled with the sound of happy animals singing, even on the iciest of days.
Once upon a time, four friends were at a special meeting.
They looked up in the sky and saw a beautiful point.
It was a star twinkling with a special sparkle!
The friends were fascinated and wanted to see it up close.
So they decided to go on a special adventure.
They stepped on the bus and soon they were at the star.
They stepped out, and it was all so beautiful.
The star seemed to shine brighter, and they looked at it with curiosity.
The star had a special message for them, which made them all smile.
Then they had to say goodbye.
But before they left, they decided to have a meeting again and went back home.
Tom and Lily liked to play with their toys.
They had many toys, but their favorite was the number machine.
The number machine was a big box with buttons and lights.
When they pressed the buttons, the number machine made sounds and showed numbers on the screen.
One day, Tom and Lily were playing with the number machine in their room.
They took turns to press the buttons and say the numbers out loud.
"Two, four, six, eight!" Tom said, pressing the buttons.
"Ten, twelve, fourteen, sixteen!" Lily said, pressing the buttons.
They were having fun, until they heard a knock on the door.
It was their big brother, Sam.
Sam was older and did not like to play with toys.
He liked to read books and do puzzles.
"Hey, what are you doing with that ugly machine?" Sam said, walking into the room.
"It's not ugly, it's fun!" Tom said, holding the number machine.
"It's silly, it's boring!" Sam said, grabbing the number machine.
"Give it back, it's ours!" Lily said, pulling the number machine.
Sam was stronger and pulled harder.
He took the number machine away from Tom and Lily and threw it on the floor.
The number machine broke into pieces.
The buttons and lights stopped working.
The screen went black.
Tom and Lily cried.
They loved their number machine.
They were sad and angry.
"Look what you did, you meanie!" Tom said, pointing at Sam.
"You're a bad brother, you're a bully!" Lily said, stamping her foot.
Sam did not care.
He laughed and walked away.
He did not say sorry.
Tom and Lily hugged each other.
They picked up the pieces of their number machine and put them in a box.
They hoped they could fix it someday.
They wished Sam would be nicer to them.
They wished they had a new number machine.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy.
She was always curious and playful.
One day, while she was out playing, Lucy came across a weird veil in the middle of the field.Intrigued, she wanted to take the veil but her mom came and stopped her.

Lucy was upset, she wanted to know why taking the veil was wrong.

But she always wondered what might have happened if she took it.
Once upon a time, there was a kind dog named Spot.
Spot liked to play with his friends in the park.
One day, Spot saw a little bird who was sad.
Spot asked the bird why he was sad.
The bird said he lost his family and didn't know where to go.
Spot was compassionate and wanted to help the bird.
Spot asked his friends if they knew where the bird's family was.
One friend said he saw a bird family in the tree by the pond.
Spot and the bird went to the tree, but the family was gone.
The bird was sad again.
Spot said, "Don't worry, I will support you and we will find a new family for you." They searched and searched, but no family was found.
The bird was still sad and missed his family.
Spot said, "Let's go back to the park, maybe we will find your family there tomorrow." The next day, the bird was gone.
Spot and his friends searched for the bird, but he was nowhere to be found.
Spot said, "I'm sad we couldn't find his family.
It's okay though, we will remember him and his history of being a part of our park."
Once upon a time, there was a girl called Joy.
She had a big backyard.

Every day, Joy liked to play outside.
She liked to run, swing, and explore.

Once she was done loading the wagon, Joy pulled it to the park.
She sang and laughed as she walked along the path.
She explored every corner of the park.
After a long day of exploring, Joy loaded her wagon with toys and took it back to her backyard.
She was tired, but she was very happy.
Her backyard was so safe and so much fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to play with her toys and sing songs.

Lily said, "Welcome!
You can go after me." But Sarah didn't want to wait and tried to push Lily off the slide.
Lily said, "Pause!
That's not fair.
We can take turns." Sarah agreed, and they played together on the slide, taking turns and having fun.
They even became friends and played together every day at the park.
The end.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to eat her soup with a lovely spoon that her grandma gave her.
One day, while Lily was eating her soup, her spoon disappeared.
She looked everywhere but couldn't find it.
Lily asked her mom, "Where did my spoon go?" Her mom said, "Maybe it's hiding somewhere.
Let's look for it together." They searched high and low, under the table and in the cupboards, but they couldn't find it.
Just then, Lily's little brother came in and said, "Look what I found!" He held up Lily's spoon with a big smile on his face.
Lily was so happy to have her lovely spoon back.
She hugged her brother and said, "Thank you for finding my spoon.
You're the best!" From that day on, Lily made sure to keep her spoon safe and never let it disappear again.
Lily was a little girl who liked to eat.
She liked to eat apples and bananas and cheese and bread.
She liked to eat in the kitchen with her mom and dad, or in the garden with her dog and cat.
One day, Lily saw something different under the table.
It was a big brown box with a red ribbon.
Lily was curious.
She crawled under the table and opened the box.
Inside, she found a lot of yummy things to eat.
There were cookies and candies and chocolates and cakes.
Lily was very happy.
It was her mom.
She said, "Lily, where are you?
It's time for lunch!" Lily looked at the box.
She saw a card.
It said, "Happy birthday, Lily!
Love, Grandma and Grandpa." Lily realized that the box was a gift for her.
She felt bad.
She had eaten some of her gift without asking.
Lily crawled out from under the table and said, "Mom, I'm sorry.
I found a box under the table and I ate some of it.
It was from Grandma and Grandpa.
It was for my birthday." Mom smiled and hugged Lily.
She said, "It's okay, Lily.
I'm sure Grandma and Grandpa would want you to enjoy their gift.
But you should always ask before you eat something that is not yours.
And you should save some for later.
You don't want to spoil your appetite for lunch, do you?" Lily nodded and said, "No, Mom.
I don't want to spoil my appetite.
I want to eat lunch with you and Dad and Dog and Cat.
And I want to say thank you to Grandma and Grandpa for the nice gift.
Can I call them later?" Mom said, "Of course, Lily.
You can call them later and tell them how much you liked their gift.
And how much you love them.
And how much they love you." Lily smiled and said, "I love you, Mom." Mom said, "I love you, too, Lily.
Happy birthday, my sweet girl."
The little girl was playing in the garden.
She had a delicate tube in her hand.
She kept it in her hands and twirled it around.
She smiled as the sun lit up the tube.
All of a sudden she heard loud noises coming from the sky.

"That was a plane my darling.

Lily and Tom like to play in the park.
They like to swing on the big swings.
They go up and down, up and down.
They feel happy and free.
One day, they see a goat in the park.
The goat is thin and hungry.
It has no grass to eat.
It sees the swings and thinks they are food.
It runs to the swings and starts to bite them.
"Hey, stop that!" Lily shouts.
"That is our swing, not your food!" The goat does not listen.
It keeps biting the swing.
It makes a big hole in it.
"Go away, goat!" Tom yells.
"You are ruining our fun!" The goat does not care.
It moves to the next swing and bites it too.
Lily and Tom are angry and sad.
They love their swings.
They do not want the goat to destroy them.
They look for help.
They see a man with a hat and a rope.
He is the goat's owner.
He is looking for his goat.
"Sir, sir!" Lily and Tom call.
"Your goat is here!
Your goat is eating our swings!" The man sees his goat and runs to it.
He throws the rope around its neck and pulls it away.
"I'm sorry, kids," he says.
"My goat is very naughty.
He escaped from his pen.
He is always looking for something to eat.
I will take him home and give him some hay." Lily and Tom are glad.
They hope the man will keep his goat away from the park.
They look at their swings.
They are broken and torn.
They feel sad.
They cannot swing anymore.
They decide to play something else.
They hope someone will fix their swings soon.
They still like to swing on the big swings.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She wanted to buy a long candy cane from the store.
She asked her mommy if they could go to the store to buy it.
Her mommy said yes and they went to the store.
At the store, Lily saw a big brain on a shelf.
She asked her mommy what it was.
Her mommy told her it was a toy brain for learning.
Lily thought it was cool and wanted to buy it too.
Finally, they found the candy canes.
Lily picked a long one and was so happy.
She held the candy cane in one hand and the toy brain in the other.
She couldn't wait to play and learn with her new toy brain.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very eager to play.
She asked her mom if she could invite a friend over to play.
Her mom said yes, so the little girl ran off to invite her friend.
When her friend arrived, they decided to play a game.
They each picked a bulb and had fun pretending to plant flowers in a pretend garden.
The little girl had a great time with her friend.
They played together until it was time for her friend to go.
When her friend left, the little girl was sad but still very eager for their next play date.
Anna was lonely.
She lived in a big house with no friends.
She only had her doll, Lily, to play with.
She wished she had a real friend to hug and talk to.
One day, she saw a sign in the shop window.
It said: "Buy a puppy today!
They are cute and friendly and need a home." Anna ran inside and asked the shop lady, "Can I buy a puppy, please?" The shop lady smiled and said, "Of course, dear.
They are in the back.
You can choose one you like." She led Anna to a room full of puppies.
They were all different colors and sizes.
They barked and wagged their tails.
Anna looked at them and felt her heart melt.
She wanted to take them all home.
But she knew she could only buy one.
She saw a small brown puppy in the corner.
It looked sad and scared.
It did not bark or wag its tail.
Anna felt sorry for it.
She walked over and picked it up.
It licked her face and snuggled in her arms.
"I want this one," Anna said.
"He needs a friend, like me." The shop lady nodded and said, "He is a good choice.
He is very sweet and gentle.
He just needs some love and care.
What will you name him?" Anna thought for a moment and said, "I will name him Lucky.
Because he is lucky to have me, and I am lucky to have him." The shop lady helped Anna pay for Lucky and gave her a leash and a collar.
Anna thanked her and left the shop with her new friend.
She felt happy and excited.
She could not wait to show Lucky her home and her doll.
She ran all the way to her house and opened the door.
She called out, "Mom, Dad, I have a surprise for you!" She heard her parents' voices from the living room.
They were sitting by the fireplace, reading and drinking tea.
They looked up and saw Anna and Lucky.
"Anna, what is that?" her mom asked, surprised.
"It's a puppy, Mom.
His name is Lucky.
I bought him with my allowance.
He is my friend.
Can I keep him, please?" Anna said, pleading.
Her parents looked at each other and smiled.
They saw how happy Anna was and how cute Lucky was.
They knew Anna was lonely and needed a companion.
"Of course, you can keep him, Anna," her dad said.
"He is adorable.
And he is lucky to have you, too." Anna hugged her parents and thanked them.
She introduced Lucky to Lily and put them on the couch.
She joined her parents by the fireplace and cuddled with Lucky.
She felt warm and cozy.
She was not lonely anymore.
