He made them disappear and reappear in different places.
He made the children laugh and clap.
Then, he gave Lila and Ben their toys back.
He said they could keep them or trade them again.
He said it was up to them.
Lila and Ben looked at their toys and then at each other.
They smiled and hugged.
They said they wanted to keep their own toys, but they also wanted to share them sometimes.
They said they were happy to be friends.
The clown smiled and said they had learned a good lesson.
He said it was important to be happy with what you have, but also to be generous and kind.
He said that was the best trade of all.
Once upon a time, there was a jolly little girl named Lily.
One day, Lily and her mommy went to a hotel for vacation.
Lily was so excited to explore the hotel!
She saw a big elevator and asked her mommy if they could go up.
Her mommy said, "Sure, let's push the button!" They went up to the top floor and saw a beautiful view.
Lily said, "Wow, this is amazing!"  Later that day, Lily and her mommy went to the pool.
Lily saw a boy playing with a ball and she wanted to play too.
She asked the boy, "Can I play with you?" The boy said, "Yes, let's push the ball back and forth!" They had so much fun playing together.
At the end of the day, Lily was tired but happy.
She said to her mommy, "Thank you for taking me to the hotel.
I had a great day!"
Once upon a time there was a squirrel who lived in the woods.
He was fit and strong and he loved the forest.
He was often seen scurrying around the trees and frolicking in the meadow.
One day, he saw something he had never seen before - a school.
He watched the children playing and enjoying themselves and wondered what was going on.
The next day, the squirrel found his way inside and saw the children learning.
He was curious, so he decided to stay and learn too.
The children taught him all kinds of things, like how to read and write, and he was getting smarter every day.
The squirrel soon became the best student in the entire school.
He amazed all the other children with his knowledge and they were very proud.
The squirrel had become fit and clever.
He had learned all kinds of new things and he had made a lot of friends.
He was so happy that he decided to stay in the school and learn even more.
Tim and Sam are friends.
They like to play at the beach.
They see the big blue waves and the white sand.
They want to test how brave they are.
"Let's go in the water!" Tim says.
He runs to the edge of the water and splashes his feet.
"Wait for me!" Sam says.
He follows Tim and feels the cold water on his toes.
They laugh and jump in the water.
They see the waves coming and going.
They try to catch the waves and ride them.
"Look at me!" Tim says.
He stands on a wave and balances.
He feels like a surfer.
"Wow, you are so good!" Sam says.
He claps his hands and cheers.
But then a big wave comes.
It is bigger than Tim and Sam.
It makes a loud noise and pushes them down.
"Help!" Tim says.
He is scared and wants to get out.
"Grab my hand!" Sam says.
He reaches for Tim and pulls him up.
They swim to the shore and cough out the water.
They are wet and cold and tired.
"That was a big wave!" Tim says.
He shivers and hugs Sam.
"That was too big!" Sam says.
He nods and hugs Tim back.
They are happy they are safe.
They are happy they are friends.
They decide to test something else.
"Let's build a sandcastle!" Tim says.
"Let's do it!" Sam says.
They run to the sand and start to dig and pile and decorate.
They forget about the big wave and have fun.
They are brave and happy.
One day, Jimmy wanted to organize his toys.
He thought it would be fun to have them all put away in their proper places.
He grabbed his calendar and made a plan.
He decided he could organize them each day of the week.
The first day was for sports toys.
Jimmy was so embarrassed when he saw how many toys were scattered around his room.
He quickly picked them all up and put them in their proper places.
The second day was for puzzles.
Jimmy was much less embarrassed this time.
He had a good plan and he worked quickly.
He soon had all of his puzzles put away nicely.
The third day was for blocks.
Jimmy felt so proud that he was able to organize all his toys.
His room looked very neat, and he was so pleased with his accomplishment.
Jimmy knew he had done a great job organizing.
He smiled and looked proudly at his calendar, happy with his accomplishment.
Once there was a little boy.
He loved to play in the garden.
One day he saw a tiny thing on the ground.
It was so small he almost didn't see it.
He carefully picked it up.
As he held it in his hands he saw it was shrinking.
He laughed and was excited.
He wanted to know what it was.
The little boy put the thing in his pocket and ran to his mom.
He said, "Mom, look what I have!
What is it?" She smiled and said, "That's a shrinky thing.
It's special magic that's available for you to play with." The little boy was very excited that he had found something so special.
He carefully took it out of his pocket and looked at it.
It was getting smaller and smaller.
He wanted to see what would happen if it got really small.
He watched as the shrinky thing got smaller and smaller until it was a tiny speck.
He couldn't believe his eyes!
He was fascinated by the shrinky thing and wanted to play with it every day.
So, mom put the shrinky thing in a slightly bigger container so that it wouldn't get lost.
The little boy was so excited to play with the shrinky thing every day.
He loved watching it get smaller and smaller.
He was never bored with this special thing that was available for him!
Anna likes to play with her doll.
She has a pink comb for her doll's hair.
She combs her doll's hair every day.
She makes her doll look pretty.
One day, Anna's brother Tom comes into her room.
He is naughty.
He sees the comb on the floor.
He picks it up and runs away.
He laughs and says, "This is my comb now!" Anna is angry.
She runs after Tom.
She says, "Give me back my comb!
It is not yours!
It is for my doll!" Tom does not listen.
He shakes the comb in the air.
He says, "No, it is mine!
I like to shake it!
It makes a funny noise!" Anna tries to catch Tom.
She jumps and reaches for the comb.
But Tom is too fast.
He runs around the room.
He shakes the comb harder and harder.
He says, "Ha ha ha!
You can't get it!" Anna is sad.
She cries.
She says, "Please, Tom, give me back my comb!
You are hurting it!
It is not a toy!
It is for my doll's hair!" Tom stops.
He sees Anna's tears.
He feels sorry.
He says, "I'm sorry, Anna.
I was just playing.
Here is your comb.
I won't shake it anymore." He gives the comb back to Anna.
Anna smiles.
She says, "Thank you, Tom.
You are a good brother.
I love you." She hugs Tom.
She takes the comb and goes back to her doll.
She combs her doll's hair gently.
She says, "Don't worry, doll.
Your hair is still pretty.
I will take care of you."
Maggie the girl went out to the garden with her dad.
She was so excited because there were so many strawberries.
Her dad told her, "Maggie, take your basket and mark the large strawberries".
Maggie was delighted as she had never seen so many strawberries before.
She started running around the garden and happily placed large strawberries in her basket.
Suddenly, Maggie heard her dad say, "Look, there is an even bigger strawberry than the ones you are marking.
Would you like to pick it up?"  Maggie ran to the spot her dad called out from, and lo and behold, there was an extra-large strawberry waiting for her!
She carefully picked it up, and put it into her basket, as she started to fill it up with all the large, juicy strawberries.
Afterwards, Maggie said to her dad, "I marked so many strawberries, Dad!" Her dad smiled and said, "You sure did, sweetheart.
Let's go home to have some strawberry pies!" Maggie was thrilled and couldn't have been happier.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She was very excited to go to her grandma's house.
She packed her bag and went to the car with her mom and dad.
They drove for a long time and finally arrived at grandma's house.
When they got inside, Lily saw a big cupboard in the kitchen.
She asked her grandma, "What's in the cupboard?" Her grandma replied, "That's where I keep all my dishes and cups." Lily was grateful when her grandma gave her a cup to drink from.
She said, "Thank you, grandma!
This cup is so pretty." They all sat down and had some cookies and milk.
Lily was very happy to be with her family and couldn't wait to come back again.
Anna liked to play dress-up with her mom's clothes.
She found a big skirt in the closet and put it on.
It was very long and dragged on the floor.
She wanted to make it shorter, like her mom's skirts.
She asked her brother Ben to help her.
Ben had a ruler and a pencil.
He said he could measure the skirt and mark where to cut it.
Anna stood still while Ben measured the skirt.
He put the ruler on her leg and drew a line with the pencil.
"Here, this is how short you want it," he said.
"Thank you, Ben," Anna said.
She took the scissors and cut along the line.
She threw away the extra fabric and looked at her new skirt.
It was warm and soft and just the right size.
She twirled around and smiled.
She ran to show her mom her new skirt.
Mom was in the kitchen, making cookies.
She saw Anna and hugged her.
"What a lovely skirt, Anna!
Did you make it yourself?" she asked.
"Yes, Mom, I did.
Ben helped me measure it," Anna said proudly.
Mom praised Anna and Ben for being creative and careful.
She gave them each a cookie and a kiss.
Anna and Ben were happy.
They liked to play dress-up and eat cookies.
They loved their mom and each other.
Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a gloomy day.
The sky was gray, and the trees were sad.
In this town, there was a little boy named Tim.
Tim liked to play with blocks.
He made many patterns with his blocks.
One day, he saw that his patterns were always the same.
Tim wanted to change them.
He asked his mom, "How can I change my patterns?" His mom said, "You can try new things and learn from others." So Tim went to his friend, Lily.
Lily showed him new ways to make patterns with the blocks.
They made patterns with colors, shapes, and sizes.
Tim was happy because he learned to change his patterns.
From that day on, Tim and Lily played together and shared their ideas.
They made many new patterns with their blocks.
The town became less gloomy because the children were happy and learning from each other.
The moral of the story is that when we try new things and learn from others, we can change and grow.
Tom and Mia are friends.
They like to play in the park.
One day, they see a big pile of stuff near the slide.
They go to look at it.
"Wow, what is this stuff?" Tom asks.
He picks up a stick and pokes the stuff.
"Yuck, it is smelly!" Mia says.
She covers her nose with her hand.
"It smells like old socks and rotten eggs!" The stuff is brown and green and has flies around it.
It is garbage.
Someone threw it away and did not put it in the bin.
"Who did this?" Tom wonders.
He is angry.
"This is bad.
It makes the park dirty and smelly.
And it can hurt the animals and the plants." Mia nods.
She is sad.
She loves the park and the animals and the plants.
She does not like garbage.
"Let's tell someone," she says.
She takes Tom's hand and they run to find a grown-up.
They see a park ranger near the swings.
They wave to him and tell him about the stuff.
The park ranger is glad that Tom and Mia told him.
He thanks them and says he will clean up the stuff.
He also says he will put up a sign to remind people to put their garbage in the bin.
Tom and Mia are happy.
They helped the park and the ranger.
They go back to play on the slide.
They do not see the stuff anymore.
They only see the sun and the sky and the flowers.
They smile and laugh.
They have fun.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
Timmy loved to ride his bike, but he never wore his helmet.
His mom always told him to wear it, but he thought it was too tough to wear.
One day, Timmy decided to go for a ride without his helmet.
He was having so much fun that he didn't notice a big rock in his path.
He hit the rock and fell off his bike.
He hurt his head really badly and had to go to the hospital.
After that, Timmy always wore his helmet when he rode his bike.
He learned that it's important to follow safety rules, even if they seem tough.
The moral of the story is that safety should always come first, even if it's not fun or easy.
Once upon a time, there was a sweet little girl called Mary.
Mary was so grateful for the love her family had for her.
Mary's mom and dad loved her with all their hearts.
They would always tell her that no matter what happened, they would always love her.
Mary knew this love was true.
She always felt it in the warmth of their hugs, and the kindness in the way they spoke to her.
She was very thankful to have them in her life.
Mary wanted to share her love with them and so everyday she would do something to make them happy - like cooking them breakfast or picking flowers for the house.
Her mom and dad were so proud of all the loving things she did.
Mary knew from experience that love can make the world a better place.
She knew that love was the most special feeling ever and it was always worth treasuring.
Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a big skeleton.
The skeleton was very icy and cold.
He liked to turn around and dance all day.
All the kids in the town were scared of him because he was so big and icy.
One day, a little girl named Lily went up to the skeleton and said, "Hi, Mr.
Skeleton!
Why are you so icy and cold?" The skeleton looked at her and said, "I don't know, little girl.
I have always been like this." Lily thought for a moment and said, "Do you want to be warm and happy like me?" The skeleton nodded his head.
So, Lily held the skeleton's hand and they danced together.
As they danced, the skeleton started to feel warm and happy.
He was not icy anymore.
The other kids saw this and they all joined in the dance.
From that day on, the big skeleton was not icy and cold anymore.
He was warm and happy because he had friends to dance with.
The kids in the town were not scared of him anymore.
They all learned that even someone who looks scary can be a good friend if you give them a chance.
There was a boy named Brad who was three years old.
Brad was curious about the world and he wanted to learn all he could.
One day, his mother took him to an igloo.
It was very cold outside, but he was very excited!
They went inside the igloo and Brad saw that it was very interesting.
There was a lot to learn here.
His mom showed him how the walls of the igloo were built with blocks of ice.
He also learned about how igloos were used by people for shelter in the ancient past.
Brad had a wonderful time learning about the igloo.
His mind was filled with exciting, new knowledge.
He knew he would remember this interesting experience for a long time.
Once upon a time, there was a girl named Daisy.
One day, Daisy was hungry so she decided to eat some honey.
She opened the jar and found that it was full of sweet, yellow honey.
She was very excited and began licking the honey off the spoon.
Suddenly, she noticed something that made her tremble.
It was a shiny razor blade in the honey!
"Mommy," she said in a trembling voice, "Look what I found in the honey!" Her mommy quickly came to investigate.
She carefully looked at the razor blade and told Daisy, "Don't worry, I'll take care of it."  She then took the razor blade away and Daisy felt much better.
The next day, Daisy had a big smile on her face.
She knew that if she always listened to her mommy, she would always be safe.
The end.
Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max.
Max loved to play in the park and chase after balls.
One day, Max saw a big dog with a shiny chain around his neck.
Max was curious and went to say hello.
The big dog nodded his head and Max barked happily.
Max loved playing with the big dog, but he also loved being independent.
He didn't want to be tied up with a chain like the big dog.
So, Max ran around the park and played with his ball, feeling free and happy.
The big dog watched Max play and nodded his head in approval.
Max was happy to have a new friend, but he was even happier to be independent and free.
Once upon a time, there was a fearful hippo.
He was feeling scared and lonely, so he went for a long walk.
His long legs carried him around the meadow, across the river and up the hill.
The hippo was very tired by the time he reached the top of the hill, so he lay down in the warm sunshine and rested.
He felt the gentle breeze cool his skin as he rested, and soon his fear and loneliness disappeared.
The hippo enjoyed resting in the sunshine, so he did it often.
After a while he even made some friends who liked to rest with him.
They would spend all day, every day, resting together on the hill.
And that is the story of the fearful hippo.
He found a place to safely rest and eventually made some friends.
Lila and Ben are playing with clay in the garden.
They make balls and snakes and stars with the clay.
They are happy and laugh a lot.
"Look, I made a big ball!" Lila says, holding up her clay ball.
"Can you catch it?" She throws the ball to Ben, who tries to catch it with his hands.
But the ball is too big and heavy, and it falls on the ground.
It breaks into pieces and makes a mess.
"Oh no, your ball is broken!" Ben says, feeling sorry for Lila.
"I'm sorry, I couldn't catch it." Lila is sad and looks at her broken ball.
She starts to cry.
"Don't cry, Lila.
We can make another ball.
Or something else.
What do you want to make?" Ben says, trying to cheer her up.
Lila thinks for a moment.
She wipes her tears and smiles.
"I want to make a hat.
A clay hat.
For you!" She says, picking up some clay.
"A hat?
For me?
Thank you, Lila.
That's very nice of you." Ben says, feeling happy again.
Lila makes a hat with the clay.
She shapes it like a cone and puts some flowers on it.
She gives it to Ben.
"Here, try it on.
Does it fit?" She says, hoping he likes it.
Ben puts the hat on his head.
It is a bit big and wobbly, but he doesn't mind.
He thinks it is a beautiful hat.
"It fits!
It fits perfectly!
Thank you, Lila.
You are a great friend." He says, hugging her.
They both laugh and play with their clay hats.
They are happy and have fun.
Once there was a person who was very foolish.
They thought they could do whatever they wanted without any consequences.
One day, the foolish person decided to cover a hole in a boat with their hands.
It seemed like it would be an easy job, but before long the hole was full of water and the boat started to sink!
The person quickly realised their mistake and started to cry.
They had been so foolish to try and cover the hole with their hands instead of getting something to plug the hole properly.
The person decided to never be so foolish again and started to think more before acting.
This story has a moral to it: it’s not wise to be too quick and careless when making decisions.
It’s important to take time and think things through before taking action.
Once upon a time, there was a farmer who had a big field.
In the field, there was some hay.
The hay was yellow and smelled nice.
One day, the farmer saw a bird sitting on the hay.
The bird was fragile and looked scared.
The farmer tried to catch the bird, but it flew away.
The farmer just shrugged and went back to work.
The end.
Sam was walking down the street, looking up at the church.
He was so excited; he couldn't wait to go inside.
Suddenly, he tripped and fell on something rough.
He looked down - it was a jump rope!
Sam realized this must be a sign - someone had left the jump rope here for him.
He quickly grabbed it and jumped up and down the street.
Every jump made him even more excited for what he was about to do.
The church doors opened, and he walked inside.
He was welcomed by the warm sunshine that shone through the windows.
After a few minutes of awe-inspiring beauty, Sam looked down.
There it was again - the jump rope!
He couldn't believe it!
Suddenly, he realized the jump rope was meant to be a sign - it had been meant to lead him to this church.
With this in mind, Sam knew that he had been preparing for this moment his whole life, and he couldn't wait to find out what was in store for him.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She was very scared of the dark and had a nightmare every night.
One day, she told her mom about her nightmare.
"I had a bad dream last night, Mommy," said Lily.
"What did you dream about, sweetie?" asked her mom.
"I dreamt that a big monster came out of my closet and scared me," replied Lily.
"Oh no, that sounds scary," said her mom.
"But don't worry, I'll check your closet before you go to bed tonight.
And if you still feel weak, you can always come sleep with me and Daddy." "Thank you, Mommy," said Lily.
"Please don't forget to check my closet." "I won't forget," promised her mom.
"Now let's go play with your toys and forget about that scary nightmare."
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy.
She was very fond of playing.
One day, she and her Mama were walking together in the city.
Amy said to her Mama, "I see a shop!" Mama pointed around and said, "Yes, that's a shop.
Do you want to take a closer look?" Amy said, "Yes please!" When they got to the shop, it was very filthy.
Amy was surprised to see how dirty it was.
Mama said, "Look at all the dirt!
We should not go in there.
Let's go somewhere else." Amy said, "Ok, Mama." So Amy and her Mama went to a different shop instead.
It was much cleaner and Amy was happy.
The end.
Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily.
She loved to bake with her mommy.
One day, they decided to make a cake.
Lily helped her mommy pour the flour and sugar into the bowl.
She also cracked the eggs and mixed everything together.
After they finished baking the cake, they wanted to eat it.
But mommy said they couldn't until daddy came home.
Daddy had the license to cut the cake.
So they waited patiently.
When daddy finally came home, he cut the cake into slices.
Lily took a bite of her slice and made a funny face.
It was bitter!
Mommy and daddy tasted it too and agreed.
They forgot to put sugar in the cake!
But they still ate it and laughed about their mistake.
Once upon a time, there was a box of crayons.
The crayons were very organized.
They were all in a row, like a rainbow.
The crayons liked to color pictures for kids.
They were happy when kids used them.
One day, a new crayon came to the box.
The new crayon did not have a name.
The other crayons wanted to help the new crayon.
They all thought of a name for the new crayon.
They picked a name that was fun and happy.
The new crayon liked the name.
The name was "Sunshine".
Sunshine was a pretty yellow color.
Now, Sunshine could color pictures with the other crayons.
They all had fun together.
And the kids loved the pictures they made.
Once upon a time, there was a family of four, Mom, Dad and their two young boys.
Mom and Dad had a plan that they wanted to try out with their boys.
They asked the boys to be obedient and to not ask many questions.
The boys agreed, so Mom and Dad gave them each a lime.
The boys wondered what the plan was but they waited patiently, confident that Mom and Dad would tell them soon.
The boys happily went outside to play with their limes while they waited.
A few days later, Mom and Dad called the boys in and gave them each a tall glass of limeade.
The boys laughed together as they took a sip.
The tart and sweet taste of the limeade was delicious.
They knew the plan now!
Mom and Dad had been preparing the limes for a special treat.
The boys thanked Mom and Dad for the delicious limeade and for teaching them to be obedient.
They enjoyed the limeade even more knowing that it was part of a special plan!
Once upon a time, there was a man.
He wanted to go for a swim, but when he looked, the pool seemed empty.
He was very sad.
He looked around, and saw that the park was empty too.
He decided to keep looking and found a pond.
He was happy when he saw that the pond was not empty.
He took off his shoes, and put his toes in the water.
The water was really cold, but it seemed nice.
He started to swim around in the pond.
He swam around and around, and had lots of fun.
After a while, he noticed it was getting dark, so he got out of the pond and put his shoes back on.
He was still happy that he had been able to swim in the pond.
He waved goodbye and started to walk home.
He was glad that he had found the pond.
The End.
Once upon a time there was a dad who was planning a surprise.
He dressed up in his best boots, grabbed his tidy bag, and went outside.
He drove to the park and sat down on a bench.
Then he saw a little girl with her mum, who had brought a present.
Dad planned to give the present to the little girl.
He opened the tidy bag and took out a shiny red boot.
The little girl's eyes lit up with excitement when she saw it!
She put on the boot and ran around the park.
Everyone laughed as they watched her twirling and dancing.
Then, dad gave her a big hug and they went home.
The little girl wore her shiny new boots every day, and whenever she put them on, she remembered the surprise her dad had planned for her.
Once upon a time, there was a cute little bunny named Benny.
Benny loved to eat jelly, especially strawberry jelly.
One day, Benny went to the store to buy some jelly.
He met a little girl named Lily who also loved jelly.
"Hi, Benny!
What are you doing here?" asked Lily.
"I'm buying jelly.
Do you want to come with me?" replied Benny.
Lily happily followed Benny to the jelly section.
They picked out their favorite flavors and went to pay.
Suddenly, a big mean dog came running into the store and scared Benny and Lily.
They both started to weep and cry.
The dog ran straight to Benny and ate all of his jelly.
Benny was very sad and Lily was scared.
They ran out of the store as fast as they could.
Benny never wanted to go back to that store again.
Once upon a time there was a skeleton who had done something bad.
Nobody wanted to be his friend anymore, and he felt so sad.
He wanted to make things right, so he asked everyone to forgive him.
The skeleton apologized with a sweet smile.
He promised he would never do it again, and he wished that everyone would give him another chance.
At first everyone was scared and didn't know what to do.
But then one little boy said that he would forgive the skeleton.
That made the skeleton so happy, and soon all the other children followed.
The skeleton was thrilled and everyone was friends again.
They all laughed, danced and had a wonderful time together.
The skeleton was so thankful for the little boy's kindness and generosity.
He realized that forgiveness can be sweet, just like honey!
Once upon a time, there was a small boy called Kevin.
He was very happy, and loved to play with his toys.
One day, while playing outside, he saw a tire in the garden.
He said to himself, "I'm going to win this tire!" It looked so fun and exciting.
He ran as fast as he could and grabbed the tire.
He was so happy to have won it!
But, when he held the tire, he realised it was very fragile.
He was a bit scared that it might break.
Kevin then heard his mum's voice coming from the kitchen, "Be careful with that tire!
It looks quite fragile." Kevin was glad to hear his mum's voice and decided to be extra careful with the tire.
He continued to play with it, but he was very careful not to break it.
He had won the tire and wanted to keep it safe.
And happily, he did keep it safe!
Anna and Ben are friends.
They like to play with blocks and cars.
They have a task to do.
They have to clean up their toys before lunch.
Anna wants to play with the red car.
Ben wants to play with the red car too.
They both reach for the car.
"Mine!" Anna says.
"No, mine!" Ben says.
They pull the car from each other.
The car breaks.
They both cry.
Mom comes and sees the broken car.
She is sad.
"Anna, Ben, what happened?" Mom asks.
"We both wanted the red car.
We did not yield.
We broke the car." Anna says.
"I'm sorry, Mom.
We were not kind.
We did not share." Ben says.
Mom hugs them.
"It's okay, Anna, Ben.
I'm glad you are sorry.
You can fix the car together.
Then you can finish your task and clean up your toys.
Then we can have lunch." Mom says.
Anna and Ben nod.
They say sorry to each other.
They fix the car.
They share the car.
They clean up their toys.
They are happy.
They have lunch with Mom.
They are kind friends.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
Timmy loved to play outside and explore.
One day, he went on a hike with his family.
They climbed up a big mountain.
Timmy was so happy and excited to see everything from up high.
As they walked, Timmy noticed something strange.
He saw a little bird that looked upset.
It was sitting on a tree branch all alone.
Timmy wanted to help the bird, so he observed it for a while.
He saw that the bird's wing was hurt.
It couldn't fly anymore.
Timmy felt sad for the bird.
He knew he had to do something to help.
So, he told his family about the bird and they called a wildlife rescue team.
The team came and took care of the bird.
Timmy was happy that he could help the upset bird.
He felt proud of himself for observing and noticing when something was wrong.
Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Jane.
She had a pet rabbit named Peter.
Every day, Jane would mail Peter some delicious carrots and lettuce, so he could stay healthy.
One day, Jane mailed some meat to Peter.
She thought it would be harmless, but instead the meat made Peter very sick.
Peter was so sick that he could barely move.
Jane was very worried, so she decided to take Peter to the vet.
When they got to the vet, the doctor said, "What did you mail your rabbit?" Jane sheepishly replied, "I mailed him some meat." The vet smiled and said, "Meat isn't harmless for rabbits.
You have to be careful what you feed them.
But don't worry, I can treat Peter and get him back to health." Jane was so relieved.
And soon enough, Peter was back to his energetic rabbit self.
Jane happily mailed Peter carrots and lettuce from then on.
One day, in a backyard, there was an unknown thing.
The thing made a loud noise when it was cut.
Suddenly, the unknown thing became two pieces!
They were so small, like toys.
The little girl who lived in the backyard was very excited.
She started to play with the two pieces.
She used them to make another unknown thing.
But it was not as loud as the first one.
The little girl smiled and ran back into her house, happy to have cut the unknown thing.
Max had a rubber duck.
He loved playing with it in the bath.
He would squirt water at it, and make it fit into the biggest bubbles.
Today, Max wanted to take his duck outside.
He quickly put on his shoes, grabbed his duck and walked outside.
Max was in the garden, and he saw a pond.
He wanted to put his duck in the water.
He slowly placed it in the water, and watched it float away.
Max felt thirsty.
He walked to the kitchen and found a glass.
He drank all of the water in the glass.
Max was now full.
He ran back to the pond and saw that his rubber duck was still there, floating happily.
He grabbed it and brought it back into the bath.
Max was very happy.
He was going to play in the bath all day, because it was the perfect place to be fit and have fun.
Once upon a time, there were two kids named Mia and Jack.
Mia had short, curly hair and Jack was bald for his age.
They were best friends and did a lot of fun things together.
One day, Mia and Jack found an old, bald model.
It was locked, so they wanted to unlock it.
Jack reached into his pocket and pulled out an old rusty key that he had found earlier.
He looked at Mia and said, “Let’s see if this key fits!” Mia took the key and put it in the lock.
It fit perfectly!
She turned the key and the model unlocked.
They both looked inside and found a bunch of surprise toys!
The kids were so excited and began playing with the toys.
They had so much fun and enjoyed their special day together.
The End
Once there lived a girl named Hope.
She was only three years old, but she was so brave.
She had a skull that she always carried around.
Every day she would go outside and explore the world, and she always looked so glad.
One day, Hope went to the park and saw a big tree.
She took her skull and climbed the tree.
Up high in the tree, she could see the whole town.
She was so happy, she wanted to stay there forever.

I will always remember what a generous and kind heart you have.”  The moral of the story is that when we are eager and generous with our gifts, we can make somebody else very happy.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Rachel who loved to spend time outdoors.
She noticed something white coming from the house of her neighbor, who lived across the street.
She asked curiously, "What is that white stuff coming from your house?" The neighbor replied, "It's snow!" Rachel had never seen snow before and she was so excited.
Rachel decided to grab a handful of the white snow and take it home with her.
When she got home, she couldn't wait to show it to her mom.
But as she got close to her mom, she began to sneeze.
Her mom knew that the snow was too cold for Rachel and quickly said, "Rachel, don't touch the snow from our neighbor's house.
It's too cold for you." Rachel heeded her mom's advice and went outside to play in the sunshine.
Rachel learned from this experience that we should be considerate towards our neighbors.
We should respect boundaries and not take what does not belong to us.
No matter how exciting something is, it is important to always be mindful of the feelings of those around us.
Lily and Tom were happy.
They wanted to have a picnic in the park.
They packed some bread, cheese, fruit and juice in a large basket.
They took a blanket and a ball too.
They walked to the park with their mom.
They found a nice spot under a big tree.
They spread the blanket on the grass and put the basket on it.
They were ready to start their picnic.
"Can I have some juice, please?" Lily asked.
"Sure, here you go," mom said and gave her a cup.
"Can I have some cheese, please?" Tom asked.
"Sure, here you go," mom said and gave him a slice.
They ate and drank and talked.
They were having fun.
Then they heard a loud roar.
They looked up and saw a large bear.
The bear was hungry.
It smelled the food.
It ran towards them.
"Run, run, run!" mom shouted.
They grabbed the blanket and the ball and ran.
But the basket was too heavy.
They had to leave it behind.
The bear reached the basket.
It opened it and ate everything.
It was happy.
Lily, Tom and mom were sad.
They had no picnic.
They had no food.
They had to go home.
They were scared of the bear.
They did not have fun.
Once upon a time there was a little girl called Bella who wanted to ask a question.
She asked her mom: "What is an olive?".
Mom looked at her and said "It is a fruit"!.
Bella said, "I would like to have an olive".
So mom took her to the store and found an olive for Bella.
Bella held the olive and asked "What do I do with it?".
Mom answered: "You can eat it".
So Bella did and said it tasted nice.
Bella wanted to ask more questions, so she asked her mom if she could get more olives.
Her mom said "Yes, but they aren't very reliable fruits".
Bella asked "What do you mean?".
Mom answered "Olives don't always taste the same, so you should be careful when you eat them.
However, they are delicious and are a great snack".
Bella was so happy to find out about olives and she liked them a lot.
She decided to always be reliable when eating olives, so that she could enjoy their taste.
Terry was a tall boy.
He had a special jacket.
It was made for stretching.
Every morning, Terry put on his special jacket and started stretching.
He would stretch his arms above his head, reach down to his toes, and twist from side to side.
He loved stretching in his favorite jacket.
One day, Terry saw his friend Jack stretching too.
He asked Jack, "Why are you stretching?" Jack said, "I'm stretching because it keeps me healthy!" Terry thought that was a great idea and decided to stretch more with his special jacket.
As Terry stretched, he felt his body getting stronger and taller.
He kept stretching each morning and saw that he was growing taller and taller each day.
He even convinced his friends to join him and stretch together.
Terry became very good at stretching and was proud of his special jacket.
He kept stretching his arms, reaching his toes, and twisting from side to side.
Terry always remembered one thing: stretching in his special jacket made him feel strong, healthy, and most of all, tall!
Once upon a time there was a little boy.
He saw a barber and wanted to see what the barber was doing.
The barber had thick, dry hair and he was cutting it.
The little boy admired him.
The barber stopped cutting the man's hair and smiled at the little boy.
The barber asked the boy if he wanted to have a turn with the scissors.
The little boy was very excited.
He held out his hand, careful not to touch the scissors.
The barber put the scissors in the boy's hand and the little boy was amazed.
He began to cut his own hair with the scissors.
The barber stood there and admired the little boy's courage.
The little boy was very proud of what he had done.
When he finished, he looked at the barber with a big smile.
The barber said, "You did a great job.
You did a better job than some adults!"  The little boy was very happy.
He thanked the barber and he knew that he had gained a special skill.
From then on, he knew he had the power to take care of his own hair.
Mama was very busy with her work today and she had a deadline to meet, so she told her daughter to be very patient.
Her daughter had never been asked to do such a difficult thing before--be patient and not interrupt right away.
But eventually, the little girl did as she was told and waited and waited.
Finally, the time came and Mama got her paycheck.
The little girl saw it when Mama was counting and she noticed a penny!
She was so excited that she shouted "Can I have it, Mama?
Can I use it?".
But Mama replied: "No, sweetheart.
I'm sorry.
This penny is too delicate for us to play with.
You'll just have to delay having a penny for a little while." The little girl was a bit sad about the delay, but she nodded in understanding.
Mama told her that one day she would get a penny of her own--a nice shiny new one!
This made the little girl very happy and she couldn't wait for Mama to give her the coin.
Days passed, and one day the little girl's birthday arrived.
Mama gave her a special gift: a shiny new penny just for her!
Now the little girl could play with it and treasure it forever.
It was a delayed pleasure, but now the little girl knows that she finally has her penny!
Once upon a time, there was a famous beetle.
He was so famous that everyone wanted to meet him.
One day, the beetle was sleeping in the grass, when he suddenly woke up!
He didn't know why he had woken up, but he soon found out.
A kind boy had come to see him.
The boy said, "Hello, famous beetle!
I heard you were the best beetle around and I wanted to see you for myself." The beetle and the boy became the best of friends.
They played and laughed until the sun went down.
The beetle was so happy that he hadn't stayed asleep.
He was glad he woke up to meet his new friend.
Once upon a time, there was a bouncy kitten called Lucy who lived with her mom and dad in a cozy house.
Every day, Lucy would go out and wander in the sunshine, looking for fun.
One day, when she was out exploring, she spotted something glinting in the grass.
She went over to take a look and saw that it was a hoop!
It was made of shiny metal and it made Lucy feel so excited.
She picked up the hoop and started to play with it, rolling it around and hopping over it too.
She wiggled and jiggled and had the best time ever.
Nearby, her mom was watching and called out, "Lucy, come here!
What's that you have there?" Lucy proudly held up the hoop and announced, "Look!
I found this hoop and it's so playful!" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes it is.
You can keep it and play with it whenever you want." After that, Lucy was always seen wandering with her hoop, playing and having lots of fun.
The end.
Once upon a time, there was a kind father who had a daughter.
Her name was Lily.
One day, the father gave Lily a shiny new toy.
Lily loved her toy very much and played with it all day long.
But one day, Lily forgot to put her toy away and left it outside.
That night, it rained very hard and the toy got wet.
The next day, the toy was broken and Lily was very sad.
The father said to Lily, "Remember to always lock your toys away when you're done playing with them.
That way they will stay safe and last a long time." From that day on, Lily always locked her toys away and took good care of them.
And she never forgot the lesson her father taught her.
Once upon a time, there was a new red ball.
The red ball wanted to go on an adventure.
It rolled out of the house and down the street.
The red ball saw a big tree, a small dog, and a tall man.
The red ball was very happy.
One day, the red ball met a blue square.
The blue square wanted to go on an adventure too.
They went to a fun park.
They played on the slide, the swing, and the see-saw.
The red ball and the blue square had a great time together.
After playing, the red ball and the blue square were tired.
They went back to the red ball's house.
The red ball showed the blue square a big cupboard.
Inside the cupboard, there were many toys.
They played with the toys until it was time to sleep.
The red ball and the blue square became best friends.
Once upon a time, there was a brave little boy who lived in a small village.
Everyone in the village called him brave because he was always so kind to everyone.
One day, he heard a strange noise coming from outside his home.
He went to investigate and saw a pistol lying on the ground.
He picked it up and showed it to the village chief.
"What is this?" he asked the chief.
The chief was amazed that he knew what it was.
He said "It looks like a pistol, why did you find it?" The brave little boy said "I heard a loud noise and I was curious." The chief was impressed and said "You must have a gift for finding things!
But it's dangerous, so we need to get rid of it." The brave little boy said "But I can fix it!
I'm fit and I can heal it." The chief was surprised and said "Maybe you can!
Let's give it a try." The brave little boy carefully took the pistol apart and started to mend the broken parts.
Once he was finished, the pistol looked like new.
The village chief clapped and said "Well done!
You not only found the strange noise, but you also managed to heal it.
You really are a brave little boy!" The brave little boy smiled and said "Thank you!" He took the pistol back to his home, where it stayed for many years.
Once upon a time, there was a pretty little girl named Lily.
She loved to play with her toys and draw pretty pictures.
One day, her parent told her not to pour water from the big jug in the kitchen.
But Lily didn't listen and poured the water all over the floor.
Her parent was very angry and scolded her.
Lily felt sad and promised to never pour water again.
But one day, when her parent was not looking, Lily poured water again.
This time, she slipped on the wet floor and hurt herself badly.
The moral of the story is that we should always listen to our parents and not do things we are told not to do, or else we might get hurt.
Once upon a time there was a charming little girl named Sarah.
She was only three years old and loved to explore around her house.
One day, Sarah decided to open the refrigerator, which had so many interesting things inside.
When she opened it, suddenly a friendly voice said, “Hello Sarah, what can I do for you?” Sarah was so surprised she stepped back and looked around.
“Who said that?” Sarah said.
What would you like?”  Sarah thought for a minute and said, “Can I have a juice please?” So, the refrigerator gave her a tasty juice and she thanked it.
Sarah and the refrigerator had a lovely conversation and she realized that the refrigerator was really charming.
From that day onward, Sarah and her refrigerator talked to each other whenever she opened the refrigerator door.
Tom and Lily wanted to build a castle with their blocks.
They had many blocks of different colors and shapes.
They put some blocks on the floor and stacked them up.
They made walls and towers and a gate.
"Look at our castle!" Tom said.
"It is big and strong and pretty!" "Yes, it is!" Lily said.
"But it needs something more.
It needs magic!" "Magic?" Tom asked.
"What is magic?" "Magic is something that makes things special and fun.
Like a fairy or a dragon or a rainbow." Lily said.
"We can make magic with our imagination!" "How do we do that?" Tom asked.
Lily picked up a small red block and held it in her hand.
She closed her eyes and made a wish.
She wished that the block would turn into a magic ruby that could make their castle fly.
She opened her eyes and showed the block to Tom.
"Look!
It is a magic ruby!" she said.
"If we put it on top of the highest tower, our castle will fly!" Tom looked at the block.
It was still a small red block.
But he wanted to believe Lily.
He wanted to see their castle fly.
He smiled and took the block from Lily.
He climbed on a chair and reached for the highest tower.
He placed the block on top of it.
"Ready?" Lily asked.
"Ready!" Tom said.
They both clapped their hands and shouted: "Fly, castle, fly!" They looked at their castle.
It did not move.
It was still on the floor.
But in their eyes, it was flying.
It was flying high in the sky, over the clouds and the stars.
It was a magic castle.
And they were happy.
Johnny was a very special boy.
He had a rare brain.
It made him very smart.
He could do things that other boys and girls his age couldn't do.
One day Johnny was playing with his toys in the garden.
He wanted to show his mum how smart he was.
He started to do somersaults and jump.
He had so much fun!
Mum was so proud of him.
She said, "You have a rare brain, Johnny.
You can do so many things!"  Johnny was very happy.
He felt special that he had a rare brain.
He kept practicing and having fun.
Whenever he had questions, he knew he could always ask mum.
Once upon a time, there was a big red door.
The door would always open and close when people came to visit.
One day, a small girl named Lily came to visit her friend, the reliable dog named Max.
Max lived behind the big red door.
Lily said, "Max, I want to play with you!" Max barked and wagged his tail.
They played all day long.
They knew they had to close the big red door when they were done playing, but they forgot.
Later, it started to rain.
Lily and Max went back to the big red door to stay dry.
They saw the door was open.
They remembered they forgot to close it.
Max closed the door, and they both stayed dry and warm inside.
From that day on, Lily and Max always remembered to close the big red door when they were done playing.
They knew it was important to keep their home safe and dry.
And they lived happily ever after.
Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jill.
They were very friendly and loved to play together.
One day, Jack and Jill were playing together when suddenly Jack noticed something strange.
Jack said, “Jill, look.
All the people around us are speaking different languages.” Jill looked around and said, “Wow, that is so amazing!
Can you understand them?” Jack thought for a moment, “No, they all sound very separate.” Jill smiled, “Let's join them.
They look friendly and maybe they can teach us something new.” Jack agreed, and soon they were learning new words and having fun with the people around them.
They soon realised that even though different languages can separate people, it can be fun and exciting to learn about each other.
Once upon a time, two friends were out walking together.
One of them, Tess, had an umbrella.
Suddenly, the sky grew dark and rain started to fall.
Tess pulled out her umbrella and opened it up.
"Be careful," she said to her friend.
"We need to take it slow so we don't fall." But it was too late!
Her friend started running, and she stumbled and fell.
Tess stepped in and closed the umbrella.
She held it over her friend's head to protect them from the pouring rain.
Her friend blinked away the rain from their eyes and looked up at Tess gratefully.
"Thank you," they said.
Tess smiled.
"You're welcome!" she said.
"That's what friends are for!"
Once upon a time, there was a small puppy named Hugo who wanted to explore the world.
One day, Hugo decided to take a walk in the park.
As Hugo was walking along, he stumbled upon a goose.
The goose was quite polite and said hello to Hugo.
Hugo was so excited to have made a new friend and smiled back.
The two new friends decided to play hide-n-seek together.
Hugo counted while the goose ran off to hide.
Hugo looked everywhere but couldn't find his new friend!
Finally, Hugo found the goose behind a big tree and shouted "found you!" The goose was so happy and thanked Hugo for being polite and not giving up.
Hugo realized that being polite was very important and even when things get difficult, he should never give up and be kind.
The two friends had so much fun and when the sun began to set they said goodbye - the small puppy and the new goose.
Once upon a time, there was a big yellow turkey named Tom.
Tom lived on a farm with many friends.
Tom liked to worry a lot.
One day, Tom lost his favorite toy.
He looked everywhere, but he could not find it.
Tom felt sad and started to worry.
"Oh no, where did my toy go?" Tom asked his friend, the cow.
"I don't know," said the cow, "but don't worry, we will find it." Tom and the cow looked all around the farm.
They asked all their friends if they had seen the toy.
But no one knew where it was.
Tom started to worry more and more.
Finally, they found the toy under a big tree.
Tom was so happy!
He said, "Thank you for helping me find my toy.
I will try not to worry so much next time." Tom and his friends played with the toy and had lots of fun.
Once upon a time, there was a nice musician.
He liked to play songs on his guitar.
People loved to hear him play.
One day, the musician went to the beach.
He saw a big blue sea.
He wanted to go swimming.
So, he took a deep breath and dive into the water.
The water was cool and fun.
After swimming, the musician sat on the sand.
He played his guitar and sang a song about his dive.
Everyone clapped and danced to his music.
They all had a great day at the beach.
One Wednesday, Bill and his mom went to the store to get food.
Bill looked in the grocery cart and noticed they only had sweet things like candy and ice cream.
Bill wanted something sour.
He asked his mom, "I need something sour?" She said, "Yes, you do.
Let's look around and see what we can find." They looked in all the aisles, but they couldn't find anything sour.
Finally, they went to the produce department and Bill saw it - a lemon!
It looked juicy and sour.
Bill was so excited.
He said to his mom, "I need that lemon." She smiled and said, "Ok then let's bring it home." When they got home, Bill cut the lemon in half, squeezed the juice into a cup, and added a little sugar.
Then he tasted it.
It was sour and delicious!
From then on, Bill always remembered to get a lemon on Wednesday.
He knew that sometimes he just needed something sour.
Once upon a time, there was a little bunny.
The bunny lived in a cozy shelter made of leaves and grass.
One day, a big wind started to move everything around.
The bunny was scared because it had never seen such a strong wind before.
The bunny hopped around trying to find a safe place to hide.
It saw a big rock and decided to move towards it.
The rock was very big and strong, and the bunny felt safe behind it.
The wind continued to move everything around, but the bunny was no longer scared because it had found a good shelter.
Jack was a very curious three year old.
He loved discovering new things.
He was always looking for something to explore.
One day he was walking in the woods when he saw a mysterious violin lying on the ground.
He had never seen a violin before and was very excited.
He picked it up gently and looked around, but he couldn't find anyone.
Jack wanted to know more about the violin so he ordered it to tell him a story.
He waited, but nothing happened.
He tried again.
Suddenly, the violin started playing a beautiful melody.
Jack was mesmerised.
He watched as the music filled the air.
He clapped along and sang with it.
When the music ended, Jack thanked the mysterious violin for its story.
He hugged it before putting it back on the ground and running off to find his next adventure.
There was a swamp near the town.
The town people were worried about it and wondered how they could manage it.
Then, one day, an impressive thing happened - a frog showed up!
Everyone in town was amazed.
The frog said, "I can manage this swamp for you!" So the town people let him try.
The frog hopped around the swamp and worked with the other animals.
Slowly but surely, the swamp became less swampy.
All the animals helped the frog, and soon the swamp was managed!
The town people were so happy and thanked the frog for being so impressive.
The frog smiled and said, "I managed the swamp with the help of all the other animals - that's what being a team is all about!"  The town people agreed, and everyone lived happily ever after!
One day, a little girl named Sarah wanted to take her puppy to the veterinarian.
She promised her puppy that it was going to be fun.
The veterinarian was really nice, and he promised Sarah he would take good care of her puppy.
He said it would be quick and cheap.
The veterinarian checked if her puppy was healthy.
He checked all of its eyes, ears and teeth.
Everything looked good.
The puppy was so happy everything was ok.
Sarah promised to take better care of her pet and to take it to the veterinarian more often.
The little girl and her puppy thanked the veterinarian for being so kind and for helping her puppy, and then they both left the clinic very happy.
Lisa was so impatient to see what Grandpa had brought her.
She tiptoed to the room, hoping he would not see her, and then she peeked around the corner.
Sure enough, there was a huge mattress on the floor!
She started to run, but stopped herself.
She didn't want Grandpa to know she was so eager.
Lisa took a few more steps, and when Grandpa wasn't looking, she peeked under the mattress.
There was a big box with her name written on it!
Lisa smiled with glee, and quickly grabbed the box.
Grandpa came into the room and she spun around to face him, holding the box to her chest.
"What do you have there?".
He asked, with a twinkle in his eye.
Lisa laughed with delight.
She showed him what was inside - a bright, new tricycle!
Grandpa had been so patient, and now she could finally ride it.
Lisa gave her Grandpa a big hug, and thanked him for the tricycle.
Then she grabbed the handlebars and zoomed out of the room, smiling as she rode away on her new toy.
Once upon a time, there was a huge grape on the ground.
It was so big that it looked like a small melon.
Sam was a little boy, who was only three years old and loved grapes.
He went to pick up the huge grape and imagine what it would taste like.
Sam was about to take a bite when an old man stopped him.
The old man told Sam he should not eat this grape.
He said the grape was special, because it was meant to be made into a jar of wine.
Sam was very curious but he knew he had to obey the old man.
He put the grape down and looked away.
The old man smiled and said that if everything went according to plan, they would be able to make a special kind of wine.
Sam was confused and asked the old man what kind of wine that would be.
The old man said it would be the kind you don't find anywhere else--and said it would be the best wine in the world.
Little Sam was so curious that he could hardly wait to taste it.
The old man smiled and said that if Sam was patient, he would eventually get to try the special wine.
The old man put the grape into a jar and Sam said goodbye to the grape and went back home.
The grape was transformed into a delicious jar of wine, and little Sam was very happy that he got to try it!
Once there was a clever girl named Susie.
She loved to make soup.
Every day she would go to the store and buy the ingredients for her soup.
She would come back home and put all the ingredients into a pot and boil it until it was nice and hot.
Everyone in Susie's neighbourhood loved her soup.
Susie was always very happy when people liked her soup and thanked her for making it.
One day Susie invited her friends to her house for lunch.
She made a big pot of her soup, and her friends ate it all up.
They praised her soup and said it was the best soup they had ever tasted.
Susie was so proud of her soup and her cleverness.
She smiled gleefully, knowing that she had made something that people enjoyed.
From that day onwards, everyone in the neighbourhood knew her name - Susie the Soup-Maker!
Today, Joe was feeling very excited.
His mom had promised him that they would go outside and play.
Joe put on his jacket and ran excitedly to the front door.
"Wait, Joe," said his mom.
"Where's your hat?" "Oh, my hat," said Joe.
He went back to his room and felt around under his bed.
Then, he found it.
"Here it is," said Joe.
He grabbed the cottony sheet and put it on his head.
"It's cold outside," warned Joe's mom.
The wind was indeed cold, and Joe quickly felt the bitter chill.
But he was still too excited to care.
He ran around outside, touching trees, rocks, and even the grass.
Joe smiled and said, "I love touching everything!"  His mom smiled back.
"Me too," she said.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to drink milk every day.
One day, her mom gave her a cup of milk that tasted funny.
Lily was troubled and didn't know what to do.
She wanted to ask her mom about it, but she was afraid.
Lily decided to ask her dad for help.
Her dad listened to her and asked her to show him the milk.
He smelled it and realized that it was spoiled.
He explained to Lily that it's important to ask questions when we are unsure about something, especially when it comes to our health.
From that day on, Lily learned to ask questions when she was troubled or unsure about something.
She knew that it was better to ask and get an answer than to stay quiet and worry.
And she never drank spoiled milk again!
Once upon a time, there was a train.
The train was going to the station.
The train was happy because it was going to see its friends at the station.
But then, something bad happened.
The train hit a tree and it stopped.
The train was stuck and it couldn't move.
The train was sad because it couldn't see its friends at the station.
But then, the train had an idea.
The train thought it could reverse and go back to the station.
So, the train reversed and went back to the station.
When the train got to the station, all its friends were happy to see it.
They asked the train why it came back.
The train told them about the tree and how it was stuck.
The friends were sad that the train had a bad experience.
But they were happy that the train came back to see them.
Ben and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the garden.
They liked to zoom them on the grass and make loud noises.
They saw a big tree with a nest on a branch.
They wanted to see what was inside the nest.
"Let's climb the tree and look at the nest," Ben said.
"OK, but be careful," Lily said.
She was anxious.
She did not like heights.
They put their toy cars down and started to climb the tree.
They held on to the trunk and the branches.
They got closer and closer to the nest.
They saw some feathers and some eggs.
"Wow, look at the eggs!" Ben said.
"They are blue and speckled.
I wonder what kind of birds they are." "Shh, don't be loud.
You might scare the birds," Lily said.
But it was too late.
A big black crow flew out of the nest and cawed angrily.
It saw Ben and Lily and thought they were trying to steal its eggs.
It flapped its wings and pecked at them with its sharp beak.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben and Lily cried.
They let go of the branch and fell to the ground.
They hurt their arms and legs and heads.
They dropped their toy cars and they broke.
The crow flew back to the nest and guarded its eggs.
It was happy.
Ben and Lily were sad and sore.
They ran to their house and told their mom what happened.
She hugged them and put bandages on their wounds.
She said they should not climb trees and touch nests.
They learned their lesson.
They did not play with their toy cars again.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to eat pancakes for breakfast.
One day, Lily's mom made her pancakes on a big plate.
Lily was so happy and started eating right away.
But then, Lily accidentally knocked over the plate and it broke into many pieces.
She felt sad and didn't know what to do.
Her mom saw what happened and said, "Don't worry, we can reverse this.
Let's clean up the pieces and I'll get you a new plate." Lily was happy again and said, "Thank you, Mommy.
I was ignorant and didn't mean to break the plate." Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, accidents happen.
Let's be more careful next time." And they enjoyed their pancakes together on a new plate.
Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy.
Timmy loved to play outside with his friends.
One day, Timmy found a glove on the ground.
He picked it up and waved it around to show his friends.
They thought it was cool!
But then, Timmy's friend Billy wanted to play with the glove too.
Timmy didn't want to share because he was feeling selfish.
He didn't want Billy to touch his special glove.
Timmy's other friend, Sarah, saw what was happening and told Timmy that he should share his glove with Billy.
Timmy thought about it and realized that sharing was a good thing to do.
He gave the glove to Billy and they all played together happily.
The end.
Once upon a time there were two best friends, Jon and Katy.
They were always looking for new ways to have fun and make their day exciting.
One day, they came up with an idea.
"Let's create something using nature!", Jon said.
"Like what?", asked Katy.
"Let's design a wild shade!", Jon said.
So Jon and Katy went out and gathered flowers, leaves and twigs.
They arranged them in a beautiful shape, and created a wild shade.
It looked amazing!

Katy said, "This is even better than I ever imagined!" Jon smiled and replied, "Let's enjoy this shade together!" Jon and Katy laughed and smiled as they spent the day enjoying the shade that they designed.
Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily.
She loved to play outside in the snow with her mittens on.
One day, she lost one of her mittens in the snow.
She looked and looked, but she couldn't find it anywhere.
Lily was sad because her hands were getting cold without her mitten.
Suddenly, her dad had an idea.
He said, "Let's reverse our steps and see if we can find your mitten!" So, they walked back the way they came and looked for the missing mitten.
After a while, they found the mitten buried under the heavy snow.
Lily was so happy and put her mitten back on her hand.
She thanked her dad for helping her find it and they went back inside to drink hot cocoa.
The end.
Once there was a little shape.
It was very gentle and kind.
Every day it would go on long journeys.
One day, it started out on a new journey and it was having lots of fun.
But then it got tired and suddenly, it couldn't go any further.
The shape was so sad that it started to cry.
But then a gentle breeze came and whispered to it, "keep going!
Don't give up!
You can finish your journey." So the shape tried very hard and finally, it reached its destination.
It could hear a sound of joy and it was the most wonderful sound ever!
The shape was so happy to have finished its journey and it thanked the gentle breeze for giving it the courage and strength to keep going.
Jake was three years old.
One day he and his family went to the park.
When he arrived, he noticed a huge old tree with a swing attached to it.
"Mommy, can I swing?" he asked with excitement.
"Yes!" his mom replied.
Jake was so happy.
He ran to the swing and hopped on.
He started to swing as high as he could.
He looked up and saw the sky above him.
He felt so free and happy.
Suddenly, a blackbird flew under the swing and made a loud noise.
Jake screeched with surprise and stopped swinging.
The bird flew away and Jake's mom ran to him.
"Are you ok, honey?" she asked.
"Yes," Jake said, ready to swing again.
"Let's swing higher!"  And so Jake and his mom continued swinging until dinner.
Jake had so much fun and couldn't wait to come back and play on the huge tree swing again.
Jim was a lazy boy.
One day he went to the park to meet some friends.
They were hungry so they decided to get some pizza.
At the pizza shop they saw a big pizza with cheese, ham and veggies.
Jim was so excited that he asked if he could have a slice.
The shopkeeper gave him a big slice and he gobbled it up.
After they finished eating, they played in the park for a while.
They ran around, played tag and rode their bikes.
It was so much fun!
When it was time to go home, Jim said goodbye to his friends and thanked the shopkeeper for giving him the pizza.
He was so happy to have met them and enjoyed eating the yummy pizza.
Once upon a time, there was a zebra who liked to walk around the forest.
One day, the zebra saw a weird animal that looked like a big, scary monster.
The zebra got scared and started to run away.
As the zebra ran through the forest, it saw other animals like birds and squirrels.
The zebra asked them if they had seen the weird animal, but they had not.
The zebra kept walking and looking for a safe place to hide.
Finally, the zebra found a cave and went inside.
It was dark and scary, but the zebra felt safe.
Suddenly, the weird animal appeared at the entrance of the cave.
The zebra was very scared, but it remembered that it had strong legs and could run fast.
So, the zebra ran out of the cave and away from the weird animal.
After a while, the zebra realized that the weird animal was not chasing it anymore.
The zebra felt relieved and continued to walk around the forest, enjoying the beautiful scenery and the company of its animal friends.
Tom and Sam were friends.
They liked to play with their toys.
Tom had many toys, but Sam had only one.
Sam's toy was a soldier.
He loved his soldier very much.
One day, Tom came to Sam's house.
He saw Sam's soldier on the floor.
He picked it up and said, "This is a nice toy.
Can I have it?" Sam was sad.
He said, "No, you can't have it.
This is my toy.
I own it.
It is my only toy." Tom did not listen.
He said, "I want it.
I have many toys, but I don't have a soldier.
Give it to me or I will hit you." Sam was scared.
He did not want to fight.
He said, "Please, don't hit me.
You can have it.
But please, be kind to it.
It is a mild soldier.
It does not like to hurt anyone." Tom took the soldier and ran away.
He laughed and said, "Thank you, Sam.
You are a fool.
I have your toy now.
I will do what I want with it." Sam cried.
He had no toy.
He had no friend.
He was alone.
He wished he had his soldier back.
He wished Tom was not mean.
He wished he was happy.
But he was not.
He was sad.
The end.
One day, Sally was walking with her dad.
She loved exploring the park and playing with all the animals she could find.
Suddenly she saw something shiny under the ground.
She was excited, but when she tried to pick it up, it got stuck.
"Dad, look!
What is it?" she asked, pointing to the shiny thing.
"It looks like a mineral, Sally," her dad said.
Sally was determined to get the mineral, so she kept trying to pull it out of the ground.
But no matter how hard she pulled, it wouldn't come out.
Suddenly, the ground started to shake and the mineral slipped out of her hands.
Sally was so sad that she lost it.
"Don't worry, Sally," her dad said.
"You were very brave to try and get that mineral, even though you were feeling weak." Sally smiled and they went off to explore the rest of the park.
Once upon a time, there was a mighty dog named Max.
Max loved to play ball on the pitch near his home.
One sunny day, Max saw a little girl named Lucy.
Lucy was sad because she lost her ball.
Max wanted to help Lucy.
He said, "Don't worry, I will find your ball!" Max ran all around the pitch, looking for the ball.
He looked under the trees and behind the bushes.
Finally, he found the ball near a big rock.
Max brought the ball back to Lucy.
She was so happy!
She said, "Thank you, Max!
You are a mighty helper!" They played ball together until the sun began to set.
As the day came to an end, Max and Lucy walked home, knowing they had made a new friend.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy who was three years old.
She liked to take care of things, like her toys and her pet dog Spike.
One day, Lucy was very sad.
Her mom had given her a sour lemon to eat, and she didn't like it.
Lucy started to cry, and Spike looked so sad too.
But Spike had a plan to make Lucy feel better.
He ran to the kitchen and grabbed a few yummy snacks.
He ran back to Lucy and gave them to her.
Lucy smiled and hugged Spike, feeling very happy and cared for.
They finished the snacks, and Spike went back to the kitchen to get more.
Lucy hugged him again and saw how much he cared for her.
From then on, Lucy and Spike were the best of friends.
Even when things were sour, Lucy knew that Spike was always there to take care of her.
Jack and his twin, Jill, were walking home from the playground one day.
Jack noticed a thin branch on the ground and decided to remove it from their path.
He looked over to Jill and asked, "Jill, want to help me remove that thin branch?" Jill smiled and said, "Yes!
Let's remove it together!"  Jack and Jill both grabbed the thin branch and carefully started to pull it up.
Suddenly, the branch snapped in two and the twins were left with two thin pieces.
Jack smiled and said, "Jill, I think we should keep the thin branches!" Jill was surprised but agreed.
She picked up one piece while Jack held the other and they both ran home.
Once inside, Jack and Jill brought the thin branches over to their toy box.
They carefully arranged the thin branches so that the two pieces made a great bridge for their toy cars to drive over.
Now, the twins smile every time they play and remember how they worked together to remove the thin branch from their path.
One day, a boy named Tom wanted to eat yogurt.
He was very hungry.
He went to the kitchen and saw a big yogurt cup.
Tom was very happy.
He wanted to eat it all.
Tom's sister, Lily, came into the kitchen.
She saw the yogurt too.
She said, "I want some yogurt too!" Tom did not want to share the yogurt.
He wanted it all for himself.
This made Lily sad.
Tom thought about it for a moment.
He wanted to be a generous brother.
So, Tom said, "Okay, we can share the yogurt." But when he tried to open the yogurt cup, it was very hard.
He pulled and pulled, and then the yogurt cup broke!
Yogurt went everywhere!
Tom and Lily looked at each other and started to laugh.
They knew they had to clean up the mess.
After cleaning, they both learned to share and be more careful with their food.
And from that day, Tom and Lily always shared their snacks and became more generous with each other.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim.
Tim lived in a small house with his mom, dad, and his dog, Max.
They were a happy family.
Tim loved to play outside with Max, but one day, it was very dry and hot.
Tim's mom said it was not a good day to play outside.
Tim was sad, so his mom had an idea.
She said, "Let's order a new toy for you to play with inside." Tim was excited and picked a toy car.
His mom went to the computer and ordered the toy car.
They had to wait for it to come in the post.
After a few days, Tim heard a knock on the door.
It was the postman with a big box.
Tim knew it was his toy car.
He opened the box and found the toy car inside.
He played with it all day and forgot about the dry weather outside.
Tim was happy, and so was Max, because they could play together inside.
The little girl was walking in the park, looking around.
Suddenly, she heard a noise.
She looked closely and saw a hard vegetable.
She walked over to it and started to touch it.
Suddenly, a big bear appeared.
He was angry and started to growl.
The little girl was scared and started to run away.
Suddenly, her mom came to help.
She shouted for the girl and warned her.
She said, "Don't touch the vegetable, it's dangerous!
Let's go home." The little girl was scared but she listened to her mom.
She followed her mom and went home.
The little girl learned that it's important to listen to warnings.
Once upon a time, there was a silly prince who loved to drink juice.
He drank so much juice that he got sick.
His mommy said, "Prince, you need to drink water instead.
Juice is not good for you." But the prince did not listen.
He kept drinking juice and got sicker and sicker.
One day, he had to go to the doctor.
The doctor said, "Prince, you need to stop drinking juice.
It is not good for you." The silly prince finally listened and started drinking water.
He felt much better and learned that too much of anything is not good for you.
The moral of the story is to listen to your mommy and the doctor, and to drink water instead of too much juice.
Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park.
One day, they saw a big lion in a cage.
The lion looked sad and bored.
"Hello, lion," said Lily.
"Why are you in the cage?" The lion roared softly.
"I was caught by bad men who wanted to show me to people.
They forget to feed me and give me water.
They forget to let me run and play.
They forget that I am a lion, not a toy." "That is not fair," said Ben.
"You should be free and happy.
Can we help you?" The lion nodded.
"You can help me by finding the key to the cage.
It is hidden under a rock near the fence.
But be careful, the bad men might come back soon." Lily and Ben looked around and saw a rock that looked different from the others.
They ran to it and lifted it up.
There was a shiny key under it.
"Quick, let's open the cage," said Lily.
They ran back to the lion and put the key in the lock.
The cage door opened and the lion jumped out.
He licked Lily and Ben and thanked them.
"Thank you, friends.
You are very kind and brave.
You did not forget me.
You did not forget that I am a lion, not a toy.
You helped me to be free and happy." The lion ran to the fence and jumped over it.
He ran to the woods where he could find his family and friends.
He roared happily and waved goodbye to Lily and Ben.
Lily and Ben smiled and waved back.
They were happy that they helped the lion.
They learned that they should not forget to be nice and helpful to others.
They learned that they should not forget that animals have feelings and needs too.
They learned that they should not forget to respect and love nature.
Once there was a boy named David.
He was only three years old and was always in awe when looking at the big world around him.
One day he was playing in the park when he found a letter on the ground.
He picked it up and read it out loud.
"Dear David, I have a terrible secret to share.
Please, don't get mad at me.
I need your help.
Please, can you yield this mysterious letter to the person I'm talking about?
You can find him at the post office.
Thank you for your help.
Signed, Anonymous" "Mysterious!" thought David, as he tucked the letter into his pocket and made his way to the post office.
When he got there, David saw a big man with a funny hat behind the counter.
He took out the letter and said, "I need to yield this letter to you."  The big man smiled and said, "No problem.
You have been very brave.
Thank you for yielding this letter to me."  David smiled and felt a sense of accomplishment.
He had done something to help someone else, and it felt great!
One day, a little boy named Tim found a filthy buckle in his yard.
He picked it up and showed it to his mom.
"Mom, look what I found!" he said.
His mom looked at the buckle and said, "Oh, that's very dirty, Tim.
We should clean it up." So they went inside and washed the buckle until it was shiny and new.
Tim wanted to find out where the buckle came from, so he asked his dog, Spot, to help him.
"Spot, can you lead me to where this buckle came from?" Spot wagged his tail and started to sniff the buckle.
Spot led Tim to a big tree in the yard.
There, they found a hidden treasure chest!
Tim opened the chest and found many shiny buckles and other fun things.
"Wow, Spot, we found a treasure!" Tim said with a big smile.
They played with the buckles and had a fun day together.
Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl named Lily.
She loved to play outside and jump on the steps of her porch.
One day, her mommy came outside and said, "Lily, let's go to the park!" Lily was so excited and her smile increased even more.
At the park, Lily saw her friend Max.
Max was sad because he lost his favorite toy.
Lily said, "Don't worry Max, we can help you find it!" They looked all around the park and finally found Max's toy on a step by the slide.
Max was so happy and his smile increased too.
After they found the toy, they all played together and had so much fun.
Lily's mommy said it was time to go home, but Lily and Max wanted to stay and play more.
Lily's mommy said, "Okay, we can stay for five more minutes." Lily was so happy that they got to play a little longer.
When it was time to go, Lily said goodbye to Max and her smile increased even more because she had such a fun day.
Once upon a time, there was a king who lived in a big castle.
He liked everything to be organized and tidy.
He had many servants who helped him keep the castle clean.
One day, the king went for a walk in the forest and he met a friendly dragon.
They became friends and the dragon visited the king every day.
They played games and had fun together.
But one day, the king forgot to remember that he had left the castle door open.
The dragon saw the open door and went inside to explore.
He accidentally knocked over some candles and started a fire.
The castle burned down and the king was very sad.
From that day on, the king always remembered to close the castle door and he never forgot the importance of being organized.
But he missed his friend, the dragon, who had to go away because he felt bad about what had happened.
Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet.
Tweet liked to fly high in the sky and sing songs.
One day, Tweet met a little girl named Lily.
Lily said, "Hi Tweet!
Do you want to be my friend?" Tweet said, "Yes, I want to be your friend!" Lily and Tweet played together every day.
They played hide-and-seek, tag, and flew around together.
One day, Tweet said, "Lily, I'm scared of the dark.
Can you stay with me tonight?" Lily said, "Yes, I will stay with you.
You are my friend and I will always be there for you." That night, Lily and Tweet slept under the stars.
Tweet said, "Lily, you are my true friend.
Thank you for being with me." Lily said, "You're welcome, Tweet.
I will always be here for you." And they both fell asleep, dreaming of flying high in the sky together.
Once upon a time, there was a crane.
The crane had a weird bow on its head.
The bow was red and had polka dots.
The crane liked to show off its weird bow to all the animals in the forest.
One day, the crane saw a butterfly flying by.
The butterfly had a pretty bow too, but it wasn't weird like the crane's bow.
