She asked herself what to do with it.
Then she smiled and made a plan.
Jane took the bow and went outside.
She carefully hid it in the bushes so that no one would find it.
Then she ran back home.
The next day when Jane came back, the bow was still in its hiding spot!
She smiled and carefully picked it up.
Jane twirled and danced with the bow and thought she was the luckiest girl in the world.
Once there was a very eager bird who wanted to fly.
She had big, strong wings and was determined to jump off the tree branch and take off into the air.
The bird stood on the branch for a moment, taking a deep breath.
Then, she jumped with all her might.
But instead of sailing up, she grabbed on to a branch below.
She was a bit confused, so she tried again.
This time, she grabbed onto another branch and hung on tight.
She tried one more time and this time was the charm.
She soared into the sky, happy as could be.
She flew around and around, enjoying the feeling of the cool breeze against her feathers.
She was so happy that she started singing just like the other birds.
The little bird flew high in the sky and was happy with her journey.
From that day on, the bird was always eager to take to the skies once again.
Once upon a time, there was a normal boy named Tim.
Tim loved to play a game with his ball.
One day, while playing, his ball rolled far away.
Tim went to find his ball.
As Tim searched, he heard a small voice.
It was a little bird.
The bird said, "Help, I am stuck!
Can you save me?" Tim saw the bird in a bush.
He was very careful and saved the bird.
"Thank you," said the bird.
"Let's play your game together!" Tim and the bird played the game with the ball.
They had a lot of fun.
From that day on, they were best friends and played the game every day.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
Timmy loved to play outside in the sun.
One day, Timmy found a shiny coin on the ground.
He was so happy and excited to have found it.
But then, he saw his friend Billy coming towards him.
Billy wanted the coin too.
Timmy didn't want to give it up, but he knew it was the right thing to do.
He yielded the coin to Billy and they both smiled.
Later that day, Timmy's mom asked him to help with the laundry.
She gave him a wet shirt to hang up.
Timmy hung it up outside, but it wasn't drying.
He was sad and didn't know what to do.
But then, he remembered the sun.
He put the shirt in the sun and it became dry.
Timmy was happy again.
The end.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim.
Tim had a big rock and a small glass.
One day, he went to play with his friends in the park.
Tim liked to rock the glass back and forth, making it go up and down.
He thought it was fun.
While Tim was playing, a rude boy named Max came and took Tim's rock.
Tim was sad and asked Max to give it back.
Max laughed and said no.
Tim's friends saw this and didn't like it.
They wanted to help Tim.
Tim's friends came up with a plan.
They found more rocks and gave them to Tim.
Then, they all played rock and glass together.
Max saw how much fun they were having and wanted to join.
Tim said Max could play, but only if he said sorry and gave back the rock.
Max said sorry, gave back the rock, and they all played together.
From that day on, Max was not rude anymore.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jess.
Jess loved to spend time in her bedroom, which was filled with cool things.
On her wall she had a cool mirror.
She loved to stand in front of the mirror and look at herself.
She would smile and make funny faces at its reflection.
Jess spent so much time in front of the mirror, that it almost seemed like the mirror was her best friend.
She liked to look at her beautiful dresses and pretend she was at a special party.
Jess also liked to talk to the mirror, and it always seemed like the mirror was listening.
When Jess was tired, she liked to look into the mirror and tell herself a story.
She would make up adventures and tell the mirror all about them.
Jess loved spending time in front of the cool mirror.
She knew it was her special friend.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to draw with her pen and make pictures of flowers and animals.
One day, Lily's big sister, Sarah, came into the room and said, "Lily, I need to use your pen.
Can I borrow it?" Lily didn't want to share her pen because Sarah was always bossy and never let her play with her toys.
But Lily didn't want to suffer and be sad, so she decided to be nice and let Sarah use her pen.
Sarah was surprised that Lily was being so kind.
"Thank you, Lily," she said.
"You're not usually so nice to me." Lily smiled and said, "I don't want to suffer.
I want to be happy and have fun with my pen." From that day on, Sarah was nicer to Lily and they played together with their pens and made beautiful pictures.
And Lily learned that sometimes it's better to be kind and not suffer than to be mean and unhappy.
Once there was a small boy named Joe who lived by a street with lots of trees.
Every day he would go out and play in the street but he was always very naughty.
He would never listen to his parents and always wanted to have his own way.
One day Joe's parents took him to a nearby park.
He saw many different things, a pond, a swing and a garden.
Suddenly, Joe saw a bird in the garden, and he wanted to get it for himself.
Joe's mom saw what he was about to do and she said, "No Joe, you must remain here and stay with us.
The bird should remain in the garden so that it can stay safe".
Joe was disappointed, but he knew his mom was right.
He started to understand that it was bad to be too spoiled and not listen to his parents.
From that day, he started to be more respectful and kind to those around him.
Joe had learned that even in small things he must remain.
Once upon a time, there was a little bunny who loved to run.
Every day, he would rush around the meadow, chasing after butterflies and playing with his friends.
One day, while he was playing, he saw a white shape in the distance.
Curious, he hopped over to investigate.
As he got closer, he realized that the shape was a little bird who had fallen from her nest.
The bunny knew he had to help her, so he carefully picked her up in his soft, furry paws and brought her back to her nest.
The bird's mother was so grateful that she gave the bunny a shiny white feather as a thank you.
From that day on, the bunny learned that helping others was more important than just rushing around and playing all day.
He felt proud of himself for being kind, and he always kept the white feather as a reminder of the important lesson he had learned.
Once upon a time, there was a smart girl named Liza.
She loved to sing and was always interested in fashion.
Every morning Liza woke up and sang a happy little song.
Her song was always noticed by the neighborhood birds, which would come and join in with their own chirps.
One day, Liza had an idea.
She decided to make her own fashion show.
She carefully selected her best outfits and accessories, and began preparing for the fashion show.
She sang a happy little song as she got ready.
Finally the day of the fashion show arrived.
Everyone was very excited.
Liza walked out onto the stage, wearing her finest outfit.
The crowd cheered loudly as she twirled around showing them her pretty dress.
She finished her routine with a final flourish and sang a beautiful song.
The crowd was delighted.
Liza had put on a truly amazing show.
She was very smart, indeed.
From that day on, Liza and her pretty dress became a part of the town's fashionable landscape.
And her songs were often heard echoing in the streets.
Lily liked to paint.
She had many colors and brushes.
She painted on paper, on walls, on boxes, and on her face.
She was very independent.
She did not want to share or listen to anyone.
One day, Lily found a big cushion in the living room.
It was white and soft.
She thought it would be fun to paint on it.
She took her paints and brushes and sneaked to the cushion.
She started to paint flowers and stars and rainbows on the cushion.
She was very happy.
But then, her mom came in and saw the cushion.
She was very angry.
She said, "Lily, what have you done?
This is not your cushion.
This is grandma's cushion.
She gave it to me as a gift.
You have ruined it.
You have to say sorry and help me clean it." Lily felt very bad.
She did not know it was grandma's cushion.
She did not mean to hurt anyone.
She said sorry to her mom and tried to help her clean the cushion.
But the paint was hard to remove.
The cushion was still stained and ugly.
Lily learned a lesson.
She learned that being independent does not mean doing whatever she wants.
She learned that she has to respect other people's things and feelings.
She learned that she has to ask before she paints on something.
She learned that painting is fun, but only on the right things.
Once upon a time, there was a man.
He was walking in the park when he saw a harmless butterfly.
He wanted to touch it, but he accidentally tore its wing.
The man felt sad because he didn't mean to harm the butterfly.
He tried to fix the wing, but he couldn't.
He realized that he should be more careful around small creatures.
From that day on, the man made sure to be gentle and kind to all animals.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
Timmy was very sleepy and wanted to go to bed.
So, he climbed up the stairs to his bedroom.
But before he could sleep, he remembered that he had a toy car that he wanted to store away.
So, he went to his toy box and put the car inside.
Finally, Timmy was ready to sleep.
He closed his eyes and drifted off to dreamland.
The end.
Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom.
Tom was honest and he always tried his best to do the right thing.
One day, Tom was walking past a gum store when he saw something special.
He saw two separate pieces of wondrous gum!
Tom had never seen gum like this before.
He knew he really wanted to try it.
So he opened his pocket and pulled out all his money.
He counted the coins and it was enough to buy the gum.
Tom took the gum and went home.
He was so excited!
But when Tom sat down on the couch, the gum slipped out of his hand and landed on the floor.
The pieces of gum had separated!
Tom was sad.
He didn't want the gum to be apart.
Then, he remembered how honest he was.
He had enough coins to buy the gum, so he ran back to the store and bought two more pieces.
When Tom came back, he put the pieces of gum together.
He was so happy!
The gum was back together, just like he wanted.
From that day on, Tom was always honest and he never separated gum anymore.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to play outside, but one day she lost her boot in the mud.
She was worried that she wouldn't be able to find it.
Lily's mom told her to try looking for it, so she did.
She searched high and low, but couldn't find her boot anywhere.
Just when she was about to give up, she spotted it stuck in the mud.
Lily was so happy to have found her boot and ran back to her mom.
From then on, she always made sure to tie her boots tight so she wouldn't lose them again.
Once upon a time there was a dog named Max.
He was a happy dog who liked to play in the park.
One day, he saw an interesting bone on the ground.
He wanted to take it, so he happily trotted over to it.
“Do you want to sign for it?" said a big man.
Max tilted his head and wondered what signing meant.
The big man saw his confusion and explained it was like a promise.
So Max nodded and made a sign with his paw.
The big man gave Max the bone and he took it over to the most comfortable place he could find - a big green patch of grass in the corner of the park.
Max curled up and hugged the bone close as he fell contentedly asleep.
Once upon a time there was a little bunny.
His name was Bob.
Bob was always so full of fun and joy.
One day Bob was hopping around the garden when out of nowhere a loud noise started.
It was so loud and so scary that it made Bob vanish!
Bob's friends were shocked, they looked everywhere for him but he was nowhere to be seen.
The friends kept looking for him for what felt like forever when suddenly Bob appeared!
He was so happy to see them that he started to hop around in joy.
Bob had been hiding because the loud noise scared him.
Suddenly the loud noise appeared again and once more Bob vanished!
Bob's friends were very worried this time, they looked everywhere but still they could not find him.
The next day Bob reappeared, he had been hiding in a secret place.
He was so happy to see his friends that he hopped around in joy again.
From then on, Bob no longer vanished whenever he heard loud noises.
One day, Bill the rabbit was walking along the field when he saw something pink and shiny.
He quickly hopped over and discovered it was a pistol.
Bill was very excited, and wanted to show the pistol to all his friends.
But then, he heard a voice.
"That is my pistol," said the voice.
It was Liz the fox.
Bill had not seen her coming.
Liz was very angry.
"I found this pistol first," said Bill, trying to settle the situation.
But Liz wasn't happy.
"You must give the pistol back to me," she said.
Bill knew this was a tricky situation.
He didn't like the idea of giving the pistol back to Liz, so he came up with an idea.
"I shall keep the pistol, but I'll give it back to you whenever you want to borrow it," said Bill.
Liz thought about this for a moment and then smiled.
She agreed that this was a good way to settle the dispute.
From then on, Bill could keep the pistol for himself, and Liz could borrow it whenever she wanted.
They smiled at each other, happy the dispute had been so easily settled.
Tom liked to bounce his ball.
He bounced it high and low, fast and slow, near and far.
He bounced it on the grass, on the path, on the wall.
He bounced it all day long.
One day, he bounced his ball too hard.
It flew over the fence and into the road.
Tom ran after it, but he could not catch it.
The ball bounced and bounced and bounced, until it was out of sight.
Tom was sad.
He lost his ball.
He did not have another one.
He sat on the grass and cried.
A girl saw him crying.
She was walking with her mom.
She had a ball too.
It was red and shiny.
She liked to bounce it too.
She went to Tom and said, "Hi, I am Sue.
Why are you sad?" Tom said, "I lost my ball.
It bounced away to the east.
I can't find it." Sue said, "That's too bad.
Do you want to play with my ball?
We can share it." Tom looked at her ball.
It was very nice.
He said, "Thank you, Sue.
You are very kind.
You have a nice ball." Sue said, "You're welcome, Tom.
You are very modest.
You don't need a fancy ball to have fun." They smiled at each other.
They bounced the ball together.
They had fun.
They became friends.
The sun was out and the sky a bright blue.
Little Jimmy could feel the warmth of the sun on his back as he peeked out of the window of the train.
Everywhere he looked, he saw life.
The train went faster and faster, but Jimmy wasn't scared.
He was looking forward to his new home.
As the train slowed down and came to a stop, Jimmy took a deep breath and looked at his mum.
She smiled and said "Come on, let's go Jimmy!" Jimmy got off the train, feeling a little afraid.
He wasn't sure what to expect, but his mum held his hand tightly and told him that everything was going to be ok.
They got to their new home, and Jimmy peeked in through the window.
It was a small but cozy place, and suddenly Jimmy wasn't so fearful anymore.
He knew that this was the beginning of a new and exciting life.
He smiled and squeezed his mum's hand tight, with happiness in his heart.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
Timmy loved to play outside in the sunshine.
One day, he found a big rock and wanted to carry it home.
It was heavy, but he didn't give up.
He carried it all the way home and felt very proud of himself.
The next day, Timmy went to the park and saw a toy sailboat in the pond.
He wanted to play with it, but it was too far away.
He asked his friend for help and they worked together to get the boat.
They were able to sail it and have fun together.
Later that day, Timmy's mom made him some lemonade.
He took a sip and made a sour face.
His mom explained that sometimes things might taste sour, but it's important to keep trying new things.
Timmy learned that trying new things can be fun and rewarding.
One day, a sheep named Bob was very happy.
He had lots of soft wool on his body.
Bob loved to march around the farm with his friends.
Bob and his friends, Tom and Sue, decided to march to the big tree.
They marched and sang a fun song.
"Let's march and play, it's a sunny day!" they sang together.
When they reached the big tree, they saw a little girl named Amy.
Amy was sad because she was cold.
Bob had an idea.
"We can give you some wool to keep you warm," he said.
Amy smiled and was happy.
They all played together under the big tree, and everyone was happy.
Once upon a time, there was a family who went on a trip.
They had lots of luggage with them, which had all their clothes and toys.
They went on a big airplane and flew high in the sky.
When they landed, they went to a hotel by the beach.
It was very peaceful there, with the sound of the waves and the seagulls.
They went to their room and unpacked their luggage.
Later that day, they went to the beach and played in the sand.
Suddenly, a big crab appeared and scared them!
But then they laughed and realized it was just a funny crab.
They had a great time on their trip and made lots of fun memories together.
The end.
Once upon a time there was a brilliant oyster.
It lived in the sea with many other oysters.
Each day it was filled with joy and it loved to play and explore with its friends.
One day, the oyster decided to clean its shell.
It wanted to make sure it was shiny and sparkly.
So, it scraped and scrubbed with all of its might.
It worked so hard that it was soon finished and its shell was the shiniest in the sea.
Everyone admired its brilliant shell.
The oyster was so happy with its work.
From that day on, it always kept its shell clean and sparkly—just like a brilliant oyster should.
Once upon a time, there was a weak elephant.
He was so weak he could hardly balance.
He tried to stand on one leg, but he couldn't do it.
He tried to stand on two legs, but he wobbled and fell over.
The elephant was sad, so he decided to find someone to help him.
He looked around until he spotted a small boy.
He could tell the boy was very clever.
The elephant asked the boy for help.
The boy smiled and thought of an idea.
He told the elephant to concentrate and find his balance.
The elephant closed his eyes and tried again.
Amazingly, after a few tries, the elephant managed to balance on one leg.
Then he balanced on two legs.
He felt strong and happy!
The little boy was so proud of the elephant and cheered with joy.
From then on, the elephant and the little boy were best friends as they practiced balancing together.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to play outside with her friends.
One day, she saw her friend, Timmy, kneel down by the road.
"What are you doing?" Lily asked.
"I'm looking at the traffic," Timmy replied.
"I like to watch the cars go by." Lily joined Timmy and they watched the cars together.
Suddenly, they saw a pale woman walking along the road.
"Is she okay?" Lily asked.
"I don't know," Timmy said.
"Let's go ask her."  They ran over to the woman and asked if she needed help.
She said she was lost and didn't know how to get home.
So, Lily and Timmy took her by the hand and helped her find her way back.
The woman was very grateful and thanked them both.
From that day on, they became good friends.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She liked to talk a lot, especially to her toys.
One day, she was playing with her doll when she heard her mommy say, "I need to cut some vegetables for dinner."  Lily wanted to help her mommy, so she asked if she could cut something too.
Her mommy said no because the knife was too sharp for her.
But Lily was persistent and kept asking.
Finally, her mommy gave her a plastic knife and some play dough to cut.
Lily was so happy and started cutting the play dough into little pieces.
She talked to her doll all about it and showed her the pieces she cut.
After dinner, Lily's mommy praised her for being such a good helper and for being persistent in wanting to help.
Lily felt proud of herself and went to bed with a big smile on her face.
Once upon a time there was a prince who lived in a big castle.
He wanted to find a special friend.
One day he saw a nice little girl.
He said, "Hello!" The girl said well and politely.
She said, "Hello!" The prince said, "Would you like to be my friend?" The little girl thought for a moment and then said, "Yes, I'd like that!" So the prince and the little girl became friends.
They had lots of fun together playing tag in the castle garden and telling stories in the dining hall.
They also got to visit the castle kitchen and the castle library, where they looked at all the interesting books.
The prince was very polite and always said please and thank you.
He taught the little girl to be polite too.
They laughed and played together happily for many days.
The end.
Once upon a time there was a little pig who was very excited for sunrise.
He was outside his house looking for something to mark.
He saw a big rock and decided it was perfect for marking.
He picked up a big stick and marked a smiley face on the rock.
The pig was so proud of his work.
Just then a bird came flying by and noticed the rock with the smiley face.
"That is such an amazing thing to mark.
Where did you learn to do it?" asked the bird.
The little pig was so excited to explain.
"I learned it all by myself!
I just wanted to make something special for the upcoming sunrise," he said.
The bird was very impressed and flew away.
The little pig smiled and knew that the smiley face would cheer up the sunrise.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Sam.
He was playing hide and seek with his friends.
Sam wanted to be the first one to hide, so he quickly ran and hid in a big bush.
But when he was hiding, he saw something scary!
It was a ghost!
The ghost was very big and it was making loud, angry noises.
Sam was scared but he could not move.
He was too scared to come out of the bush.
But then, his friends came to the same bush.
They did not see the ghost.
They started to cover up Sam with leaves, because they thought he was still playing hide and seek.
But as soon as the leaves touched Sam, the ghost got even angrier.
It started to throw pieces of rocks and sticks at them.
Sam and his friends ran away as fast as they could.
They all survived and never saw that ghost ever again!
Once upon a time, there was a 3 year old boy named Jack.
He liked to play with his toys, but today he was looking for something different.
Then, all of a sudden, he heard a voice.
The voice said, "Come in and get some yarn!" Jack was very excited and ran to the door.
He opened it and entered.
Inside was a shop full of colorful yarn!
It was all very exciting.
He then saw a woman sitting behind the counter.
She was kind, yet bossy.
She showed him all kinds of wonderful yarn.
He chose a bright green one and ran over to a corner to play with it.
He made a big ball with the green yarn.
He played with it all afternoon and had lots of fun.
When the day was done, Jack thanked the bossy woman for the yarn and ran outside, back to his home, with a smile on his face.
And that is the story of how Jack found his special yarn.
Once upon a time there was a small bear.
The bear was very happy, but he was also very curious.
He wanted to try something new that day.
He found some smoke and decided to spin around in it.
He spun and he spun and he spun until he got dizzy.
He laughed and laughed but then he started to cough.
The smoke was very long and soon he couldn't see the sun.
He spun around even more, but the smoke just wouldn't go away.
He waved his paw around, but nothing worked.
"Help!" he cried, but no one came.
The small bear was all alone and soon the smoke got thicker and thicker.
He started to spin faster and faster, but the smoke just stayed there.
The small bear was scared and sad.
He kept spinning and spinning until he was too tired to spin anymore.
But the smoke never went away.
The small bear was never seen again.
He was lost in the long smoke forever.
Once upon a time, there was a stable.
It was very important.
There was a big machine in the stable.
It was called a printer.
Every day, it printed pictures.
It printed pictures of animals, toys and many other things.
It was fun to look at the pictures and see what the printer made.
Every day, the printer printed something new and it was always so exciting to see.
One day, the printer printed a special picture.
It was the most important picture of all!
Everyone was so happy that they celebrated with a big party.
They all thanked the printer for making such an important picture.
Everyone loved the printer and the pictures it printed.
Once there was a little girl named Chloe.
She was three years old and she loved to travel.
One day, Chloe went to the mall with her mom.
She was so excited, she couldn't help but smile.
Chloe ran around the mall, looking at all the amazing things she could buy.
She spotted a bright teddy bear and asked her mom if she could buy it.
Her mom said she could, and Chloe was so happy she screamed!
Chloe's mom said that it was time to go home, but Chloe wanted to stay.
Her mom said she could come back again soon, because it was so easy to travel to the mall.
So Chloe smiled and said, "Okay, let's go!"  Chloe and her mom said goodbye to the mall, and Chloe was already dreaming about the next time she would get to travel there.
Once upon a time, there was a big rhinoceros.
He was a little bit crazy.
He liked to tell funny stories to his friends.
His friends were a cat, a dog, and a bird.
They all lived in a big green forest.
One day, the crazy rhinoceros told a new story.
He said, "I can jump very high and touch the sky!" His friends laughed and said, "No, you can't!" The rhinoceros said, "Yes, I can!
Watch me!" He started to run very fast.
The cat, the dog, and the bird watched the crazy rhinoceros run.
He jumped high into the air.
But he could not touch the sky.
He fell down on the ground very hard.
The rhinoceros was hurt and sad.
His friends felt bad too.
The crazy rhinoceros learned not to tell stories that were not true.
Timmy loved to swing.
He would always wait for his dad to take him to the park to swing.
When they would go to the park, Timmy's dad would push him on the swing and make him giggle.
It was his favorite thing.
One day Timmy's dad picked up something special at the store.
It was a big vase for their living room.
It was a beautiful vase, with red and blue colors.
It was available for a very good price.
When they got home, Dad found the perfect spot for the vase in the corner of their living room.
Timmy thought the vase was so cool and he wanted to show it to his friends the next day.
That night since he was excited, Timmy couldn't sleep.
He wished they had a swing inside their house.
Then he had an idea.
He got out of bed and started pushing the vase, like it was a swing.
He swung back and forth, until he got tired and woke up his dad.
His dad said it was time to go to sleep, but was still very amused by Timmy's idea.
From that day, Dad would always gently swing the vase for Timmy, and he would laugh and giggle.
It was his new favorite thing.
Once upon a time there was a little boy named Tim.
Tim was only three years old.
One day, Tim's mommy made him a nice bowl of his favorite soup.
Tim took a big bite and then he went to watch his favorite film.
The film was about a big, scary monster.
It made Tim so scared that he started to weep.
Mommy heard Tim's cries and ran into the room.
"Oh no, why are you crying Tim?" asked Mommy.
"The film was too scary," said Tim.
Mommy hugged him tight and said, "It's okay, Tim, it's just a film.
There are no real monsters.
You are safe." Tim smiled and mommy wiped his tears away with a tissue.
Mommy tucked him into bed and said, "Good night, Tim.
Sweet dreams." Tim closed his eyes and soon he was sound asleep.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to reach a mole in her garden.
The mole was digging a very deep tunnel and the little girl wanted to see what was down inside.
She was so excited when she saw the mole!
The little girl reached out her hand and was about to grab the mole when it scurried away.
The mole was so fast!
She was amazed at how quickly it moved.
The little girl followed the mole as it ran around the garden.
She chased after it as fast as she could.
Finally, she reached the mole just as it was about to go into its hole.
She grabbed it with her two hands and gently held it.
The mole felt so soft and the little girl thought it was so pretty.
The little girl then gave the mole a kiss on the head and opened her hands to set it free.
The mole scampered away and the little girl smiled.
She had reached the mole and it was such a wonderful experience.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved ice cream, especially when it came in a cone.
One day, she went to the ice cream truck and got a big cone with lots of flavors.
She was so happy!
Suddenly, her little brother came and asked for some ice cream.
Lily didn't want to share because she wanted it all for herself.
But then she felt guilty and decided to pass him a little bit of her cone.
He was very happy too!
From that day on, Lily learned that sharing is important and it made her feel good inside.
She always made sure to pass a little bit of her cone to her brother and friends.
And they all lived happily ever after, enjoying their ice cream cones together.
The end.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
One day, Lily and her mom went to church.
Lily loved going to church because she got to sing and hear stories about Jesus.
During the service, Lily saw a man sing a beautiful song.
When the song was over, everyone clapped and cheered.
Lily asked her mom, "Why did everyone applaud?" Her mom explained that when people like something, they clap their hands to show they are happy.
After church, Lily and her mom saw an old man walking on the street.
He looked very weak and tired.
Lily's mom asked him if he needed help.
The old man said he needed help carrying his groceries.
So, Lily and her mom helped the old man and he was very grateful.
"Thank you so much," he said.
"You are very kind." Lily felt happy inside because she had done a good deed.
She told her mom, "I am happy we helped the old man.
I want to make people happy like the man who sang at church." Her mom smiled and said, "That's a very kind thing to say, Lily."
Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Joe.
He wanted to go on a grand adventure, but he needed something to help him.
He found a box with a lock on it.
He tried to unlock it, but it was too hard for him.
Joe asked his mom for help.
His mom told him that if he helped around the house, she would unlock the box for him.
Joe was excited!
He quickly got to work, cleaning the dishes, tidying the toys and making his bed.
After he had done this, his mom came back with a key.
She unlocked the box for Joe.
When he opened it, Joe was so impressed!
Inside was a beautiful set of new clothes!
He quickly put them on and started exploring the world, on a grand adventure!
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy.
Timmy liked to visit his grandma's house.
She always had yummy cookies for him to eat.
One day, Timmy went to visit his grandma's house and he saw a ghost!
The ghost was see-through and floated in the air.
Timmy was scared at first, but then he realized the ghost was friendly.
Timmy's grandma told him that the ghost was her friend and she had been trying to find him for a long time.
Timmy was happy to help his grandma be successful in finding her friend.
They all had a nice visit together and even the ghost got to try some of grandma's cookies.
The end.
The little boy had a uniform that was too big for him.
His mom saw how sad he was, so she hugged him and said, "It's okay sweetie, don't feel sorry." He felt better, but still not quite ready to put his uniform on.
His mom told him, "The sun is rising, and you have to get ready for school." He looked outside, and she was right; the sun was rising slowly in the sky.
He knew he had to get ready for school, so he said, "Yes mommy, I understand."  He put his uniform on, but it still felt too big.
So his mom got out the sewing machine and said, "Don't worry, I'll make it fit you better." She worked on his uniform while he watched, and then he put it back on.
He saw how it fit him much better than before; he felt happy and ready to go to school.
He thanked his mom and gave her a big hug.
Then he quickly ran outside and watched the sun rise above the horizon.
He was so excited for another day of school, and he knew he could do it in his new uniform.
Once upon a time, there was a brave ostrich named Ollie.
Ollie was very tall and had big, strong legs.
One day, Ollie was walking in the forest when he saw a little bird.
"Hello little bird," said Ollie.
"What are you doing here?" "I'm lost," said the little bird.
"Can you help me find my way home?" "Of course," said Ollie.
"I'll help you." Suddenly, a snake struck Ollie with its sharp teeth.
Ollie fell to the ground and couldn't move.
The little bird flew away to find help, but it was too late.
Ollie had died.
The little bird was very sad.
"Goodbye, brave Ollie," it said.
"Thank you for trying to help me."
Sara and Ben like to play with their toys.
They have many toys, but their favorite is a soft fox.
The fox is brown and white, and has a long tail.
Sara and Ben hug the fox and pretend it can talk.
One day, a man comes to their house.
He has a big bag and a big smile.
He knocks on the door and says, "Hello, I am here to sell you some new toys.
Do you want to see them?" Sara and Ben run to the door.
They are curious and excited.
They want to see the new toys.
They say, "Yes, please, show us the new toys!" The man opens his bag and takes out some dolls, cars, blocks, and books.
He says, "Look at these wonderful toys.
They are shiny and colorful and fun.
You can have any of them for a small price.
How about this doll?
Or this car?
Or this block?" Sara and Ben look at the new toys.
They are shiny and colorful and fun.
But they do not want to give up their fox.
They love their fox.
They say, "No, thank you, we do not want these toys.
We have our fox.
Our fox is soft and cuddly and smart.
We do not want to trade our fox for anything." The man is impatient.
He wants to sell his toys and make money.
He says, "But these toys are better than your fox.
Your fox is old and dirty and boring.
You should get rid of it and buy something new.
How about this book?
Or this block?" Sara and Ben shake their heads.
They do not like the man.
They do not like his toys.
They say, "No, thank you, we do not want these toys.
We want our fox.
Our fox is our friend.
We do not want to sell our fox.
Please go away." The man is angry.
He says, "Fine, then.
You are silly and stubborn.
You do not know what is good for you.
I will go and find someone else who will buy my toys.
Goodbye." He puts his toys back in his bag and leaves.
Sara and Ben close the door.
They hug their fox and say, "We are sorry, fox.
We did not mean to make you sad.
We love you very much.
You are the best toy ever." The fox smiles and says, "I love you too, Sara and Ben.
You are the best friends ever." They play happily together.
Lily liked to wander in the park.
She saw many things: trees, flowers, birds, dogs.
She liked to say hello to them.
Sometimes she picked up sticks or stones and played with them.
One day, she saw a man with a big bag.
He was picking up trash from the ground.
He had a job to keep the park clean.
Lily wanted to help him.
She ran to him and said, "Hi, I am Lily.
Can I help you?" The man smiled and said, "Hello, Lily.
You are very kind.
But this is not a job for a little girl.
This trash is dirty and can hurt you.
You should play somewhere else." Lily felt sad.
She wanted to do a good thing.
She said, "But I like the park.
I want to make it nice." The man said, "I understand.
But there is another way to help.
You can be careful not to drop any trash yourself.
And you can tell your friends and family to do the same.
That way, you can keep the park nice for everyone." Lily nodded.
She said, "OK, I will do that.
Thank you for your job.
Bye!" She waved to the man and ran to find her mom.
She told her what she learned.
Her mom hugged her and said, "You are a smart and caring girl.
I am proud of you." They walked home together.
On the way, they saw a wild cat.
It was hiding under a car.
It had yellow eyes and black fur.
Lily wanted to pet it, but her mom said, "No, Lily.
That cat is wild.
It is not like our cat at home.
It can scratch or bite you.
You should leave it alone." Lily said, "OK, mom.
I will not touch it.
But can I say hello?" Her mom said, "Sure, you can say hello.
But be quiet and gentle.
Do not scare it." Lily said, "Hello, wild cat.
You are pretty.
I hope you are happy." The cat looked at her and meowed softly.
Then it ran away.
Lily smiled and said, "Bye, wild cat.
Have a nice day." The end.
Lily liked to talk to her plant.
She gave it water and sun and said nice things to it.
She hoped the plant would reply, but it never did.
It only grew green leaves and sometimes flowers.
One day, Lily saw a new plant in the garden.
It was big and purple and had a mouth.
Lily was curious and went to say hello.
"Hi, plant.
What is your name?" she asked.
The plant opened its mouth and said, "I am a Venus flytrap.
I eat bugs and sometimes birds.
Who are you?" Lily was surprised and scared.
She had never heard a plant talk before.
She ran back to her house and hugged her normal plant.
"You are my friend, plant.
You don't eat bugs or birds.
You are nice and quiet and pretty," she said.
The normal plant did not reply, but it seemed to smile.
Lily felt happy and safe with her plant.
She decided to stay away from the purple plant in the garden.
It was too strange and scary for her.
Once there was a little boy who wanted to look nicer.
He decided he wanted to get a haircut.
He went to the barber and the barber welcomed him.
The little boy was so excited for his new look.
The barber got to work.
He used scissors and comb to give the little boy his new haircut.
After the haircut, the little boy looked in the mirror and he was so pleased with how he looked.
The barber smiled and welcomed him to come back anytime he wanted.
The little boy thanked the barber.
As he left the barbershop, the little boy felt so spoiled because he had a very nice haircut.
He was very excited and happy about his new look.
Once upon a time, there was a poor sign maker named Jack.
He had an old box full of empty signs.
Everyday he went out and tried to fit these signs onto windows, but nothing ever seemed to fit.
He was walking along one day, when he saw a small window.
He fit the last sign he had into the window and smiled at the perfect fit.
As he looked closer, he noticed a sad little girl inside the window, looking right back at him.
He asked her, "What's the matter?" She said softly, "I miss my parents, they said they will be back soon but they never come home."  Jack put his hands on her tiny shoulders and said, "Don't worry.
You just wait here.
I'll make a sign special for your parents and I know it will fit just right so they will be sure to find you."  The little girl was so grateful for the kindness of Jack.
Jack's kindness that day was rewarded when the girl's parents thanked him and rewarded him with a bag of coins.
From then on, Jack was no longer poor and he never had another sign that didn't
Once upon a time there was a mommy and a baby.
The baby's name was Anna.
Every day Mommy would raise Anna up high in the air and then give her a big hug.
One day, Anna was feeling a little bit of pain in her tummy.
Mommy asked her what was wrong, and Anna said her tummy was hurting.
Mommy knew she needed to help.
“Please take care of my baby,” Mommy said as she picked Anna up and hugged her close.
Mommy looked after Anna all day and made sure she was better.
But then the next day, Mommy was being careless.
She was not paying attention to Anna and Anna started to feel the pain again.
Anna asked Mommy to pick her up and raise her in the air again.
After seeing the pain in Anna’s eyes, Mommy knew exactly what she had to do.
Mommy quickly picked Anna up, hugged her tight and then raised her in the air.
Anna smiled, and the pain went away.
Mommy smiled back and said, “Always take care of yourself and make sure you stay safe.”
Once there was a little girl named Ruby.
She was 3 years old and loved to play outside.
One day, she noticed something very special up on her roof.
It was a big, pink balloon.
Ruby couldn't help but wonder how the balloon got there.
She thought it must have been a special gift from the sky.
Ruby grabbed a ladder and set it up against the side of her house.
She climbed up to the roof and carefully grabbed the pink balloon.
It was made of brightly coloured paper, and had the word "love" written on it.
Taking a deep breath she blew up the balloon, filling it with air until it was big and round.
For the rest of the day, Ruby watched in amazement as the balloon floated across the sky.
Suddenly, it disappeared around a corner of the pink-painted house.
The happy little girl smiled, knowing that the pink balloon had gone on a great adventure.
Tom and Mia were playing in the park.
They liked to run and jump and slide.
They saw a big tree with many leaves.
They wanted to climb the tree and see what was up there.
They took turns to go up the tree.
Tom went first.
He saw a bird nest with three eggs.
He saw a squirrel with a nut.
He saw a spider web with a shiny insect.
He wanted to touch the insect, but the spider scared him.
He said, "Mia, look at this insect!
It is so pretty and shiny!" Mia went up the tree.
She saw the insect too.
She liked it very much.
She said, "Tom, can I have the insect?
I want to keep it as a pet!" Tom said, "No, Mia, it is mine!
I saw it first!" Mia said, "But I like it more!
Please, Tom, give it to me!" Tom and Mia started to fight.
They pulled and pushed and shouted.
The spider was angry.
It bit Tom on his hand.
Tom cried out loud.
He let go of the insect.
The insect flew away.
Mia said, "Tom, are you okay?
I am sorry, I did not mean to hurt you." Tom said, "Mia, I am sorry too.
I should have shared with you.
The insect is gone now.
We were silly to fight over it." Tom and Mia hugged each other.
They climbed down the tree.
They saw their mom waiting for them.
She had a basket with snacks and juice.
She said, "Are you hungry, my loves?
Come and have some food.
You look tired from playing." Tom and Mia said, "Yes, mom, we are hungry.
Thank you for the food.
We love you, mom." They ran to their mom.
They ate and drank and told her about their adventure.
They learned to yield and share and be kind.
They had a happy day in the park.
Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Jack.
He wanted to take a ride in the park.
He couldn't wait any longer!
So he grabbed his pencil and hopped inside his car.
When Jack got to the park, he noticed it was very dirty.
All around were pieces of garbage and leaves from the trees.
Jack got out of his car and began to explore.
He stepped around the garbage and even found a dirty old pencil!
He was so excited that he took it with him.
Suddenly, he heard a voice.
A kind old man said, "What a nice pencil, son!
Would you like to join me for a walk around the park?" Jack was overjoyed!
He said, "Yes, please!" The old man and Jack went around the park together, pointing out all the different flowers and animals they found.
As they walked, Jack even stopped to pick up a few more pieces of litter that he found.
When they finished their walk around the park, the old man said, "You're such a kind-hearted boy, Jack!
Always remember to keep the park clean!" Jack smiled.
He said, "I will!" And he put his pencil and the litter in his car before he drove away.
Once upon a time, there was a little old lady.
She was silly and liked to dance and sing.
One day, she was walking down the street and suddenly had an idea.
She said to herself, "I will drop my old hat on the ground and I will dance around it!" So, she took off her old hat and dropped it on the ground.
Suddenly, a boy walked by and saw her silly hat on the ground.
He wanted to keep it for himself.
He started to pick it up and the old lady said, "No!
That's my hat." The boy didn't listen and kept trying to take the hat.
The old lady was very angry and decided to teach the boy a lesson.
She said, "If you don't drop my hat, I will start singing a silly song and dance around it!" The boy was scared and quickly dropped her hat and ran away.
The old lady was very happy.
She was glad that she stood up to the boy and was able to get her hat back.
She picked it up, put it on her head and then started to sing and dance around it.
Once upon a time, there was a kind lady named Mrs.
Smith.
She wore a big apron and liked to bake yummy treats.
One day, she went to her garden to pick some fresh vegetables.
She was very humble and always shared her crops with her neighbors.
As she was picking some carrots, she noticed a little bunny hopping around.
The bunny was so cute and Mrs.
Smith wanted to pet it.
But the bunny was scared and ran away.
Mrs.
Smith didn't want to scare the bunny, so she left it alone and went back to her kitchen to bake some carrot cake.
Later that day, Mrs.
Smith brought the cake to her neighbor's house.
The neighbor was so happy and said it was the best cake she had ever tasted.
Mrs.
Smith felt proud and happy that she could make someone else smile.
From that day on, Mrs.
Smith always made sure to pick extra vegetables for her neighbors and share her delicious treats.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl.
She was a bit fearful, so she had to learn how to be brave.
One day, she picked up a mug.
She liked it a lot, so she decided it would be her special mug.
From then on, each day she used her mug to learn something new.
She put a little bit of water in it and pretended it was oceans and rivers.
She did this to learn about the world.
She also took a few small pebbles she had found and pretended they were treasure.
She did this to learn about money.
All the while, her mug kept her feeling brave.
Each day she felt a little more brave and a little less fearful.
Soon, she felt as strong and fearless as a lion.
Once upon a time, there was a small house.
Inside the house lived a family of three.
One day, the family members heard a knock on the door.
When they opened it, a lovely lady entered.
The family was so happy and excited.
"Welcome to our small home!", said the mom.
The lady smiled and said, "It is such an honor to be here.
I am here to celebrate with you all.
Today, your family is getting married." Everyone was thrilled.
They hugged and danced around the room.
Then the parents put on their wedding clothes and they all went outside.
It was a glorious day.
They had a small ceremony and said their special vows.
Finally, they kissed and a lovely marriage had started.
The family was so happy and thankful for the special lady who had entered their home and brought them this amazing gift.
From that day forward, the family was full of love.
The End.
Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a stubborn little dog named Spot.
Spot loved to play outside all day long.
He would run, jump, and chase his tail under the warm sun.
One hot day, Spot was feeling very tired.
He wanted to find some shade to rest in.
He looked around and saw a big tree.
Spot ran to the tree and laid down in the cool shade.
The shade made him feel much better.
After resting for a while, Spot saw a big bone nearby.
He wanted to finish eating the bone before going back to play.
So, Spot picked up the bone and started to chew on it.
He was very happy to finish the bone in the shade of the big tree.
Once upon a time there was a small kitten called Mr Fluffy.
Mr Fluffy would love to explore the outdoors, but he was scared and would always stay inside.
One day he decided to try something new, he wanted to balance on the coal which was kept next to the fireplace.
He was nervous, but he knew he had to try.
Mr Fluffy slowly crept up to the coal pile.
His tiny paws were shaking with fear but he was determined to do it.
He stepped onto the lump of coal and, with practice, started to balance.
After only a few seconds he was standing still, with both paws firmly planted on the lump of coal.
He felt proud.
Suddenly, there was a loud noise and Mr Fluffy was scared.
He quickly lost balance and fell off the coal pile.
He lay there for a few seconds, feeling sad and scared.
But after a few moments, he plucked up the courage to climb back up the coal.
He took a deep breath, and stepped onto the coal again.
After a few moments of practice, he once again managed to balance.
He stayed there for a few seconds and felt very happy.
The next day, Mr Fluffy balanced on the coal pile again and again until he was no longer scared.
He had conquered his fear and now he was happy and brave.
Alice loved to explore the wild beach.
She ran through the sand and discovered many fun things.
Today, she found a big oyster.
She had never seen one before and was so excited!
Alice tapped the oyster and talked to it.
"Hello, oyster!"  The oyster did not move.
Alice decided to open the oyster.
She found a rock inside.
It was so heavy she needed help to carry it.
Alice asked her parents for help.
They said, "Let's cover the oyster with a rock.
Then we can bring it home." Alice said, "Ok!" and she found the perfect rock to cover the oyster.
When they got home, her parents took off the rock and revealed something lovely.
Inside the oyster was the most beautiful pearl!
Alice screamed with glee, "Look what I found in the wild oyster!"
Once upon a time, there was a little gray mouse who loved to play on his computer.
He would spend all day clicking and tapping away, never taking a break.
One day, the mouse felt very tired and his eyes hurt from staring at the bright screen.
Suddenly, he heard a loud "spring" sound coming from outside.
He went to investigate and found a beautiful garden full of colorful flowers and trees.
The mouse realized he had been missing out on the beauty of nature because he was always on his computer.
From that day on, the little gray mouse made a promise to himself to take breaks from his computer and enjoy the wonders of the world around him.
He learned that there is more to life than just staring at a screen all day.
Once upon a time there was a green top.
The green top glowed in the dark.
It was so shiny and sparkly.
Everyone wanted to have the green top.
One day, a little girl saw the green top.
She was so happy and she wanted to keep it.
She asked her mom if she could have the green top and her mom said yes.
The little girl kept the green top in her bedroom.
Every night when it was dark, the green top glowed so brightly.
It lit up her bedroom and she was never scared in the dark.
The little girl and the green top were best friends and they played together every day.
The green top glowed and it was the best top in the whole world!
Tim and Mia like to play with their toys.
They have many toys, but their favorite is a robot.
The robot can talk and move and make funny sounds.
Tim and Mia call him Robby.
One day, Tim and Mia are playing with Robby in their room.
They make him walk and dance and sing.
They are very happy.
But then, their mom comes in and says, "Time to clean up, kids.
Put your toys away and get ready for dinner." Tim and Mia do not want to stop playing.
They say, "No, mom.
We want to play more.
Robby is fun." Mom says, "You can play later, after dinner.
But now you have to tidy up.
Robby is fragile.
He can break if you leave him on the floor." Tim and Mia resist.
They say, "No, mom.
Robby is strong.
He can not break.
He is our friend." Mom says, "I know, but he is still a toy.
And toys need to be taken care of.
Come on, help me put him in his box.
He will be safe there." Tim and Mia look at Robby.
He looks at them and says, "I am your friend.
But I also need to rest.
Please put me in my box.
I will wait for you." Tim and Mia feel sad.
They love Robby.
But they also love their mom.
They decide to listen to her.
They hug Robby and say, "Bye, Robby.
We will play with you later.
We love you." They put Robby in his box and help mom clean up.
Mom smiles and says, "Thank you, kids.
You are very good.
Now let's go have dinner." Tim and Mia nod and follow mom.
They are hungry.
They think about Robby and hope he is not lonely.
They promise to play with him again soon.
A mom and dad were getting ready for a trip.
The mom packed their luggage and the dad loaded it in the car.
Then they hugged each other, kissed their three year old daughter and said goodbye.
The daughter was sad, but she knew they would come back soon.
The mom and dad traveled to a big city.
They were very serious because they had important business to do.
They carried their luggage as they went from meeting to meeting.
After many days of hard work, they were done, and they were ready to go home.
At home, their daughter ran to hug them.
She was so happy that they were back.
As she held them close, she could tell how much they cared for her.
She knew that no matter what, her mom and dad would always be there for her.
Once upon a time, a long, long time ago, there was an ancient castle.
The castle was very big and very old.
It had been there for a very long time.
Inside the castle, there was a big room where people would sing and dance.
This was called an opera.
One day, a little boy came to the castle.
He was very curious and wanted to see the opera.
He walked inside and saw all the people singing and dancing.
He was amazed!
But then he noticed an old lady sitting in the corner all by herself.
She looked sad.
The little boy went up to her and asked, "Are you okay?
Do you need help?" The old lady looked up and smiled.
She said, "Yes, I'm just feeling a little lonely." The little boy knew he cared about her, so he took her hand and brought her to the front of the room.
They watched the opera together and had a wonderful time.
From that day on, they became good friends and would always go to the opera together.
Once upon a time, there was a star.
The star was so broken that it trembled in the sky.
Every night it shook and wobbled, making all the animals around it scared.
Every night, a little mouse would come and try to help the star.
The mouse would carefully brush each of the star's broken pieces back together.
Every night, the mouse made the star a little bit brighter, a little bit bigger.
But the star still trembled.
One night, something special happened.
The mouse had put all of the star's pieces together and suddenly, the star stopped trembling.
It was strong, and bright, and beautiful in the sky!
The mouse had done it!
The mouse jumped and clapped and called all the animals around, so they could see the shining star in the night.
All the animals cheered and clapped for the brave little mouse who had saved the star!
Once upon a time there was a bird.
The bird wanted to fly high and explore the world.
Every day it flew up in the sky.
It loved to fly!
One day the bird got married!
It was a very humble ceremony.
Other birds came to celebrate.
Everyone was happy.
Eventually the bird said to its partner "Let's fly together".
The partner agreed and together they flew high in the sky.
They had so much fun.
The bird said "This is why I wanted to marry you, so I can fly with you forever!".
The partner smiled and said "Me too".
And so they flew and flew, together!
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to cook with her mom in the kitchen.
One day, Lily's mom asked her to help make spaghetti for dinner.
Lily was so excited to help!
As they were cooking, Lily accidentally made a messy sauce spill on the counter.
"Uh oh, Mommy!
I made a mess!" she said.
"It's okay, Lily.
Let's clean it up together," her mom replied.
After they cleaned up the messy sauce, Lily's mom showed her how to make a loop with the spaghetti on her fork.
"Look, Lily!
You made a loop!
Great job!" her mom exclaimed.
Lily was so happy and proud of herself for helping cook dinner and making a loop with her spaghetti.
She couldn't wait to eat it and tell her dad all about her cooking adventure.
Once upon a time, there was a car.
It had original parts, and it needed oil.
So the car went to the park.
When it got to the park, the car stopped and the driver put some oil in.
Then, the car started running again.
It was happy and ready to go on a new journey.
Next, the car drove around the park.
It drove over the grass and around the trees.
It felt so happy to be out and about.
Finally, after a long day of playing in the park, it was time for the car to go home.
The car thanked the driver for the oil and drove all the way back.
It had had a great time, and was ready to do it all again the next day.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to ride her bike with her friends, but one day she noticed her tire was flat.
She tried to ride it anyway, but it was wobbly and hard to balance.
Lily was sad because she couldn't ride her bike with her friends anymore.
But one day, her dad came home with a new tire.
It was available at the store and he bought it just for her.
Lily was happy again and put the tire on her bike.
She rode it all around the park with her friends.
But then, she saw another little girl who didn't have a bike at all.
Lily thought about how sad she was when she couldn't ride her bike and decided to share it with the other girl.
The other girl was so happy to have a bike to ride and Lily felt good about helping someone else.
She learned that sharing is important and it made her feel even more balanced and happy.
Once upon a time there was a big dream.
Every night the dream would provide a special adventure to a little girl.
One night she dreamed of going to a special land filled with grand castles and big animals.
The little girl was so excited and she couldn't wait to go exploring!
She traveled through the enchanted forest filled with singing birds and friendly bunnies.
Later she came across a big river with a rainbow bridge for her to cross.
The girl was so happy to explore the new land and she soon found a grand castle made of colourful glass.
She went inside and discovered that a friendly dragon had been living there all along.
The dragon was happy to provide the girl with a wonderful gift - a beautiful sparkly wand!
The little girl smiled and thanked the dragon.
She then waved goodbye, hopped on the rainbow bridge and returned home.
The little girl kept visiting the big dream night after night.
The dream always provided her with new adventures, new friends and so much fun!
Anna likes to play with her model cars.
She has many cars of different colors and sizes.
She makes them roll on the floor, on the table, and on the sofa.
She pretends they are racing or going on a trip.
One day, Anna's mom tells her to tidy her room.
She says there are too many toys everywhere and Anna could trip and hurt herself.
Anna does not want to tidy her room.
She wants to keep playing with her cars.
She thinks her mom is not fun.
Anna decides to hide her cars under the bed.
She thinks her mom will not see them there.
She puts some books and dolls on the bed to make it look tidy.
She hopes her mom will be happy and let her play.
But Anna's mom is not fooled.
She sees the bump under the bed and lifts the blanket.
She finds all the cars and scolds Anna.
She tells her to put them away in the box.
She says Anna has to learn to be tidy and respectful.
Anna feels sad and sorry.
She knows her mom is right.
She loves her cars, but she loves her mom more.
She says she is sorry and hugs her mom.
She puts her cars in the box and promises to be tidy next time.
Her mom smiles and kisses her.
She says she loves her and lets her play with one car for a while.
Anna is happy and rolls her car on the floor.
She thinks her mom is fun.
Mommy and daddy took their little girl to the park.
She giggle and when she saw the big cart.
She ran to it and asked Daddy to push her in.
Daddy said yes, so he started pushing the cart.
Mommy, Daddy, and their little girl went all around the park.
Daddy pushed the cart faster and faster, until finally they stopped to take a break.
But the little girl was still anxious to keep playing.
So they went to a big hill and Daddy pushed the cart up and down the hill.
The little girl squealed with excitement.
They did that for a while until the little girl started feeling sleepy.
Daddy stopped pushing the cart and the little girl said goodbye to the park.
She waved at the cart as if she was saying goodbye to a special friend.
Mommy and Daddy took their little girl home and she dreamed of the fun she had at the park.
Once upon a time, there was a high hill.
On the hill lived an old mechanic.
Every day he would work on the machines he loved.
He was very careful and took special care of each one.
One day, a little girl named Jennifer came to visit the mechanic.
She asked if the mechanic could show her all the machines he loved.
The mechanic smiled and said yes.
Jennifer was so excited and watched as the mechanic worked on each machine.
She was curious and asked "Why do you love these machines so much?" The mechanic replied, "Because they make me happy.
Every time I work on them, I feel so special."  Jennifer and the mechanic worked together for hours.
She smiled and said, "Now I love machines too!" The mechanic smiled back, "That's good to hear!
Now you and me, we can both love machines!"  The mechanic was so happy to have a friend who liked machines as much as he did.
Together they worked on the machines, enjoying each other's company.
Even when the day was over, the two of them were still smiling.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Molly.
She loved to explore, and she found a twig on the ground.
She picked it up and started playing with it.
Suddenly, a bird flew down and perched on the twig.
Molly was very excited, and she and the bird talked to each other.
"Hello!" said Molly.
"What's your name?"  "I'm Tweet," said the bird.
"I saw you picking this twig, and I thought it would make a great place for me to rest."  Molly was happy to help Tweet gain a comfortable place to sit.
She put the twig up in a nearby tree for the bird.
Then she said goodbye and went on her way.
From then on, Molly and Tweet were good friends.
Every time Molly went to explore, Tweet was always there to greet her.
And Molly was glad to help Tweet gain a comfortable place to rest.
Sara likes to wear her yellow dress.
It has flowers on it and a big bow.
She thinks it is pretty and sunny.
She likes to play in the garden with her dress.
One day, she sees a bee on a flower.
The bee is busy and noisy.
Sara is curious and wants to say hello.
She goes near the flower and smiles at the bee.
But the bee does not like Sara.
The bee thinks Sara is too close and wants to take the flower.
The bee is angry and scared.
The bee stings Sara on her arm.
Sara cries out loud.
It hurts a lot.
Mama hears Sara and runs to her.
She sees the bee and the sting.
She hugs Sara and takes her inside.
She puts some ice on her arm and gives her a kiss.
She tells Sara that the bee was not helpful.
The bee was mean and rude.
Sara feels better and learns a lesson.
She still likes her yellow dress and the flowers.
But she does not go near the bees anymore.
She knows they are not her friends.
She plays with her toys and her cat instead.
They are helpful and nice.
Lily and Ben were playing with magnets in the kitchen.
They liked to attach them to the fridge and make shapes and patterns.
Lily made a heart with red magnets and Ben made a star with blue magnets.
"Look, Lily, I made a star!" Ben said, proud of his work.
"That's nice, Ben.
I made a heart.
Do you like it?" Lily asked, showing him her heart.
"Yes, it's pretty.
But I like stars more.
They are bright and shiny," Ben said.
Lily felt sad.
She wanted Ben to like her heart too.
She liked stars, but she liked hearts more.
They were warm and compassionate.
"Can we share?" she asked Ben.
"You can have some of my heart magnets and I can have some of your star magnets.
Then we can make both hearts and stars." Ben thought for a moment.
He liked his star, but he also liked Lily.
She was his friend and he wanted to make her happy.
"Okay, Lily.
We can share.
Here, you can have two of my star magnets and I can have two of your heart magnets.
Then we can make both hearts and stars," he said, giving her the magnets.
Lily smiled and hugged Ben.
She was glad he was compassionate and willing to share.
They attached the magnets to the fridge and made new shapes and patterns.
They had fun playing with magnets and being friends.
Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom.
He had a sister who was very special to him.
One day, Tom and his sister were playing together when suddenly she got very sick.
Even the doctors couldn't make her better.
She died that night, and Tom was very sad.
He asked his mom what a 'dead' sister means.
She told him that it meant his sister was not alive anymore; she was gone forever.
Tom felt very sad and cried for a long time.
The days went by, and Tom slowly started to feel better.
He remembered his sister and the happy times they shared.
He knew that she was gone, but he held her in his heart forever.
No matter what, he would never forget her.
In time, the sadness ended.
Tom still felt very sad when he thought about his sister, but he knew that he had to be strong.
He carried his sister in his heart and was able to find peace.
Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Bill.
He was a very bouncy bunny, always hopping around the garden.
One day, Bill was feeling a bit grumpy.
He wanted to do something exciting, something new!
He decided it was time to do an adventure.
He followed his nose along a path, deep into the forest.
It soon became very dark, so he hopped faster and faster.
Suddenly, he stumbled over a big muscle!
He was a little scared at first, but then he noticed the muscle was smiling.
He asked the muscle what he was doing there.
The muscle said he was looking for an adventure too!
Bill was so excited and asked the muscle if he wanted to come with him.
The muscle happily followed Bill along the path.
Everywhere they went, they had an incredible adventure.
Bill's grumpy mood soon vanished and they both had the best time ever!
One day there was a brave mouse named Max.
He wanted to find some olives so he could eat them.
Max rolled across the floor and looked everywhere.
He was so brave he even checked under the big sofa.
"Oh look!" he exclaimed.
"I found some olives!" He was so excited.
Max gathered up the olives and rolled back across the room towards the door.
Then he heard a noise.
Max stopped and asked, "Who's there?" But no one answered.
Max was a bit scared but he was also brave.
He decided to keep rolling so he could get home.
Max ran across the room and out the door.
He was so happy to be safe.
He rolled back to his home where he could eat his olives in peace.
He was very brave.
Max the mouse was getting warm.
He spread out his paws and heated up the ground.
He could feel the heat going all around.
Suddenly, he saw a group of birds.
They looked very competitive and started to fly around in different directions.
Max felt a little nervous but decided to spread his wings too.
He joined the group of birds and flew in the air.
The heat strongly followed him, so Max felt very warm.
The birds spread out in the sky and made beautiful shapes.
Max was full of energy and he kept flying higher and higher.
He was going places!
The team of birds and Max had a great time.
They spread heat and happiness until the sun started to set.
Now it was time to go home.
Max thanked the birds for the fun competition and flew away into the night.
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim.
Tim loved cake more than anything.
One day, his mom made a big, yummy cake for him and his sister, Sue.
Tim and Sue were very happy.
But Tim was selfish.
He wanted the whole cake for himself.
When Sue tried to take a piece, Tim said, "No!
This is my cake!" Sue was sad and didn't know what to do.
Sue went to their mom and told her what Tim said.
Mom was not happy.
She went to Tim and said, "Tim, you must share the cake with your sister.
It is not nice to be selfish." Tim felt bad for making Sue sad.
In the end, Tim learned to share and gave Sue a big piece of cake.
They both ate the cake and were very happy.
From that day on, Tim was never selfish again.
Lila was upset.
She missed her mom.
Her mom went to work in the sky.
She flew in a big metal bird.
She said she would be back soon.
But Lila did not know when soon was.
She looked out the window.
She saw the moon and the stars.
They were bright and shiny.
She wondered if her mom could see them too.
She wondered if her mom was in the universe.
She wanted to talk to her mom.
She picked up her phone.
She pressed the green button.
She heard a beep.
She said, "Mom, are you there?
I miss you.
I love you.
Come back soon." She waited for an answer.
She heard another beep.
She heard a voice.
It was her mom.
She said, "Lila, I'm here.
I miss you too.
I love you more.
I'm in the sky, but I can see the moon and the stars.
They are beautiful.
Just like you.
I'll be back soon.
I promise." Lila smiled.
She felt happy.
She said, "Mom, you are beautiful too.
I'm glad you can see the moon and the stars.
They are in the universe.
Just like us.
I'll wait for you.
I promise." She pressed the red button.
She put down her phone.
She hugged her teddy bear.
She looked out the window again.
She waved to the moon and the stars.
She said, "Good night, mom.
Good night, universe."
One day, a little boy named Tim went outside to play.
He wanted to get his ball from the tree.
It was cold outside, but Tim did not care.
He was too excited to play.
Tim tried to reach the ball, but he was too small.
He felt impatient.
He called his friend, Sam.
"Sam, can you help me get my ball?" Tim asked.
Sam came running over to help.
Sam was taller than Tim, so he could reach the ball.
He got the ball for Tim, and they both played together.
They laughed and had fun, even though it was cold.
Soon, they went inside to warm up and have some hot cocoa.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl.
She was wearing yellow shoes.
One day, she went outside to play.
She wanted to have fun, so she decided to slide.
She climbed onto the slide and looked down.
It looked kind of scary, but she was brave.
The little girl started to slide down the slide.
It was fast and she was giggling.
Halfway down, she saw something yellow.
It was a something fluffy and yellow!
She wanted to know what it was.
She got off the slide and ran over.
It was a yellow caterpillar!
She had never seen one before.
It was moving slowly and she thought it was kind of cute.
But then, it changed!
It turned into a yellow butterfly!
The butterfly flew away and the little girl was scared.
But, she knew it was only trying to find a place to sleep.
So, she said goodbye and went back to the slide.
She was brave enough to slide one more time before it was time to go inside.
Lily liked to draw with ink.
She had many colors of ink in her box.
She liked to make pictures of flowers, stars, and animals.
She used a brush to put ink on paper.
One day, Lily wanted to show her ink pictures to her mom.
She took her box and her paper and went to the living room.
She saw her mom sitting on the couch, reading a book.
She said, "Mom, look at my pictures!
I made them with ink!" Mom smiled and put down her book.
She said, "Let me see, Lily.
I'm sure they are very pretty." She took the paper from Lily and looked at the pictures.
She said, "Wow, Lily, these are wonderful!
You are very good at drawing with ink.
I like the colors and the shapes.
You are very creative." Lily felt happy and proud.
She said, "Thank you, Mom.
I like to draw with ink.
It is fun and pretty." Mom said, "Yes, it is.
But you know what, Lily?
You have to be careful with ink.
Ink can make a mess.
It can stain your clothes and the furniture.
Do you know how to use ink safely?" Lily nodded.
She said, "Yes, Mom.
I know.
I have to put a cloth under the paper.
I have to close the ink bottles when I'm done.
I have to wash my hands and my brush.
I have to be careful not to spill the ink." Mom said, "That's right, Lily.
You are a smart and responsible girl.
I'm glad you know how to use ink safely.
But do you know what else you have to do?" Lily thought for a moment.
She said, "What else, Mom?" Mom said, "You have to look at yourself in the mirror." Lily was confused.
She said, "Why, Mom?" Mom said, "Because you have ink on your face, Lily.
You have a blue nose, a red cheek, and a yellow forehead.
You look like a rainbow." Lily gasped.
She ran to the mirror and saw her face.
She felt embarrassed.
She said, "Oh no, Mom.
I have ink on my face.
How did that happen?" Mom said, "I think you touched your face with your brush when you were drawing.
You didn't notice because you were so focused on your pictures.
But don't worry, Lily.
It's not a big deal.
We can wash it off with some soap and water.
It will come off easily.
And you know what?
You still look very cute.
You shine like a star, Lily.
You shine with your talent and your joy." Lily smiled.
She said, "Thank you, Mom.
You are very nice.
You make me feel better.
Can I give you a hug?" Mom said, "Of course, Lily.
I love you very much.
And I love your ink pictures.
They are very special.
Just like you."
Bob was walking through the big park.
He felt something tickle his nose.
He stopped, and tried to stop himself from sneezing.
He held his breath and pinched his nose, but it was no use.
He let out a big "ACHOO!" "Bless you!" said a voice.
Bob looked up and saw a girl standing nearby.
She was wearing a pink dress and had pigtails.
She smiled and waved at Bob.
"Are you okay?" she asked.
Bob nodded.
"I'm okay," he said.
"I just sneezed." The girl giggled.
"That's okay.
I sneezed too, a minute ago.
I'm Bertha." Bertha and Bob sat down on a bench.
Bob put his arm around Bertha's shoulder, and she leaned against him.
They watched a lazy dog sleeping in the grass.
"That dog sure is lazy," said Bertha.
"He must've been playing in the park all day." Bob smiled.
"Let's go play too," he said.
And off they went, having fun in the sunshine.
Lily and Ben are excited.
They are going to the park with Mom and Dad.
They put on their hats and shoes.
They hold hands and march to the car.
They sing a song as they march.
At the park, they see a big lake.
They see ducks and fish and boats.
They run to the edge of the water.
They wave to the ducks and the boats.
The ducks quack and the boats honk.
Lily and Ben laugh and clap.
Mom and Dad call them for a picnic.
They march back to the grass.
They sit on a blanket and eat sandwiches and fruit.
They drink juice and water.
They say thank you to Mom and Dad.
After the picnic, they play on the swings and the slide.
They make new friends and share their toys.
They have fun and are happy.
They wave goodbye to their friends and the park.
They march to the car and go home.
They are tired but still excited.
They hug Mom and Dad and say they love them.
They go to bed and dream of the park.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears.
One day, her mommy promised to fill her toy box with more toys.
Lily was so happy and excited!
But then she went to her friend's house and saw her friend's new toy.
It was a big, shiny truck.
Lily felt envious and wished she had one too.
She told her mommy about it and her mommy promised to buy her one soon.
Lily learned that promises can make you happy and that being envious is not a good feeling.
She was grateful for her mommy's love and care.
From that day on, Lily played with her toys and felt content.
Nina was walking home from the shops.
She had a box of waffles in her hands, which she had just bought.
Suddenly, she slipped and the box of waffles flew up into the air!
She tried to catch them but it was so difficult.
"Oh no!" she said.
Just then, a little dog came racing by.
The dog saw the waffles and tried to catch them.
He jumped and jumped but he couldn't reach them.
The waffles were getting further and further away.
"Help me catch the waffles!" Nina shouted to the dog.
The dog ran faster and finally he caught one of the waffles and brought it back to Nina.
She praised him and gave him a hug.
"You saved the day!" she said.
"Thank you so much!" The little dog looked so proud of himself, and Nina was so happy to have her waffle back.
They both went on their way, smiling.
Once upon a time, a little girl and her dad wanted to have a fun adventure.
They put on their shoes and went outside.
The girl and her dad climbed up a big hill.
It was so steep that they had to stop and take breaks.
The girl looked around and saw a big, blue apple tree!
The apples were so blue and shiny.
The girl was excited and wanted to pick an apple.
She asked her dad to help her climb the tree.
He did and they both carefully climbed up.
Once they were at the top, the girl plucked one of the blue apples and smiled.
She and her dad sat back in the tree and enjoyed the view.
The girl also enjoyed her juicy blue apple!
Once upon a time, there was a little girl.
She was very polite.
Everywhere she went she said please and thank you.
One day she wanted to take a march.
She put on her shoes and started to walk.
As the little girl started walking, she saw a puddle.
It was so big that if she walked in the middle, even her shoes would get wet.
She didn't want to get her shoes wet, so she stopped and watched the puddle carefully.
Suddenly, a magical voice came from the sky.
“Little girl, I can help you,” the voice said.
“Yes, please help me!” the girl said.
The voice said, “I will pour something over the puddle to make it go away.
Just march the other way, so you don’t get wet.”  The girl marched around the puddle, and the magical voice poured something on the puddle.
When she looked back, the puddle was gone!
The little girl was so happy and she thanked the magical voice.
The little girl thanked the magical voice for helping her stay polite and dry.
Then she continued her march, surefooted and happy.
Once upon a time, there was a clever dog named Max.
Max lived in a big yard with his family.
One day, Max's friend, a cat named Lily, came to visit him.
"Max, I have a plan," said Lily.
"Let's play hide and seek!" Max thought it was a great idea and agreed to play.
Lily went to hide while Max counted.
After a while, Max found Lily hiding behind a tree.
"You are so intelligent, Lily!" said Max.
"You always find the best hiding spots." Lily purred with happiness and they continued to play together in the yard.
Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily.
She loved to look up at the stars and wonder about the planet she saw up there.
One day, she asked her friend Timmy if he had ever been to the planet.
Timmy shook his head and said, "No, I haven't been there.
But I promise one day we will go together." Lily was so happy to hear that and she smiled from ear to ear.
But then, another friend named Sarah came over and saw how happy Lily was.
Sarah felt envious and wanted to go to the planet too.
"I want to go to the planet too!" Sarah said.
